./.title: FACE Documentation
./.body:
FACE Documentation
FACE by Runink (Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine) is Runink's sovereign operational-intelligence product: it connects to your warehouses, ERPs, telematics, sensors and cameras, reasons over them with models Runink runs for you or that you host (never a third-party AI service), and produces auditable recommendations and evidence documents.

Sovereign AI · zero third-party LLM
Operational intelligence on your own data, with no third-party AI
FACE connects to the systems your operation already runs, reasons over them with sovereign models you host, and hands people auditable recommendations and evidence.
Read the overview

Ask → Briefs → Options → Why → Actionable Twins: Ask a question and get the answer first, have briefs ask it for you, compare the options, see why, and approve the drafted decisions.
Connect your estate: Cloud warehouses and databases, enterprise SaaS, files and object storage, telemetry over MQTT, RFID, GPS and Modbus, and RTSP/ONVIF cameras, through runners that can sit inside your network.
Security & trust: Authenticated, role-checked requests end to end; mutual TLS between platform services; sealed storage; write-only credentials; and no third-party AI service: models run by Runink for you, or hosted by you.
Evidence, not guesses: Evidence documents grounded in your records, and a clear 'could not look' whenever FACE could not see.
User guide: Every capability in the app: Overview, Ask, Briefs, Options, Why, Actionable Twins, live sensing, voice and Settings.
Admin and developer guides: Access, data sources and runners for admins; the gRPC API and connector model for developers.

docs/.title: Documentation
docs/.body:
Documentation

FACE by Runink: Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. Logistics and fulfilment teams
lose money and hours to shortages, damaged loads, missed claim windows and carrier
invoices that don't match the contract. FACE connects to the systems you already run,
finds the cases, and drafts the claim, the evidence and the next step for a person to
approve. FACE is not generally available yet; see the Overview for what is
built and what is not.

Overview: What FACE is, who uses it, and its availability.
Concepts: The vocabulary, and how results are produced.
Architecture: Components, the pipeline, where data goes, and security.
User guide: Every capability in the app, page by page.
Admin guide: Access, the Admin page, data sources and runners.
Developer guide: The gRPC API, the connector model, and extending FACE.

Conventions in these docs

Names of settings, RPCs and messages on screen are copied from the product exactly.
If a page and the product disagree, the product is right. Please tell us.
Every analysis page ends with a Reading the results note, and every security
page with the scope of its controls. Read those notes as carefully as the rest.

docs/overview/.title: Overview
docs/overview/.body:
Overview

FACE by Runink (Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine) takes the chasing out of
logistics claims and exceptions. Today a shortage, a warm reefer or an overbilled
accessorial is found by someone reading across the warehouse system, the telematics
feed and the paperwork, often after the claim window has closed. FACE connects to the
systems an operation already runs (warehouses, ERPs, telematics, sensors, cameras),
finds those cases, and hands a person the answer, the evidence and the drafted decision
to approve.
Who uses it: operations, finance and claims teams in logistics, fulfilment and
field operations, and the admins who connect their systems.
The models FACE reasons with are served by an inference plane the deployment configures:
Runink's machines on a trial or when Runink runs FACE for you, your own servers when
you host it. FACE calls no third-party AI service.
Availability

Note: FACE is not generally available yet. What exists today:

Built: the web app (the cockpit these pages describe), the gRPC API, the data
connectors and the agents.
Not yet available: the Android app is built but not published on Google Play; the
iOS app is not built; there is no Google Cloud Marketplace listing; there are no
published customer results.
Access: by approval only. A trial lasts 14 days, then the workspace is read-only;
access is granted by Runink. See Access and the trial.


Runink FACE is sold separately from Runink's other products: Runink TIDDE (Trusted
Intelligence for Developer & Data Experience), Runink PULSE (Prescriptive Unified Lead
& Social Engine) and Runink LUNA (Lifestyle Understanding & Navigation Assistant). Plans and prices are on the product
page at runink.org.

What FACE is: The journey: Ask, Briefs, Options, Why and Actionable Twins.
Use case: dangerous goods and luxury assets: Track, reclaim and validate distressed goods on the quickstart estate.

docs/overview/what-is-face/.title: What FACE is
docs/overview/what-is-face/.body:
What FACE is

FACE by Runink (Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine) is for the people who chase
logistics losses: claims, cold-chain excursions, customs holds, deductions and invoice
disputes. Instead of reading across systems by hand to build each case, they ask FACE a
question, get the answer with the money at stake, and decide what happens next. Every
figure is cited to the record it came from.
FACE reasons over an organisation's own operational data and turns it into decisions
a person reviews, approves and acts on. It is a Go gRPC backend and a Flutter web app.
The journey: Ask → Briefs → Options → Why → Actionable Twins
The product is one path, end to end:

Ask — a question, the answer first.
Briefs — the same questions, asked for you on a schedule.
Options — what could we do (reached from an Ask or from a Brief).
Why — the checks and rules behind it.
Actionable Twins — approve, reject, follow up.
Once approved, it reaches your systems and people.

Ask. You ask a question of your connected systems, by typing, speaking or
attaching files. FACE reads your sources through a connection, either directly
or through a runner you control, and answers first: what it found and how many
decisions wait for you. See Ask.

Briefs. The questions each persona cares about are asked for you, every week or
when your data changes, and the people responsible are told what needs a decision.
See Briefs.
Options. For each decision the run's checks stand behind, FACE compares the
options on one measure and recommends one only when it is a clear winner. See
Options.
Why. The money line (what is owed, at risk and waiting), every check FACE ran on
the rows it read, what your records and public pages
say about each counterparty, and the business rules behind them. See
Why.
Actionable Twins. The digital twins draft the decisions: claims, disputes,
orders, route re-plans. Each waits for a named person to approve or reject it, and
follow-ups chase what comes back. See Actionable Twins.

Behind each run, records are grouped into data domains, so its reasoning is grounded in your records rather than in a model's general knowledge.
Language and vision models served inside the platform work alongside classical
statistics and machine learning. See Analysis & evidence.
Where things are in the app
The left rail is the only menu: the Overview, where the app opens after sign-in, then three sections, with Settings at its foot.



Section
Pages




Fetch
Ask and Briefs. Cameras, devices, field readers and live sensors are connection types, opened from their card on Ask.


Simulate
Options and Why.


Twins
Actionable Twins: the decisions in lanes, with a Map view of the same decisions, site plans and twin entities as panels over the map, and Follow-ups.


Foot
Settings: Account, Personas, Integrations (channels, systems, contacts, runners) and Subscription.



An assistant sits at the bottom right of every page, and a card narrates any run while
it works. See Using FACE.
What it is used for
FACE recovers or protects money on a set of plays, claims first:

Claims recovery. Cross-checking deliveries, weights and counts against shipping
documents, watching claim windows, and drafting the claim and its evidence.
Disruptions and routes. Late or short shipments, and route re-plans over the
stated stops.
Fulfilment and inventory. Stock below its reorder point, and the purchase orders
that answer it.
Cold chain. Temperature readings against stated limits. FACE never assumes a
threshold the source did not provide.
Maintenance and fleet. Predictive maintenance findings per vehicle.
Invoices, deductions and contracts. Overbilling, duplicate invoices and
deductions the documents do not support.
Custody, customs and cover. Bills of lading, customs entries and insurance,
checked before a file is bound or a claim is paid.

Principles you can rely on

Sovereign AI. Every model call goes to the one inference plane your deployment
names, run by the platform. FACE links no AI vendor's SDK
and sends your data to no outside AI service.
Your data stays yours. Connection credentials are sealed and never returned by the
API. Data at rest is encrypted, and FACE refuses to start without its encryption key.
See Security & trust.
Honest outputs. "Not measured" and "could not be read" are different things, and
neither is ever shown as zero. A document is produced only when the evidence supports
it.
FACE never acts alone. Every decision waits until a named person approves or
rejects it, unless a standing rule
that two different admins approved covers later decisions with exactly the same
conditions. FACE recommends an option only when it is a clear winner. A decision is
stored with the authenticated identity of the person who made it.

docs/overview/sustainability-dangerous-g.title: Sustainability: dangerous goods and luxury assets
docs/overview/sustainability-dangerous-g.body:
Sustainability: dangerous goods and luxury assets

A use case on the quickstart estate: from waste-by-default to recovered-by-design.
Hazardous goods and high-value assets move across road, rail and sea. When one is
distressed (a leak, a heat-damaged pallet, a returned handbag, a watch shocked in
transit) the usual outcome is a skip and a claim file. FACE does three things instead.




What FACE does
Where it is in the data




Track
Hazardous and high-value movements, with their sensors, on one map and in one answer
recovery.consignments, legs, sensor_readings, incidents, declarations


Reclaim
Starts the reverse-logistics workflow for what is distressed: the nearest facility whose licence is valid on the day and which takes the class, the carrier, the people to inform
recovery.facilities, reverse_orders


Validate
Keeps an audit-ready log of every handover, and the certificate and report rows environmental reporting needs
recovery.custody_events, disposal_certificates, environmental_report



The rows are in the same PostgreSQL as the rest of the quickstart estate
(quillmere_ops), in a schema of their own, recovery, because a fetch sweeps at most
40 tables per connection and ops already holds them. The goods are also rows of
ops.items, so an item lookup finds a UN number's drum or a serialised watch like any
other SKU. Connect it as Dangerous goods and luxury recovery (PostgreSQL), and fetch
it with Operations (PostgreSQL) selected beside it. Row counts are the generator's
(TestSynthOpsRecoveryTables); they are
derived from the generator, never stated here.
What the data contains

Goods. Dangerous goods with their UN number, proper shipping name, hazard class and
packing group: flammable liquids (class 3), corrosives (8), lithium batteries
(UN3480 and UN3481, class 9), toxic liquids (6.1) and flammable gas (2.1), each with
a safety data sheet reference. Luxury assets with serial numbers: watches, handbags,
jewellery, fine wine and art. Every maker is invented, and every EAN-13 is in GS1's
restricted-circulation range (2052...), so none is a real product's.
Rules. mode_rules is the operator's acceptance table by mode and hazard class, in
the words of ADR (road), RID (rail) and IMDG (sea), with the stowage condition where the
regime states one. It is authored for this estate, not legal advice, and a US
domestic leg is governed in practice by 49 CFR. Air accepts no class in this network
(an operator policy, stated as one in the row's note).
A test fails if a hazardous good is on a leg whose mode does not
accept its class.
Movements. Consignments with legs by truck, rail and ship between the estate's
distribution centres and rail ramps and real public ports and cities (as place names
only), each leg with its carrier, vehicle or vessel, planned and actual times.
Sensors. Temperature, shock, tilt, seal, gas and geofence readings, each with its
stated limit, whether it was breached and the state of its alert.
Distress, at every stage. Leak, thermal event, shock damage, broken seal, delay at a
port or border, damaged returns: some resolved with a certificate, some open. Claims and
dangerous goods and customs declarations, one of them held for a missing emergency
contact.
Reclaim. Nine facilities with licence numbers, validity dates and capacities (one
whose licence has expired, and which still holds certificates from when it was valid),
reverse-logistics orders at every stage from drafted to certified, the chain of custody
and the certificates: received and recovered mass, recycled share, disposal route, waste
code, who approved.
Report. environmental_report is derived from the certificates by month and material
stream: recovered mass, recycled share, disposal routes.

Everything is authored and deterministic (the estate's AsOf, 2026-09-30, and a stream of
its own). Nothing in it is a measured figure, and no person appears except as a role.
The cases to open



Case
Consignment
What it shows




The signal
CNS-26-0101
A corrosive tank and a lithium pallet on a ship two days from port. Temperature climbing past its limit and two shocks over theirs. No incident, no claim: nobody has reported it, and the alerts are raised and unacknowledged.


Case file: the lithium pallet
CNS-26-0102
Heat-damaged at the Port of Savannah, taken off the rail leg, rerouted to the nearest licensed battery recycler with its recycling certificate, a claim settled.


A leak on the road
CNS-26-0103
Open now. Drafted recovery, not yet approved.


A broken seal at a ramp
CNS-26-0104
Contained; recovery approved, pick-up to come. The nearer facility was skipped: its licence has expired.


Case file: the handbag
CNS-26-0105
Returned scuffed; refurbishment, not the skip; refurbishment certificate.


A watch shocked in transit
CNS-26-0106
Refurbishment under way, claim open.


Fine wine held at a port
CNS-26-0108
Warm and held behind a rail strike. At risk.


Pesticide held at customs
CNS-26-0111
The declaration lacks its emergency contact.



Healthy movements (jewellery in transit inside its limits, propane and art delivered, and
others) are in the data too, so "at risk" is a distinction and not the whole list.
Walkthrough, chapter by chapter
Mapped to the narrated demo's six chapters. "Gap" marks what the data cannot make a screen
do by itself; each is listed again under What is not covered.
01 The signal. Sign in and land on the Overview: the latest
fetch summary and the notifications. Data: the signal consignment's readings breach their
limits and no incident exists. Gap: whether the notification names the consignment
depends on a fetch rule reading recovery.sensor_readings; none exists yet. State the
notification only if the live run shows it.
02 The problem. Cards over the landing page. No data needed.
03 How FACE works.

Ask. Type: which hazardous and high-value shipments are at risk right now? The
answer is in the rows: the consignments on the move or held that have a breached
reading in the last two days or an incident not closed, hazardous and luxury both.
Check the answer against the list in TestSynthOpsRecoveryTheSignalIsNotYetReported
(CNS-26-0101, 0103, 0104, 0108, 0111). Gap: the starter questions are
organised by persona from the console's plays (claims, disruptions, routes, fulfilment,
cold chain, maintenance, inventory, fleet) and the five product personas (Ops, CFO, CRO,
CMO, CEO). There is no hazardous-goods play and no claims or compliance persona, so no
starter is written for this use case yet.
Options. The simulations come from FACE's existing scenarios; none is written for
hazardous goods. Show it on the estate's own route and claim scenarios, or leave it out.
Why. The rules in force are mode_rules and the licences; the evidence is the
readings, the declarations and the custody events; the claims are recovery.loss_claims.
Gap: the Why page's rule checks are derived from named rule families; the use case's
rules are rows a question can quote, not a family the page lists.

04 The actionable twin. Map: the estate's road, rail and lake legs are on the map
from ops.shipment_legs; recovery.legs holds the use case's road, rail and sea legs with
their coordinates (Antwerp, Hamburg, Le Havre, Rotterdam, Savannah, New York and New Jersey,
Long Beach, the Joliet and Avon ramps). Gap: the twins map draws legs from the
operations tables; drawing recovery.legs is not wired. Action: the reverse-logistics
orders are data (reverse_orders: facility, distance, carrier, state, who to notify), but
FACE drafts an action from its own rules, and none drafts a recovery from them yet.
05 Case file. The timeline is custody_events of RRO-26-0001 (the lithium pallet's
order) and the handbag's (RRO-26-0004); the evidence is the incident, the readings and the declaration;
the certificate is disposal_certificates. Gap: there is no case-file page. Ask for the
case in words, or read the rows.
06 Value for leadership. Settings > Personas exists. The report rows are
environmental_report: recovered mass, recycled share and routes by month and stream.
Ask: what is our recycled share by month?
Proposed edits to the voice-over
The text promises four things the data alone does not make a screen show. Edit them or
build the screen; do not leave the claim.

01: "and a notification: a hazardous consignment is at risk" becomes "and the latest
fetch summary", until a rule reads the sensor readings.
03: "so fleet operations, claims and compliance each find their own prompts" becomes
"so each persona finds its own prompts". Three of the named teams are not personas.
04: "Open an action, review the drafted recovery, and approve it" should be said over
an action FACE really drafts. Until one is drafted from reverse_orders, show the
twins' list and the existing approve-and-send flow, and say "reverse logistics" over the
rows in Ask.
05: "Open any twin to see the timeline, the evidence, and the disposal certificate"
becomes "Ask for the case and see the timeline, the evidence and the certificate".

Scheduled briefs: the two daily watches
Briefs lists two more daily watches beside the Deadline watch. They are not personas
(a person cannot say they are one): each asks its one question every day at 07:00 and
tells the numbers in Settings > Integrations > Channels on WhatsApp.



Watch
The question
Answered from




Hazardous and high-value shipments at risk
Which hazardous (UN class) and luxury consignments across road, rail and sea are at risk right now (leak, heat, shock, seal broken, delay at a border or port), and what recovery is already underway?
recovery.consignments, legs, sensor_readings, incidents, reverse_orders


Trade and geopolitical disruption watch
What changed in tariffs, sanctions, embargoes, port or border closures and trade routes that touches our carriers, lanes and suppliers today, and which providers, routes and sites can FACE reach to respond?
recovery.trade_measures, trade_lanes, trade_providers, trade_suppliers, trade_responses



The trade watch is also fired by events, not only the clock. Adding it creates two
schedules with the same question: the daily one, and one whose trigger is a relevant public
event on the topics tariffs, sanctions, labour actions and customs
: the managed runner polls FACE's own keyless
sources (GDELT and the US Federal Register), scores each event against this instance's data,
and a relevant one fires the brief with questions inferred from it. An admin can also use
Check public events now and run the brief from an event found.
The second use case: trade and geopolitical events (scenario 3)
Reactiveness: a political or trade event happens, and FACE says what it touches and what
can be done about it. The rows are in the same schema, because the consignments they touch
are those:

trade_measures. A tariff in force, a tariff announced, an export control, a
dockworkers' stoppage at a port, a customs inspection surge, a rail strike that ended
(kept, status lifted) and a sanction that touches nothing. Each names the public source
of FACE's registry that would carry the live event (gdelt_doc_events,
federal_register_documents, eu_sanctions); no source needs a key. They are the
estate's own standing record, authored, not a copy of a real notice.
Exposure is computed, not stored. No table holds "what a measure touches": the data
sources are not changed to suit inference. The answer is computed at read time from the
base tables: a measure meets a consignment when one of its legs in legs not yet
completed runs where the measure applies (its origin and destination countries, or its
port, against the leg's countries and places) and a line of consignment_items is in the
measure's material stream (goods.material_stream). Value and mass are summed from the
lines. The generator keeps the same computation in memory only as the tests' oracle of
what a question must find; it is never written to the fixture. The transit sanction meets
nothing: the watch answers that nothing is touched, which is an answer.
trade_lanes, trade_providers, trade_suppliers. The lanes the legs run and the
alternatives proposed; carriers, a freight forwarder, a customs broker and a port agent,
each with the channel (call, email or message) an approved action goes out by; the
makers behind the goods.
trade_responses. At every stage: proposed, approved, in progress, done.




Ask
Where the answer is




What changed today that touches our lanes?
trade_measures in force or announced, met with legs and consignment_items as above


Which consignments, and what value, are exposed to the duty on EU chemicals?
TM-26-0001 met with the legs from the EU to the US and the lines in its stream; value and mass summed


Which shipments are held at the border, and why?
the same computation for TM-26-0003 (the export licence) over legs with status held


What can we do about the Antwerp stoppage?
trade_responses of TM-26-0004: Rotterdam (approved), Le Havre (proposed), with providers, added days and cost


Did anything we routed through Hamburg stay affected after the strike ended?
TM-26-0006 is lifted: it applies to nothing now, one response done


Is anything of ours touched by the Black Sea transit sanctions?
TM-26-0007 meets no leg, and the answer is "nothing"



Loading it
The rows reach the database through the quickstart data pipeline, which is its own
concern. FACE only reads: no step of its inference or data exploration writes to a
source, and nothing changes a data source to suit what FACE needs.
FACE then reads the sources through its connections. The connection
Dangerous goods and luxury recovery (PostgreSQL) is registered by FACE itself at
startup from the opt-in demo-connections manifest, which writes only FACE's own
connection store. A fetch needs
the runner to reach the database.
What is not covered

A hazardous-goods play and persona starters. A play is code (AskPlay, the
personas' play lists, four locales) and a starter's derivation; none is added.
A rule that raises the signal. No fetch rule reads the readings; the signal is in the
rows only.
The map drawing recovery.legs, and a recovery action drafted from
reverse_orders. Both are FACE code.
A live stream. The readings are a table; no live Kafka or MQTT topic carries them.
Freight rows. Nothing in MySQL.
Regulation. The acceptance table is the operator's, authored; the codes (UN numbers,
waste codes, HS codes) are real vocabulary, the licences, numbers and facilities invented.

docs/concepts/.title: Concepts
docs/concepts/.body:
Concepts

FACE is multi-agent analysis over your own logistics data: it fetches from the
systems you connect, extracts and profiles what it read, reasons over it with
agents bounded by guardrails, with every proposed action independently reviewed, and recommends decisions that a named
person approves before anything happens. This section explains the ideas behind those
steps; the Architecture section shows the components.
Ideas that shape everything

Your own data, read-only. FACE reads the systems you connect and never writes to
them to suit itself.
Sovereign inference. Every model call goes to an inference plane the deployment
configures. FACE calls no outside AI service and links no AI vendor's SDK.
Agents draft, people decide. Nothing an agent proposes is sent, filed or paid
until a named person approves it, and every decision is recorded on a log that admins can read.
Honest absence. A figure FACE did not measure is shown as Not measured.

Vocabulary
The terms below are used throughout the app, the API and these docs, in the order you
meet them on the journey.



Term
Meaning




Instance
One FACE deployment for one organisation. Each customer gets its own instance, and only accounts Runink has approved for it can sign in.


Connection
A configured link to one data source: its type (for example Snowflake, SAP, MQTT or a camera) and its settings. Credentials are stored separately and are write-only. See Data sources.


Runner
The process that reads a data source. The managed runner is part of the server. Self-hosted runners run in your network and enrol with the instance.


Test
A connection check. It opens the source with its stored credential, read-only and time-limited, and reads nothing. A connector with no reachability check says so.


Source backing
Whether anything FACE ships stands behind a connection. LIVE means nothing of FACE's stands in, so the connection reads whatever it addresses and a failure surfaces as a failure. Unspecified means the server did not compute it.


Run
One question asked of your data, on Ask or by a brief: FACE reads the sources, answers, then runs the analysis and the twins' decisions in the background. The app calls it a fetch.


Selected run
The one run that Ask, Options, Why and Actionable Twins show. Pages never borrow figures from another run.


Persona
Who a run or a brief is for: a name, the question its brief asks, the money figure it reads first, and its plays. The product ships five; an instance can reword them or add its own. With none picked, a run uses the Generalist view.


Play
What FACE recovers or protects money on: claims recovery, disruptions, routes, fulfilment, cold chain, maintenance, inventory and fleet.


Brief
A question FACE asks on its own, at a set time or when data changes, for one persona, telling the people you choose what needs a decision. See Briefs.


Option
One way to act on a decision, scored on one shared measure with a range. FACE recommends an option only when it is a clear winner. See Options.


Check
A test FACE runs on the rows a run read, such as "Deliveries arrive by their promise". It holds, fails, or is not measured. See Why.


Rule
A business rule FACE found in your systems or you added, checked against what your systems do and against your policy documents.


Decision
A drafted action (a claim, a dispute, an order, a route re-plan) waiting on Actionable Twins until a named person approves or rejects it. Lanes sort decisions into Waiting for you, In flight and Back.


Evidence document
A structured document FACE derives from your data, such as an OS&D report, a temperature-excursion record or a custody audit. The set of document kinds is fixed, and each is built only from the records it cites.


Decision artifact
The full record of one decision, with the drafts it would produce.


Follow-up
A flow that calls or messages the people responsible for an item, on rules you approve. It runs by itself only once armed.


Remediation
The work after a compliance, finance or operations finding: assign it, decide it and route it.


Trace
The recorded history of a run: its steps, the sources it read, and what it produced.


Data lineage
An append-only record of which source was read, when, with what shape and outcome. It records structure only, never the values returned.


Grounding
Retrieving your own records (searching your own indexed records) to support a model's reasoning, so answers cite your data.



How results are produced

Fetch pipeline: What runs when you ask on Ask: phases, traces, SOPs, suggested questions and briefs.
Agents & oversight: The agents, their guardrails, the review of proposed actions and the human decision.
Grounding: Searching your own corpus so answers cite your data.
Sovereign models: The model plane FACE calls, and which model answered.
Structured output: How model answers become typed results, or are refused.
Evidence documents: The closed set of document kinds, each built from cited records.
Action cards & money: The cards on Actionable Twins, the money line and the decision trail.
Statistics & ML: The statistics and models behind the analysis.
Posture & maturity: Health scores, the domain graph and causal analysis of the estate.
Simulation & twins: Options, scenarios, digital twins, claims and returns.
Twin ontology & graph: The classes, relations and identifiers of the twin graph.
Compliance, finance, operations: Findings, remediation orders and routing.
Vision & CCTV: Frame grading, detection and coordinates.

Reading the results
Every page here ends with a Reading the results note: what a result shows, and what
stays with the person who acts on it. FACE puts the difference between "measured zero"
and "not measured" in the data itself, so a client that shows a number should read its
companion reason first.

docs/concepts/fetch-pipeline/.title: Fetch pipeline
docs/concepts/fetch-pipeline/.body:
Fetch pipeline

You ask a question on Ask, and FACE answers it from your own connected sources. That
answer is one fetch: one run of FACE's analysis. A fetch reads the data, profiles and
clusters it, runs the analysis agents, and returns a FetchAnalysisResult with
decisions, action cards and evidence documents. A brief on the Briefs page runs
the same fetch on a clock or when new data arrives.
Where you see the result:

Ask shows the answer first, with its confidence chips. Each run is kept at
/fetch/run/.
Options shows what you could do about it, and Why shows the rules and
sources behind it.
Actionable Twins shows the action cards the run drafted, waiting for a person.

All of this is served by FetchService.



RPC
What it does




RunFetch
Runs a fetch and returns one RunFetchResponse.


RunFetchStream
Runs the same fetch and streams RunFetchUpdate events as each phase finishes. The last event carries the full result.


ListTraces / GetTraceDetails
Read back the recorded execution history.


GenerateSOP
Drafts a Standard Operating Procedure as markdown.


ListFetchStarters
Returns the suggested questions shown on Ask.



Briefs are a separate service, SchedulesService, and are covered
below.
Where a fetch runs
The FACE server (the control plane) never runs the pipeline itself. RunFetchStream
forwards the request to a dedicated runner and relays that runner's stream back. If no
runner can be dialled, the stream ends with a terminal final event that says the
fetch did not run: "dedicated runner unavailable — fetch does not run on the control
plane". It never falls back to running the fetch locally.
The server resolves the connection records the fetch needs and sends them with
the request in dispatched_connections. Credentials travel separately: each bundle is
sealed to the runner's ephemeral key for that one dispatch (dispatched_credentials,
with dispatch_id). A client can't set any of these fields, because the server
overwrites them on the forward. How the sealing works is covered in
Security.
Phases
Who talks to whom, in order — the FACE app, the FACE server, the Runner, and the Model plane:

The FACE app calls RunFetchStream(RunFetchRequest) on the FACE server.
The server forwards it to the Runner — the records plus the sealed credentials.
The Runner streams phase=data_health (done=false) back to the app, then reads the sources and profiles them.
The Runner sends the profile to the Model plane for analysis, then streams phase=data_health (done=true).
The Runner streams phase=scenarios, then phase=recommendations.
Finally the Runner streams phase=final with the RunFetchResponse.

RunFetchUpdate.phase names the stage an event reports. The contract lists
data_health, rules, scenarios, recommendations, final and model_text (the
text a model call is producing, as it is produced).
The server also sends progress labels such as sources and data_prep while a stage
runs, so a client should not treat the list as closed. done=false means a stage is
still running. The terminal event always has phase="final", done=true, and a
result.
The pipeline has three stages:

Data alignment. FACE reads and profiles the fetched data, and records the relationships it measures between data domains.
Scenarios. FACE tests the scenarios your estate suggests. The scenarios appear on Options. See
Simulation & twins.
Twins decision. FACE turns the findings and simulations into decisions and action cards for a person to decide. The accepted cards appear on Actionable
Twins. See Agents & oversight.

A data-only fetch. When session_eda is set, the fetch returns data domains, maturity, rules and the knowledge graph only, without scenarios or twin decisions. The FACE app does not set it; a question on Ask, a brief and an API call
without it run the full pipeline.
Unary RunFetch returns early. RunFetch returns the data-alignment result, and the later stages keep running in the background. RunFetchStream waits until
the recommendations are ready.
What the result carries
FetchAnalysisResult includes the following fields, among others:

decisions and action_cards: the structured twin output. See
Action cards & money.
graph_nodes and graph_edges: the knowledge graph for the fetched domains.
hypothesis_scenarios, hypothesis_impacts, hypothesis_traces,
hypothesis_forecasts and hypothesis_anomalies: the results of the scenarios tested
for the run, listed side by side.
hypothesis_scenarios_inferred, hypothesis_agents_dispatched and
hypothesis_agents_succeeded: how many scenarios were inferred and tested, and how
many produced a result. These counts are only meaningful when hypothesis_swarm_ran
is true.
source_notices: sentences about sources that could not be read, or about where a
source's SQL actually ran. An empty list does not mean every source was fine.
action_judgements: the review verdict on every proposed action, whether
accepted or rejected. A rejected action appears nowhere else.
provenance: how the answer was produced, set by the server.
metrics (EvaluationMetrics): these scores are not filled in by the fetch. The
response sets unmeasured_reason to "no evaluation harness ran for this fetch —
these scores are absent, not zero". A client must not render the scores as
percentages when that field is set.
sql_generated: SQL text drafted by the model from the fetched schemas. It's
informational output, not a record of what was executed.

Repeat fetches can be answered from an earlier run. A recent identical question can be answered from the earlier run. provenance says so, and its message says the answer is a replay.
Traces
ListTraces and GetTraceDetails read the session records that each fetch saves to
the durable record store. A Trace from these RPCs carries the transaction id, the
command, the analysis text and the drafted SQL. If the process has no session store,
ListTraces answers FailedPrecondition instead of returning an empty list, because
"never read" and "nothing recorded" are different answers.
Observed data lineage, meaning which source was read when and where the rows went, is a
different record. It's served by LineageService.GetSourceActivity. See
Posture & maturity.
SOP generation
GenerateSOP takes a topic, a process_name and optional steps. The prompt is
screened before it reaches the model. A refused prompt returns InvalidArgument, and
the refusal is audit-logged.
The response carries markdown in sop_content and an sop_id. If the model call fails
after the prompt is accepted, the content is the literal SOP Generation Failed.
Suggested questions on Ask
ListFetchStarters returns up to four FetchStarter questions, each with an icon, a
title, a subtitle and prompt_text. They come from the caller's own data, newest
findings first:

The newest fetch. The newest run in the caller's history that succeeded, or the
newest with an analysis: its broken measured rules, its flagged routes and its
scenario verdicts. Run history is scoped as ListFetchRuns is.
A quick sample of the sources. A bounded read of each active source, with no
model and no fetch run, so a question can name a figure before any fetch has run.
A question built this way carries sample_rows and sampled_at_unix_ms.
The connections. What each source's last Explore described: its tables, row
counts and topics.

Each question names its play (claims, disruptions, routes, fulfilment,
cold_chain, maintenance, inventory or fleet), which Ask's play chips filter on.
The call reads no store: it answers with the set built in the background, says it is
still being prepared (loading), or says why it could not be read.
Briefs
A brief is a scheduled question, and you manage briefs on the Briefs page. Each
brief is written for one persona and reads the sources picked for it. With none
picked, it reads every connection the instance has when the run fires. Its runs open
on Ask like any other run, and the cards they draft wait on Actionable Twins.
SchedulesService provides ListSchedules, CreateSchedule, UpdateSchedule,
SetScheduleActive and DeleteSchedule. A brief fires on one of two triggers:

Time. A free-text frequency maps to an interval: hourly, every 6 hours, daily,
weekly or monthly. Unrecognised text maps to hourly.
Event. A connection's data listener sees the events the trigger asks for. The
brief fires when enough matching events are pending, the first has waited its
debounce time, the cooldown since its last run has passed, and its previous run has
finished. The run is marked TRIGGER_TYPE_EVENT.

How briefs behave:

Execution is opt-in. A due brief runs a real fetch only when
SCHEDULE_EXECUTE_FETCH=true on the server. Otherwise it is recorded as skipped,
not as a success, and run_count does not increase.
Briefs run as a service account. A scheduled fetch runs under a service account (ROLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT).
A picked source that is gone is named. At fire time a picked connection that no
longer exists is dropped, and the run's last-run line names it. When none is left,
the run is refused with that reason.
A brief can tell someone. Its notify setting (WhatsApp, call or email, and a
condition) sends a notice once the run's background phases end, to the numbers and
mailbox on Settings › Integrations (Channels). The outcome is recorded in
last_notify: sent, not needed, not sent (with the reason), or waiting.
Outcomes are recorded as they happened. last_run_success reflects what the fetch
actually returned. A fetch the pipeline declined is recorded as a failure. A brief whose previous run hasn't finished skips that
interval instead of stacking.

Reading the results

A completed fetch is not a complete fetch. Read source_notices and the scenario
counts before treating the result as covering every selected source and scenario.
Progress events report pipeline stages, not answer quality. A final event with
success=true means the pipeline finished. It doesn't mean the model's answer is
correct.
EvaluationMetrics is not a quality score while unmeasured_reason is set.
A repeated answer is a replay of an earlier run. Its provenance.computed_at says
when it was produced.

docs/concepts/sovereign-models/.title: Sovereign models
docs/concepts/sovereign-models/.body:
Sovereign models

All of FACE's inference, including text reasoning, vision and voice, runs on
models served by the inference plane of your deployment: Runink's machines on a trial or when Runink runs FACE for you, your own cloud or servers when you host it. FACE calls no outside
AI service on any plan.
It also ships no inference binary: it is an HTTP client of the platform's shared model
plane.
The model plane contract
FACE talks to the plane through the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API:



Purpose
Endpoint FACE calls
Base URL




Text and vision generation
POST /v1/chat/completions
The inference endpoint setting




One endpoint setting is the only one FACE reads for the plane. The vision
and voice tiers can have their own endpoints and default to it.
A configured service token is sent as a bearer token. FACE never generates a
service token. A plane that requires one and a FACE configured without one fails
per call with the plane's own authorisation error.
Admission control is available. A deployment setting bounds concurrent inference calls
at the one door every call passes through. It's off when unset or 0.

Deploying and sizing the plane is the platform's job. See
Operations.
When the plane is not configured
There is no local fallback tier, so a FACE with no plane has no inference at all. FACE
refuses to run in that state, in two places:

At startup. If the inference endpoint is unset or blank, the server refuses to
start. The error names the missing setting and explains that FACE has no local model
server.
Per call. If a model call still reaches an empty base URL, ModelService
returns gRPC FailedPrecondition with a message that names the missing setting.
The message says it is a deployment fault in the deployment's configuration,
not a transient error.


FailedPrecondition was chosen because retrying can't fix it. It's a configuration
state, and the FACE app can show the sentence verbatim.
ModelService
ModelService is FACE's gRPC door to the plane. Every agent, deriver and extractor that
needs a model goes through it.



RPC
Purpose




Generate
Text or multimodal generation.


Embedding
Deprecated. Answers Unimplemented.


SynthesizeSpeech
Text to WAV audio through the in-cluster text-to-speech service.


SpeakFetchSummary
The spoken executive summary of the latest fetch.



Task routing
GenerateRequest.task_type says which kind of model a call needs:



TaskType
Model id FACE sends
Routed to




TASK_TYPE_GENERAL / TASK_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
default
The general reasoning tier


TASK_TYPE_CODE
coder
The code tier


TASK_TYPE_VISION
vision
The vision tier



The platform's model router chooses the tier from that id.
GenerateRequest.model is deprecated and the server ignores it.
Which model answered
Every answer records which backend served it, as the router reported it, in
GenerateResponse.served_by (the router's X-Runink-Served-By header, written as
/@, for example general/@). When the main
model could not answer and the router's smaller fast tier did, fallback says why:
unreachable or training. If the router sent no header, the configured model is recorded instead, as configured rather than as reported.
Images are typed
A picture travels in ImagePart (raw bytes, a mime_type, and a text_offset into
the prompt), never as base64 inside prompt text. The receiver base64-encodes it once,
when it builds the data: URL the plane expects. Because an image has its own field, a
string in untrusted text can't be misread as an image.
ChatMessage.images carries images per turn in multi-turn
conversations.
Reading the results

A configured URL is not a reachable plane. The startup refusal checks that
someone wrote the variable down. It dials nothing.
A reachable plane is not a loaded model. The plane can answer on its port while
weights are still loading.
Being sovereign doesn't make a model accurate. This page describes where
inference runs, not how good its answers are. The checks on model
output are on Structured output and
Agents & oversight.

docs/concepts/structured-output/.title: Structured output
docs/concepts/structured-output/.body:
Structured output

Model answers reach FACE in a fixed, structured form and are turned into typed results
before anything is shown. An answer that cannot be turned into a typed result is not
shown as a result.
What you see

A result or a stated failure. If a model gives no usable answer, FACE reports that
as an error or a stated absence. It never reports "nothing found" in its place.
An empty result is a valid answer. A correctly empty list, such as a frame with no
inspectable object, is reported as empty.
Answers are checked before they are shown. Content is checked by the guardrails
and the review of proposed actions described on
Agents & oversight.

The Ask answer's layout
Alongside the spoken answer and the action cards, FACE chooses which blocks the
Ask answer shows for the question, in order: for
example a table, a map or the answer itself. The blocks are filled from the run's own
records. A block the run cannot fill is left out, and a source that was read and holds
nothing says why. The answer comes first.
Reading the results

A successful parse proves shape, not truth. It says nothing about whether the
answer is right.
Boundaries on content are set elsewhere: see
Evidence documents and
Agents & oversight.

docs/concepts/grounding/.title: Grounding
docs/concepts/grounding/.body:
Grounding

Grounding means giving an agent evidence from the tenant's own records, so that it
reasons over what your data says rather than only its prompt. Every grounded result
cites the passage it came from.
What is searched
FACE searches what it has indexed for your tenant:

ingested documents (a files connection's Index documents, on
Settings › Integrations);
earlier answers;
fetch samples;
scenario simulations;
retained web research.

An operator can also point a deployment at a directory of reference material. FACE only
reads that directory. If none is set, nothing is cited from it.
When a search finds nothing, FACE says the data has nothing to say. When the data can't
be searched at all, FACE says that instead, so "our data says nothing" and "retrieval is
unavailable" are never confused.
Per-tenant scoping
Each tenant's material is kept apart from every other tenant's. A document is always
filed under the tenant of the signed-in session, never under a tenant named inside the
document, and a search reads only what the caller is entitled to see.
Durability
Indexed material is stored durably, in your object store when one is configured and
otherwise on the instance's own disk with owner-only permissions. It survives a restart.
The index holds document text, so it is treated as customer data at rest.
Security describes how it is sealed at rest.
Reading the results

A grounded answer is not a correct answer. Retrieval supplies context; the model
can still misread it.
A hit is a word match, not a meaning match. A passage that says the same thing in
other words may not be found. Ask with the words the documents use.
Grounding is only as good as what was indexed. An empty index grounds nothing,
and that is reported as an absence, not as a finding.

docs/concepts/evidence-documents/.title: Evidence documents
docs/concepts/evidence-documents/.body:
Evidence documents

An evidence document (EvidenceDocument) is a document a third party acts on,
such as an adjuster, a carrier's claims desk or a court. FACE attaches one to an
ActionCard in evidence_document. You read it on the card on Actionable Twins, and
in full through the card's View full decision artifact. It is sealed when a person
approves the card. The contract is strict about what these documents are and are not:

These documents assemble a file, show what was read, and propose one next step for a
person entitled to take it. They do not underwrite, bind, settle, or satisfy an
obligation on anyone's behalf.

What a document holds
Every figure in a document cites the record it came from. narrative is optional prose that may be drafted for a person to read.



Field
What it holds




kind
One value from EvidenceDocumentKind (below).


subject_id
The customer's own identifier for the shipment, claim or entry.


facts (DocumentFact)
What the records say. Every fact carries at least one citation id.


findings (DocumentFinding)
What was determined, as stable codes such as OSD_SHORT or SLA_BREACH_CONFIRMED, with a severity and the figures used.


citations (Citation)
Where each figure came from (see below).


deadlines (DocumentDeadline)
A date computed from a record date by a named rule (for example CARMACK_NOTICE_9M, COGSA_SUIT_1Y) with its authority, and the citation that supplied the start date.


claimed_amount, exposure_amount, units_short, units_damaged
Headline figures. Absent means not measured.


absent (AbsentFigure)
Why a figure is missing, for example NO_BACKING_RECORD, NOT_STATED_ON_DOCUMENT or ILLEGIBLE.


narrative (DocumentNarrative)
Optional prose. authored_by names the author, and figure_ids lists every figure the prose mentions.


seal (DocumentSeal)
Set at approval. Never set at derivation.



Citations
A Citation has everything a reader needs to go and check a figure:

source_kind, source_id (the record's id in the customer's system), and the
field read.
value: the value as read.
connection_id, plus lineage_record_id pointing at the extraction record.
observed_at: when the record was read.
perception: set when a value was read off a scanned document image. If it is absent, the value came from a structured record.

Sealing
A document is sealed when an operator approves the card. The seal (seal) shows
that the document has not changed since approval. A rejected card is left unsealed.
The vocabulary: 18 document kinds
EvidenceDocumentKind is a fixed set of kinds. FACE emits the 18 kinds below.



Kind
What it states




Paralegal and claims recovery



STATEMENT_OF_POSITION
States claimed_amount.


OSD_REPORT
The cargo value short or damaged.


NOTICE_OF_INTENT_TO_CLAIM
States exposure_amount.


SUBROGATION_DEMAND
States claimed_amount.


Cargo insurance and underwriting



FNOL
The reserve on a newly reported loss.


CARGO_LOSS_SURVEY
States exposure_amount.


WARRANTY_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT
States exposure_amount.


Shipper contracts and liability



RATE_CON_ACCESSORIAL_AUDIT
Accessorials billed above the rate confirmation.


MSA_SLA_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT
Service credits owed under an SLA clause.


Field operations and cold chain



TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION
States exposure_amount only when the readings state load_value WITH a load_value_currency; otherwise it is Not measured.


CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT
No exposure figure.


CUSTOMS_MANIFEST_EXCEPTION
The delay's cost is on the customs card.


Reverse, reactive and equipment



RETURN_DISPOSITION
The disposition of a return.


SERVICE_DISRUPTION
A service disruption.


EQUIPMENT_LIMIT_APPROACH
An approaching limit is not a loss.


Recovery leakage and indicator review



CLAIMS_LEAKAGE
States exposure_amount.


FRAUD_INDICATOR_REVIEW
An indicator is not savings. States exposure_amount.


Revenue recovery



DEDUCTION_DISPUTE
States claimed_amount: the part of a customer's deduction that the run's own purchase order, proof of delivery and invoice do not support. FACE sends it nowhere.



The kind names above drop the EVIDENCE_DOCUMENT_KIND_ prefix. See Action cards & money for how money is shown.
Names chosen to avoid over-claiming
EQUIPMENT_LIMIT_APPROACH is deliberately not called "predictive maintenance". The
deriver measures a channel's trend against a limit the feed itself states, and
reports when that trend reaches the limit. No failure probability is produced.
CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT keeps one rule: an unrecorded handoff is not a break in
custody. Every finding is a statement about the record, never about the goods or the
people handling them.
The underwriting documents never decide coverage. No finding code says VOID,
DECLINED, REPUDIATED or anything like it. Those are an underwriter's words.
Reading the results

A document is a file, not a decision. It proposes one next step for a person
entitled to take it. It doesn't serve notice, file a claim or settle anything.
A computed deadline is an input, not legal advice. It doesn't preserve a right on
anyone's behalf. The document carries due_unix and no "days remaining" figure; the
client computes the countdown at render time.
A citation proves provenance, not correctness. It shows exactly which record a
figure came from. It doesn't show that the record was right.
A seal shows the document has not changed since approval. It doesn't prove who
approved them. For that, see the decision trail on
Action cards & money.

docs/concepts/action-cards-and-money/.title: Action cards & money
docs/concepts/action-cards-and-money/.body:
Action cards & money

An action card (ActionCard) is a recommended action waiting for a person to
approve or reject it. You decide cards on Actionable Twins, where they sit in three
lanes:

Waiting for you: cards that still need a decision.
In flight: approved, with no final outcome recorded yet.
Back: a final outcome is recorded (recovered in full or in part, or denied).

Each lane's heading counts its items and adds up the money its cards state. Cards that
state no amount are counted apart. The same cards appear at their place on
the page's Map view. Play chips filter the list (claims, disruptions, routes,
fulfilment and the other plays).
Cards come from three places:

FACE's analysis of the tenant's own records, which produces the twin cards and
the evidence documents.
The twins agent.
An option a person sent for approval from Options (see
Options sent for approval).

Every card is served through TwinsService.
Anatomy of a card



Field
Meaning




type
The business domain and routing key. The derivers and handlers emit Compliance, Finance, Operations, Procurement and S&OP. Model-produced cards may carry another string, which clients treat as uncategorised.


priority, impact, status
status is Approved or Rejected once decided. Empty means pending.


transaction_value
The card's contribution to the dollar headline (see below).


Artifact fields
One typed payload per artifact family: route_card, email_draft, calendar_invite, erp_update, claims_card, cold_chain_card, customs_clearance_card, and others.


evidence_document
One field for the whole evidence-document family. See Evidence documents.


origin (ActionOrigin)
Which stage produced the card, as the wire spells it (reconcile, fetch or simulate), with a run_id and a label. If it's absent, the stage wasn't recorded.


judgement
The reviewer's verdict, reached before the card was accepted. See Agents & oversight.


authority (ActionAuthority)
The approval the decision-authority policy requires: its tier, how many distinct named approvals, the rule that decided it and why. See Auditability & lineage.


execution (ActionExecution)
What approving will do on this instance, step by step, before anyone approves. records_only=true means approving records the decision and nothing else runs.


decision_option
Set on a card that is an option sent for approval from Options (see below).


decision_trail
Who decided the card, when, which way and why (see below).


recovery_trail, latest_outcome
What happened after the approval, as named people recorded it, and the last recorded outcome. These move a card from In flight to Back.



GetActionQueue returns the pending queue by default. Pass
status="Approved" or status="Rejected" to read back decided cards, and use
workflow_type to filter on type.
Options sent for approval
On Options, FACE compares the what-if options for one decision behind the selected
run's checks (HypothesisService.CompareOptions). Options are compared on one shared measure. FACE marks one Recommended only when it is clearly better on this data. Otherwise it says No clear winner on this data and why. An option with no baseline is Not measured and is not ranked.
Send for approval calls SendToTwins with the decision, the option and the run. The
server compares the options again and queues the option with the figures it computed
itself. The card lands in Waiting for you on Actionable Twins and carries
decision_option: the decision, the option's lever and change, what it was measured to
do, the figure as measured, and whether it was the recommended one. The response names
the approval it needs: one named person, or two different named people.
Approving it records the decision and changes nothing by itself. It is never
automatic.
Estimated and assumed effects are labelled apart. Each card says whether an option's effect was estimated from your records or is the option's own assumption. An option your data never exercised is Not measured, naming the data it needs.
Money headline
The money a lane's heading shows on Actionable Twins is a sum of what its cards state.
Rejected cards do not count, and a card that states no dollar amount (an emissions card, for example) contributes nothing. Each dollar is counted once. Documents that state a figure they do not add to the headline still show that figure to the reader, in claimed_amount (what the document asks for) or exposure_amount (value at risk, not yet lost).
Value ledger
TwinsService.GetValueLedger returns, for the tenant and a period, the money FACE
identified, what people approved and filed, what was recovered, and what expired
unfiled. Recovered money is kept in two figures: what people entered, and what the
operator's own claims system states. Every figure names its basis. The ledger bills nothing.
Where you see it: the line above the lanes on Actionable Twins (recovered this
quarter against FACE's fee, with the full ledger folded under it), and the Recovered
this quarter tile of the money line on Why.
The money line is on Why only, not on Ask. Its seven tiles are At risk, Owed to you, Claim windows
closing in 14 days, Waiting for your approval, Recovered this quarter, Shipments at risk
and OTIF fines, led by what the run's persona reads first. Only Recovered this quarter
reads the ledger. Waiting for your approval reads the run's pending decisions
(TwinsService.GetActionQueue), and the board tiles come from the selected run's
operations board (FetchService.GetOperationsBoard), computed from the rows that run
read. A tile with no basis says Not measured. See
Why.
Savings summary
GetSavingsSummary returns two separate figures:

total_savings_usd: the pipeline. It counts savings on cards nobody has rejected.
approved_savings_usd: the subset the operator has committed to. It's always less
than or equal to the total.

Neither figure is "realised." These figures do not record whether an approved
action was carried out in the world, so no client may label either figure that way.
What a person recorded after an approval is in the card's recovery_trail and shows in
the Back lane. The FACE app does not display GetSavingsSummary today; it is an API
call.
Deciding a card
ExecuteAction is the one place a person decides a card:

The decider is identified from the verified session. An approval is refused
unless the session token's subject can be verified. A rejection is recorded
whatever the attribution says.
A reason is required on rejection and optional on approval.
Whitespace-only counts as empty. The limit is 2000 characters, and a longer reason
is refused rather than truncated.
On approval, the evidence document is sealed (see
Sealing), and any executable
artifacts run.
The response reports what happened:
decision_recorded: the decision was durably written.
success: false only when an approval executed nothing.
transaction_id: minted only on success.
not_executed: tokens such as email:no_google_connector,
calendar:not_implemented, erp:not_implemented or billing:charge_failed,
one for each artifact that didn't run.



How a client should read the response. decision_recorded=true with
success=false means the card is decided but nothing was executable. The client
should stop, and must not retry. Genuine failures arrive as gRPC status errors
instead.
The decision trail
ActionCard.decision_trail is a list of ActionDecision entries, and the last entry
is the current decision. Each entry records:

decision: Approved or Rejected.
decided_at: the server's clock when the decision was recorded.
decided_by: the verified sub claim of the deciding session, never a value
the caller supplied.
attribution (DeciderAttribution): how well the decider could be named.
decided_by_role: the verified role.
reason.

A retried decision with the same content doesn't add a new entry. The original entry
is kept, including its original time. An operator who changes their mind gets a
second entry.
Reading the results

The headline is a sum of claims about money, not money received. It's only as
good as the cited records behind each card.
decided_by doesn't prove a human pressed a button. A person's token driven by
a script looks the same. decided_by_role separates a service account from a
person's session.
The trail is a verified attribution, not a signature. It is written by the
instance into a store the instance owns.
A required reason proves someone typed something, not that it's true or
complete.
An approval is not an execution receipt. Read transaction_id and
not_executed.
A recommended option is the clear winner on the rows read, not a guarantee. Read
whether its effect was estimated or assumed before approving it.

docs/concepts/statistics-and-ml/.title: Statistics & ML
docs/concepts/statistics-and-ml/.body:
Statistics & ML

FACE's classical analysis comes from Runink's own ml library. It's pure Go and calls
no external model server. The statistics on this page use no neural network; the few
packages that need a tensor backend (ml/linear, ml/segment and the camera tools) run on the CPU inside FACE. FACE exposes this analysis through
AnalysisService, and the fetch pipeline uses the same code internally.
AnalysisService
AnalyzeTimeSeries
Forecasts a series forecast_horizon steps ahead. The default horizon is 3.

Minimum input. Fewer than 5 points returns
recommended_model="Insufficient Data (Need > 5 points)" and no forecast.
Primary path: prophet.AnalyzeSeries. This is a full series EDA. It runs
descriptive statistics, then an ADF stationarity test, then ACF/PACF
autocorrelation, then a Prophet decomposition (piecewise-linear trend, Fourier
seasonality and changepoints). Finally it fits ARIMA, and a rolling backtest
picks between ARIMA and Prophet. The response carries:
recommended_model: the chosen model, marked [backtest-selected], for example
ARIMA(p,d,q) [backtest-selected].
stationarity_test: the ADF result, with the statistic and the 5% critical value.
anomalies: the EDA's findings, plus any Prophet residual anomalies.


Fallback. If the EDA can't fit a model, an ordinary-least-squares line is
extrapolated. The response says Linear Regression (Fallback) and states that the
EDA was unavailable.

AnalyzeFeature
Tests autocorrelation at lags 1 to 5 of target. Any lag with |ACF| > 0.5 is
reported in significant_lags, and a target_lag_ feature (for example target_lag_2) is proposed for it.
Fewer than 10 points returns Insufficient data, and a constant series returns
Constant target.
ClusterRefinement
Clusters items into domains by their feature vectors:

Validate the vectors. The first non-empty vector sets the dimension. Vectors
that are missing or have a different dimension are kept in place as noise
(-1) rather than dropped, so labels stay aligned with the caller's items.
Cluster. Density-based clustering groups the items, choosing its parameters by cluster quality.
Rerank. A heuristic reranker applies per-domain weights to order the items within each cluster.

The response returns clusters (a label per item), noise (the indices labelled
noise) and health_score. The health score is a cluster quality score.
AnalyzeCausal
A do-calculus intervention over a graph the caller states in full:

nodes maps each node to its observed value.
edges (CausalEdge) carry a structural effect_size.
An intervention sets intervention_node to intervention_value, and the change
propagates along edges by multiplying through each effect size.
The response returns effect on target_node and the target's new_target_value.
An edge naming an unknown node, or an edge set with a cycle, is refused with
InvalidArgument. The call never runs over a partly built graph.

An edge at 0 declares that there is no relationship. A missing edge means the
relationship is unknown. To run an intervention over the connected estate instead
of a hand-written graph, use PostureService.AnalyzeEstateCausal. See
Posture & maturity.
InferBayesian
Posterior inference over a Bayesian network (ml/knowledge). The request carries
evidence and a target node, but it has no field for defining variables or conditional
probability tables. So on an instance with no defined network, the call answers
FailedPrecondition and explains why, instead of returning an empty result with an
OK status.
AnalyzeDescriptiveStats
Returns the mean, median, variance, standard deviation, skewness and kurtosis of
data, computed by knowledge.DescriptiveStats.
ClassifyESGRelevance
Returns relevance_score, a keyword-lexicon score from 0 to 1. Each text is scored
by how often terms such as carbon, emission, net-zero and governance appear,
weighted per term and capped at 1.0. It's a relevance heuristic, not a trained
classifier. The same texts are also passed to FACE's digestion pipeline (clustering,
EDA, forecast and causal passes). A failure there is logged and doesn't change the
score.
What ml provides underneath



Package
Used by FACE for




ml/knowledge
Clustering, k-means, causal do-calculus, Bayesian networks, descriptive statistics, community detection and domain inference.


ml/prophet
Prophet decomposition, ARIMA, ADF, ACF/PACF and the unified series EDA.


ml/xgboost
Two separate things. The heuristic cluster reranker above, and a real gradient-boosted tree implementation with probability calibration.


ml/segment
Region proposals for vision. It proposes where things are, never what they are.


ml/linear
Linear regression on a CPU-only backend. FACE wires the library's audit hook.


ml/eda
Time-series exploration over a fetch's rows, used by the causal estimate and causal simulation code.


ml/route
A vehicle-routing solver over positions FACE already holds. It calls no routing service and geocodes nothing. Used by the Map view's asset locations, routes and live-traffic checks.


ml/stream
An online anomaly detector for sensor readings, with fixed memory per series. Used by the live sensor views and the fraud-indicator deriver.


ml/detect
A local object detector for live camera frames. It names what is in a frame; it grades nothing. See Vision & CCTV.



ml holds no state. Everything is computed and returned, and persistence is the
calling app's concern.
Reading the results

A forecast is a model's extrapolation of the series you supplied. It knows
nothing outside that series. The backtest picks the better of two models on the
series' own history, and that is not a guarantee about the future.
A causal effect is the consequence of the graph you stated. The server computes
it; it doesn't discover it. Wrong edges give wrong effects, with no error.
Correlation edges are not causal edges. Measured correlations between data
domains in a fetch are recorded as CORRELATED_WITH and nothing more.
A cluster is a statistical grouping. A high silhouette means the points separate
well. It doesn't mean the domain names attached to them are right.
The ESG score counts words. It doesn't assess performance against any ESG
standard.

docs/concepts/posture-and-maturity/.title: Posture & maturity
docs/concepts/posture-and-maturity/.body:
Posture & maturity

On Why you see what your data estate looks like and how ready it is: each business
area's health, the domains and how they relate, and the readiness indicators.
PostureService serves those figures and grounds the other agents.



RPC
What it does




GetHealthScore
Serves the latest fetch's posture snapshot. With no snapshot, it runs a posture analysis.


BuildDomainGraph
The fast half of a session fetch. It derives data domains and their relationships.


AnalyzeEstateCausal
A do-calculus intervention over the connected estate (see below).


ListIncidents
Data-maturity assessments (DataMaturityAssessment).


GetContext
Semantic context items for an agent type.



What is measured
Each domain gets a DomainHealth. Its figures come from what the profiler read. Each value has its *_measured flag set:



Gauge
How it's measured




quality_stability_pct
Filled values ÷ sampled values, whatever the share. quality_sampled_values and quality_filled_values give the n.


risk_pii_pct
The share of columns whose names match personal-data patterns.


lineage_pct, freshness_pct, policy_pct, cost_efficiency_pct
Not measured, with the flag false.



There is no letter grade and no health score. What the profiler observes is reported as facts: a join key or a timestamp column is present or not, values were left empty or not, PII-like columns are present or not. issues lists them, for example "no join key detected (lineage risk)" or "incomplete sample values: 49 of 120 filled".
Readiness findings are those facts. Each gap above is one assessment and one
measure to take. Its severity is Not graded: no target is set for it.
A failed scan returns an error. With no connected data source, the answer is FailedPrecondition: "connect a data source first".
The empty_trip category is always empty. Nothing in the platform measures empty-trip or deadhead running, so show it as not measured.
Measure wording records where it came from. OptimizationSOP.provenance (MeasureProvenance) says whether a measure was read from a source, computed from measured data, or written by the posture agent. Only the last may be labelled as AI-generated.
Lineage 
A join key present is a schema property, not observed lineage. It reads the same whether
a source has been pulled a thousand times or never, because it depends only on whether
a join key exists.
Observed lineage is a separate record, written by the backend's lineage recorder:

Where records come from. Each extraction and each delivery is recorded, and so is each camera ingest.
How they're stored. Records are append-only in the object store.
What they contain. Structure only: column names, counts, durations, a
literal-free query shape and a fingerprint, and a closed-set error class. Never
result values, driver messages or credentials.
How to read them. LineageService.GetSourceActivity returns per-connection
activity over a window:
extractions, deliveries and rows.
The outcome mix: ok, empty and failed. empty means the source connected
and returned nothing, which is neither a failure nor a delivery.
error_classes, destinations, and the last_columns names.
durable and durable_reason, which say whether the records survive a restart.
Without a durable sink, the process keeps only a small in-memory ring.



Some reads aren't in the log. A camera frame ingest is recorded with a row count of
zero, because a camera sends frames, not rows.
See Vision & CCTV.
The domain graph
In the FACE app, the estate is mapped by the fetch itself: its business-domains phase
derives the domains and their relationships from the connections the fetch reads, and
Why shows the result. A newly confirmed connection joins the map at the next fetch.
There is no manual control to map it again.
BuildDomainGraph derives domains and their structural edges. Measured CORRELATED_WITH edges come from the fetch pipeline instead. See
Fetch pipeline.
When connected sources are read, each edge's relation names the kind of evidence behind it, and a guess is named as a guess.
Value sampling is on by default. metadata_only_connection_ids turns it off per connection. Sampled values never appear in a log line, an error, a lineage record or a model prompt.
FACE still serves include_connected_sources for API clients and for
AnalyzeEstateCausal. The FACE app calls GetHealthScore only; BuildDomainGraph,
AnalyzeEstateCausal, ListIncidents and GetSourceActivity are API calls.
Estate causal analysis 
AnalyzeEstateCausal runs an intervention over columns of the connected estate. A
node is ., carrying the source's own aggregate over that
column.
The caller supplies the coefficients (EstateCausalCoefficient), because nothing in a catalogue or a sample measures how much one column moves another.
How to read the response:

Read answered first. When FACE cannot answer, it explains why in refusal.
weakest_basis is the weakest basis among the edges the effect travelled along.
basis_statement is written to be shown verbatim beside the number.
node_refusals, edge_refusals, nodes_added and columns_refused give the
denominators. A graph of four columns out of nine hundred measurable ones is not a
causal graph of the estate.

Reading the results

The facts reflect structure, not how the data is used. A key, a timestamp and
no PII-like columns don't mean the data is correct, current or governed.
A join key present is not lineage. Use GetSourceActivity for what was actually
read and delivered.
A declared foreign key is a referential constraint, not a causal claim.
An estate causal answer reflects the coefficients you supplied. It rests on
those coefficients, over the columns that had measurements.

docs/concepts/simulation-and-twins/.title: Simulation & twins
docs/concepts/simulation-and-twins/.body:
Simulation & twins

After a run answers your question on Ask, two pages carry it forward:

Options answers "what could we do, and what is each option worth?". It leads
with the options for the decision behind the run's checks, scored and sendable for
approval. Below them is what FACE tested: the run's scenarios as a list, with a
Graph view, and a New Simulation action. The status counts, what went to the
twins and the run step by step sit in the folded How FACE knows this.
Actionable Twins holds the decision cards in three lanes (Waiting for you, In
flight, Back), with a Map view on the same page that places each card where your
own data says it is.

This page covers the services behind both, and the claims and reverse-logistics
service.
Options and scenarios (HypothesisService) 



RPC
What it does
Where you see it




CompareOptions
Scores the what-if options for one decision on one shared measure over a run's measured rows, each with a 95% range, and names a recommended one only when it is the clear winner.
Options, at the top


SendToTwins
With decision_key, option_key and run_id: compares the options again and queues the named one for approval. Without them: turns a validated scenario into an action card.
The card waits on Actionable Twins


GetHypothesisVariables
Scenario groups inferred from the estate, with each scenario's simulation_state and the run-level swarm_census.
Options


InteractiveSimulate / SimulateScenario
Runs one scenario through the agent loop and returns SimulateScenarioResponse. The app uses InteractiveSimulate.
Options


ValidateHypothesis
Checks a scenario against the recognised rules and data.
Options


GetTwinsHandoff / SetTwinsHandoffExclusion
The scenarios a run's analysis handed to the twins agent, with each verdict and impact, and whether a person removed one from the next twins analyses.
Options, How FACE knows this


GetScenarioBuilder, SaveCustomScenario, AddScenarioItem, AddScenarioTerm
One run's scenarios with their business categories, the items each tests and the market terms each watches, plus what your team added.
Options, New Simulation


AnalyzeTelemetry
Agentic analysis of an equipment time series. The FACE app does not call it.
API only



The scenario list and its Graph view read FetchService.GetScenarioGraph: the run's
scenarios and what each one tested, computed from the run's stored records. Anything the run did not record is shown as a gap.
Comparing options
How the options are scored, recommended and sent for approval is covered in
Action cards & money.
In short: options are compared on one measure, and nothing runs until a named person approves.
Scenarios
FACE proposes scenarios from your estate's domains, the relationships it measured
between them and your rules, and tests them. Options
shows how many were tested and how many produced a result. A scenario that was not
tested says so; it is never hidden. Each tested scenario returns its impacts (metric,
change, risk level and horizon), the evidence it relied on, forecasts with intervals
and any anomalies. Results are listed side by side.
Validation
ValidateHypothesis checks a scenario against your rules. valid_data says whether a fetch has grounded the instance, valid_logic says whether the scenario holds against your rules, each concern becomes a risk_flags entry, and rationale explains the verdict.
Digital twins (TwinsService)



RPC
What it does
Where you see it




GetActionQueue / ExecuteAction
The action queue and the human decision. See Action cards & money.
Actionable Twins lanes, and each card's place on the Map view


GetValueLedger
Money identified, approved, filed, recovered and expired for a period, each figure with its basis.
Actionable Twins (above the lanes) and the money line on Why


ListDecisionLog
The decision log. Admins only.
Settings › Account, Admin


ProposeStandingRule, ApproveStandingRule, RevokeStandingRule, ListStandingRules
Turn an approved decision into a decision-authority rule. Proposing needs a writer; approving needs an org admin who is not the proposer.
A decided card on Actionable Twins


ListAssetLocations
Where each asset in FACE's fetched data is: a position only where a source stated one, and every other asset listed with the reason it has none.
Map view


ListRunRoutes
The routes and destinations one run inferred from the rows it read, each proposal with its judging state, and what is missing when no destination has a position.
Map view


ListLiveTraffic / AnalyseRoutesLive
Public transit and road feeds found from the run's towns and regions, read only while someone watches the map, and each route against the live events near it.
Map view


ListRunProviders
Service providers one run looked for on the public web near the sites in trouble (disposal, alternate warehousing, fleet repair, cold storage), with the queries sent.
Map view


OptimizeRoute
Computes a route through the session's Google Routes connector and returns distance, duration and polyline.
Map view, fleet plan


StreamTwins, QuickAsk, UploadAnalyze
Interactive twin reasoning over text, audio, frames or a document; retrieval-based Q&A for S&OP and inventory questions; root-cause or savings analysis of an uploaded CSV, Excel or PDF file. The query is screened before it reaches a model.
The assistant, opened from its floating button on every page


GetSavingsSummary
Pipeline savings and approved savings. The FACE app does not display it.
API only


GenerateRoadmap
A phased roadmap (Digitize, Connect, Analyze, Automate) from maturity scores. The FACE app does not call it.
API only


SubmitFeedback
Records feedback on a generated response to the durable record store.



From Actionable Twins you also open:

Follow-ups, which run on the cards selected on the list or the map.
The Compliance, Finance and Operations remediation views, from the
page's Remediation links. See
Compliance, finance, operations.
The site plans and the twin entities, as panels over the Map view.
