Per-account figures, with the number of rows behind each.
Concentration figures and flags.
Recommended actions, each naming who decides: re-pricing (Commercial Pricing
Manager), service-level and account reviews (Account Manager), payment terms
(Credit Controller), concentration (Commercial Director).
On request, a short written summary. It phrases the figures above and adds none.

Human oversight

Every recommended action is a draft. Sending one for approval puts it in the
approval queue, where a named person approves or rejects it.
FACE does not change a price, send a notice or close an account.

Model
The optional summary uses the general reasoning tier.
Where it runs and data handling
On the deployment's own model plane: Runink's shared machines on a Trial, your
own cloud on Cloud and your own servers on On-premises. No outside AI service is called on any
plan, and nothing leaves the deployment. See
Facts shared by every card.
Guardrails

Business accounts only. Rows that describe an individual or a consumer are
excluded and counted, never analysed.
Refuses to profile or track an individual person.
Refuses to price or segment by protected characteristics.
Refuses to inflate, hide or adjust cost to serve, margin, OTIF or payment figures.
Recommends only. It does not send notices or terminate contracts.

How to read its results

Cost to serve is what your rows state. Overheads your records do not allocate to
orders are not in it, and a missing cost is never treated as zero.
A churn signal is a pattern in your records, not a prediction that an account will
leave.
Days to pay is measured over paid invoices only.
Concentration is computed in the currency with the most revenue; accounts in other
currencies are not added to it.

Thresholds
There are no built-in thresholds. Each is a target set for a deployment, or for your
organisation by an admin under Admin → Public registries & market data. Until a
target is set, the figure it would judge is shown as measured, no signal or review is
raised on it, and the result names it as having no target. Every result shows the
thresholds it applied.



Threshold
Default




OTIF below which a service-level review is suggested
No target set


Days to pay above which a payment-terms review is suggested
No target set


One account's share of revenue above which concentration is flagged
No target set


Claim rate above which an account review is suggested
No target set


Recent orders as a share of the prior window, at or below which "order volume fell"
No target set


Days since the last order, as a multiple of the account's median gap, above which "no recent orders"
No target set


OTIF drop in points at or above which "service level fell"
No target set


Disputed share of recent orders at or above which "disputes rising"
No target set



Revenue concentration is also flagged when its Herfindahl-Hirschman index is above
1,800, the level the 2023 US DOJ and FTC Merger Guidelines call highly concentrated.
That is a market measure, applied here to your revenue shares, and the flag says so.

docs/user-guide/sign-in/.title: Sign in
docs/user-guide/sign-in/.body:
Sign in

Sign in with your email and password, or with Google when your deployment offers it,
then FACE opens on the Overview. Only accounts Runink has
approved can sign in: there is no public sign-up. See
Access and the trial.
The app opens on the sign-in page. Any page you open while signed out also brings you
here, and so does a session that ends or that the server rejects.
Sign-in methods
When the page loads, the app asks the backend which sign-in methods it offers.
The backend answers on its /auth/config endpoint.



Method
When it appears




Email and Password
Always.


Google single sign-on
Only when the backend reports Google sign-in as configured. An or divider separates it from the password form.



If the app cannot reach the sign-in service, the Google button is replaced by
Single sign-on is unavailable — the sign-in service could not be reached. You can
still sign in with your email and password. If the backend reports that it has no
single sign-on, the page shows no Google button and no message.

Enter your email and password
Type your address in Email and your password in Password. The eye button
(Show password / Hide password) reveals what you typed. Press Enter in the
email field to move to the password field.

Select Sign In
Or press Enter in the password field. While the server checks your credentials, the
button shows a spinner. Screen readers announce it as Signing in.

Complete the second factor, if asked
If your account has an authenticator enrolled, the app opens the MFA page (see
below).

Land on the Overview
After a successful sign-in you land on the Overview.
A bare address, or /, opens it too.


With Google, select the Google button and complete Google's own dialog. A browser that
is already signed in to Google may complete the sign-in without asking.
Two-factor verification
The MFA Verification page asks you to Enter the 6-digit code from your
authenticator. Type the code into the six boxes. The code is submitted as soon as the
last digit is in. Screen readers announce Verifying code while it is checked.
Cancel / Return to Login abandons the attempt. You can only reach this page while a
second-factor challenge is waiting. Otherwise the app sends you back to sign-in.
If your account is refused
An account that is valid but not approved for this FACE deployment is refused at
sign-in. Access is granted by Runink: ask your Runink contact or your organisation's
FACE administrator. Your role (Admin, Editor or Viewer) comes with that
approval, and decides whether you see the Admin entry
under Settings › Account.
Signing out
Sign out with Log out at the foot of the rail, or under Settings › Account. Signing out
closes any dialogs that were open and returns you to this page.
RPCs behind these pages

IdentityService.Login: password, Google and the second-factor step.
IdentityService.Logout.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/navigation/.title: Navigation
docs/user-guide/navigation/.body:
Navigation

Every page after sign-in shares one frame: the rail on the left, one title line across
the top, and the assistant at the bottom right. The rail is the only menu.

The rail
The rail opens with the Overview, where FACE lands after
sign-in, then three labelled sections, and Settings at its foot:



Section
Pages




Fetch
Ask · Briefs


Simulate
Options · Why


Twins
Actionable Twins


(foot)
Settings



Below Settings is the signed-in account, with Log out.
Pages that are not in the rail light the entry they belong to:



You are on
Lit entry




A past run (/fetch/run/), or a live view opened from a connection's card (Surveillance, Live sensors, Field reader, Devices)
Ask


A brief's editor
Briefs


A scenario's details page
Options


The Map view, site plans, twin entities or one entity's page, Follow-ups, a decision artifact, a remediation screen
Actionable Twins


Admin, and the connection wizard
Settings



An address the app does not know lights Ask.
Each rail entry is a button with a visible focus ring. Screen readers announce its label
and whether it is the page you are on.
The title line
The title line reads FACE and the page's name. On Ask, Options, Why and Actionable
Twins it also names the selected run, with Run
actions (Change run, Clear). On every other page it carries the audit: how the
last run ended, as Passing, Needs attention, Failing, Running or Not
run yet, with the reason and Open audit. When runs have proposed connections, the
audit counts them.
Not run yet appears only when the server has recorded no run at all.
The activity card
While a run or another long operation works, a card narrates it over whatever page is
open. Long operations include testing a connection, indexing documents and reading a
document source.

The headline says what is running, for example Running your fetch…, then how it
ended.
The steps are the phases as the server reports them, each running, done,
failed, out of time, skipped or partial.
Show reasoning opens the run's full reasoning, with every step.
While a run works, the card may show messages from Runink's partners, each under the
partner's name (From {name}).

After the answer 
The answer coming back does not finish a run. The analysis and the twins' decisions run
after it. From the answer on, the card tells the run's story:

The headline follows how the run ends: Fetch answered — still analysing while a
phase runs; Fetch finished when every phase finished; Fetch partly finished,
or Fetch partly finished — interrupted by a server restart; Fetch failed; or
Fetch answered — its phases were not recorded.
A partly finished run says Did not finish: and names each phase.
The steps are four items, one per page: Ask (what was read), Why (what it
means), Options (what could happen) and Actionable Twins (what we do). Each
shows its state and one line from the run's own record. While a phase works it says
so, for example Judging the scenarios…, or Waiting to start. Nothing
recorded appears only for a phase that ended and left nothing.
Select an item to open its page for this run.

A finished card closes itself after a short while, but not while the pointer is over it
or focus is inside it. A running card never closes on its own. If several operations run
at once, the card shows the most recent.
The automated analysis notice
If automated analysis is not ready, a strip under the title line says so:

Automated analysis is starting up… while it loads;
Automated analysis is not ready — features that need it are unavailable. when it
cannot answer.

The strip adds Everything else works now. and offers Check again. It goes away
once automated analysis is ready.
The FACE AI assistant
The round button at the bottom right of every page opens the assistant. Its tooltip is
FACE AI, and screen readers announce Open FACE AI assistant. It floats over the
page.
The assistant knows which page you are on. It suggests the question of the selected run,
your persona's question, then two prompts for the page: on Ask and Integrations,
Create new connection and Find extra docs; on Options, Trigger Shadow
Simulation and Optimize sliders; on Why, Check Rules and Find logic gaps;
elsewhere, Help me with this screen and What can I do here?.



Control
Label




Text box
Ask FACE…


Send
Send message


Microphone
Speak your question. It is sent when you stop.


Camera
Take a photo


Attachment
Attach a file



The answer lists every step FACE ran as done, failed or blocked, with the reason.
How this was worked out shows the reasoning. FACE AI could not answer means the
request failed, and the reason follows. No answer came back means the assistant
finished but returned nothing.

Behind the frame: FetchService.RunFetchStream, ListFetchRuns and
ModelService.GetModelStatus. See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/overview/.title: Overview
docs/user-guide/overview/.body:
Overview

The Overview (/overview) is where FACE opens after sign-in, and the first entry
in the rail. It answers What needs you now, from the fetch run shown. Each card opens
the page that shows how its figure was measured.
What it shows

The answer for the run shown, with its alert and two ways on: see the options
(Options) or act on them (Actionable Twins).
The money tiles: what is at risk, owed and waiting for approval. Each opens
Why or the decisions waiting on Actionable Twins.
The checks and the operations figures for the run, validated on Why.
Agents' follow-up: what came back this quarter and the value ledger, opened on
Actionable Twins.
The fetch run shown, with when it started and Open the run. With no run
selected, the cards read your newest run that kept its rows.
One line per Why category, each opening its card on Why.

On a wide screen the cards sit side by side; a phone stacks them.
Before your first fetch
With no run yet, the page is a single card, Run your first fetch, with Start a
fetch, which opens Ask. While FACE is still reading your run history it
says Looking for your fetch runs…, and if the history cannot be read it says why.
A figure that was not measured is shown as Not measured, never as zero.
Status: available in the web app.

docs/user-guide/ask/.title: Ask
docs/user-guide/ask/.body:
Ask

Ask is where you put a question to your own data and get the answer first: what the
run found, how many decisions wait for you and what they add up to. Open it with Ask,
the first entry under Fetch in the rail (/fetch). After sign-in the app opens on
the Overview, which links here.
From top to bottom, the page holds:

The question box (Ask a question or use voice command…) and who the run is for.
Start here, until your first run has finished.
The plays and FETCH STARTERS: prepared questions, filtered by play.
The answer for the selected run.
How FACE knows this, folded: the sources, connections, coverage, runners and run
history behind the answer.

Ask shows no money tiles. The money line (what is owed, at risk and waiting) is on
Why.

Ask a question

Pick who the run is for
Beside the question box, Who this run is for shows Generalist view until you pick
a persona, then For: {name}. The run is written for that persona: the plays lead with
the persona's plays, and the money line on Why
leads with what the persona reads first. The persona changes what the answer
leads with, never what FACE reads. Personas are set up under
Settings › Personas.

Type, say or attach your question
Type in Ask a question or use voice command…, or pick a question under FETCH
STARTERS. Beside the box:

the microphone dictates your question;
Camera Input takes a photo;
Attach File attaches one or more files.

Attachments appear as chips you can remove. FACE reads each file by its content,
whatever its name says:

photos: their text, and for JPEG and PNG a structured reading of the document (type,
fields, tables, checkboxes);
PDF: the text of each page, and a scanned page as a photo;
DOCX and PPTX: their text and tables;
plain text and HTML: the text;
video clips: sampled frames, read the way a camera feed is.

A spreadsheet (.xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, .tsv, up to 25 MiB) is uploaded to your
organisation's own storage and shows as a chip with its name and number of sheets. The run
reads it the way an Excel data source is read: every sheet as a table, cited as
attached:  › . Save as a data source on a workbook's chip makes it an
Excel connection you can select in later asks. Removing the chip before sending deletes the
file; otherwise it is kept until you delete your account.
Paper receipts. On a photo's chip, Read text reads a paper receipt. While it reads, the chip shows
Reading the receipt…; then it becomes Receipt: {merchant} · {date} · {total}, or
Receipt: text read, not structured when only the text could be read. Show what
was read opens the fields, the totals check and the recognised text; a field the
receipt does not carry reads not on the receipt. With no question typed, FACE asks
Check this receipt against our orders and claims: is anything overcharged, duplicated
or owed back?
Card numbers are masked before the text is structured. In the web app the photo is
read in memory by FACE's own server and not stored; in the Android app (not yet
published) the phone reads it itself and only the masked text is sent. If nothing is
readable, the chip says to try again in better light with the receipt flat and filling
the frame.
A file FACE has no reader for is skipped, and the run says why. A run with only an
attachment and no connection still answers, from what it read.

Choose how to be told
Call Me When Finished and WhatsApp Me tell you when the run ends: once every
phase has ended, not when the answer comes back. The message says whether the run
finished, partly finished, was interrupted by a server restart, or failed.

Run it
Press Enter or select the send button (Run Fetch). The
activity card narrates the run, phase by
phase, over whatever page you open next.


If the app cannot reach the server, the run is queued on your device and sent when the
connection returns.
Start here
Until a run has finished, a Start here panel sits under the persona picker, above
the plays: From no
source to your first fetch. Each step is read from the platform, never ticked by hand.
Its steps are Connect a data source, Have a runner ready and Run your first
fetch. Each says whether it is done, or Could not check this step. The panel goes
away once every step is done.
Plays and fetch starters
The plays are what FACE recovers or protects money on: All plays, Claims
recovery, Disruptions, Routes, Fulfilment, Cold chain,
Maintenance, Inventory and Fleet. Pick a chip to see only that play's
questions under FETCH STARTERS. The persona the run is for puts its plays first.
The starters come from your connections and your runs. While FACE samples your
sources the row says Sampling your sources…, then Suggestions from a quick sample
of your sources · {time}, how many sources answered, and Refresh. A source the
sample could not read is named with a short reason; Show details shows the source's
own error.
If a play has no question yet, the row says so and offers Connect a source.
The answer 
The answer card shows the selected run:

its question, or when it ran, as the card's title;
who it was for: Generalist view or For: {name};
the answer, laid out for the question (below);
three ways on: Decide in Actionable Twins, See why and See the options.

With no run selected, the card is not shown: the question box and the plays are the
page.
An answer laid out for its question
Each answer chooses its own layout. A question about late lanes can lead with the late
shipments and the map; a "should I approve" question leads with the options; a "how
much" question leads with the figure and what it was counted over. The first block
always answers the question.
Each block is filled from the run's own records. The blocks are:



Block
Shows




The answer
What the run said, checked against your data.


A figure
One measured figure, such as At risk, Delivered late or the rows breaking a rule, with the rows it was counted over.


A table
Rows from the run's board, such as Late and past promise or Claims, with chosen columns and one filter: Late only, Closing within 14 days, Below safety stock, Missing evidence or Largest first.


A chart
A series from the run's board, such as Shipments by status, as bars.


The map
The run's routes, with Open the map.


Options
One decision's what-if options, as See the options shows them..


Decisions
What waits for a decision, or the cards the answer names. Each is decided in Actionable Twins, under its own approval rules.


Files
The files the run read, and how each was read.


What this run did not check
Phases that did not finish, sources not read and board sections not measured.



Each block has How this was found: where its value was read and over which rows.
A block whose source was read but holds nothing says Nothing to show: and why. A
figure the rows do not state says Not measured. A block whose source could not be
read says Could not be read: and the error.
How this answer was laid out says whether FACE chose the blocks for your question,
or the standard layout stands in and why. It also lists any block that was left out, with the reason.
The standard layout is the answer, then how many decisions wait and what they add up
to (No decision waiting when none does). It stands in when no layout was chosen.
The layout is stored with the run. Opening a past run shows the same layout. A run from before layouts were stored shows the standard card:
what it said (the spoken answer stays on the device that asked, so a run asked elsewhere
reads The spoken answer stays on the device that asked. What the run left for you is
below.), then what waits. If a run's layout cannot be read, the card says so and shows
the standard card.
The layout is ready when the run's decisions are: until then, the card shows the
standard answer.
How FACE knows this
How FACE knows this (Sources, coverage, runners and run history) is folded under
the answer. Open it to see:

how many of its sources the selected run read, naming the ones it could not read and
why;
how the run sampled each table and what the sample shows of each column, when the
run recorded a sample;
ACTIVE CONNECTIONS, then Operational coverage, then COMPUTE RUNNERS;
EXECUTION HISTORY, with What the run also found and Runs recorded on the
server.

Connections
Under ACTIVE CONNECTIONS, each connection has a card with its name and type, what
the server holds for it (such as whether its credential is stored), and a caption:
Included in fetch or Not included for an active connection, Switched off: not
read by Fetch for one that is switched off. The caption describes your selection. It
does not say whether the source is reachable.
Tap an active card to include it in, or leave it out of, your next run. New
connection opens the connection wizard on
Settings › Integrations › Systems. Connections a run
proposed are listed with Confirm and Dismiss.
The Active switch 
The Active switch on a connection or runner turns it on or off for every run on the
instance: yours, other people's and scheduled ones. The server enforces it and refuses a
run that names a switched-off connection or runner.
Only an admin of the instance can flip the switch. Everyone else sees Active or
Inactive. If a switch cannot be saved, {name} was not switched: {error} gives
the reason. A switched-off connection also leaves the
Map view's live layers.
Live views 
Cameras, sensors, field readers and devices are connection types. Their card opens a
live view, already narrowed to that connection (Connection {id} only; Show all
widens it):



Connection type
Button
What it shows




Video Stream (cameras)
Surveillance
The Surveillance Dashboard: Feed Ingestion grades a feed (Threat Detected — {classification} or No Threat Detected), Sensor Cueing cues one sensor from another, and COP Telemetry Feed streams events. Photos taken with Camera Input are listed under Captured media.


MQTT Bus, Sensor Gateway, GPS Telematics, RFID Reader
Live sensors
What the always-on connections hear, the candidate findings, and for admins the health of the ingest path.


Runink Edge (a handheld field reader)
Field reader
That reader's sightings as they arrive. When the stream stops, the last frame stays with its age.


Any source that reports devices
Devices
The devices the connection reported, with when each was last seen.



A reading with no stated value is never drawn as a number, and silence nobody can judge
is shown as unjudged, never as fine.
Operational coverage
Operational coverage shows what FACE can see of your operations in the sources it has
read (fleet, yard, warehouse and racks, cold chain, shipments, orders, maintenance,
drones and automation, IoT sensors and tags), and which decisions that supports. Each
decision is Ready, Blocked or Couldn't check.
Runners
Under COMPUTE RUNNERS, each runner has a card with its own Active switch. Tap an
active runner to run your next question on it. The card marked Active is the runner
the next run will use; other active runners show Standby, and a switched-off one
shows Switched off. With no pick, the run goes to the managed runner if it is active,
otherwise to the first active runner. New runner opens
Settings › Integrations › Runners.
Execution history
What the run also found lists, for the selected run, the actions the judge removed
from the answer (each marked with its verdict) and the forecasts, with ANOMALY where
one was detected.
Runs recorded on the server lists every run the server recorded for you, newest
first: when it started, how long it took, the runner, and how it ended. An org admin
sees every run in the organization. The run cards above it are kept on this device.



Outcome
Means




Successful
It answered, and every phase finished.


Partial
It answered, and at least one phase did not finish. The run names each one and why.


Running
It has not answered yet, or a phase after the answer is still running.


Answered
It answered, and the server has no record of its phases. It is never counted as successful.


Failed
It did not answer.


Refused
It was refused before it ran.


Interrupted
The server stopped before it answered. Run it again.



The answer comes back before the run is done: the analysis (the checks, the rules and
the scenario verdicts) and the twins' decisions run after it, in the background.
Archive run history, for org admins, takes every run so far off every page (Ask,
Briefs, Why, Options, Actionable Twins) for everyone on the instance. Nothing is deleted:
the runs are kept for audit, and an admin can bring them back from Show archived
with Restore or Restore all.
Open a past run
Tap a run under Runs recorded on the server to see its question and how it ended;
Show this run's results makes it the selected run.
Tap a run card kept on this device to open Fetch details (/fetch/run/): how it
ended, Query, Runner, Connections, Started, Duration, Error when
there was one, Result, What happened to the sources, Automated analysis and
Generated SQL. Reuse request asks the same question again.
The page also shows What this fetch was given: each file or capture attached to the
run and how it ended (read, read, nothing on it, skipped: {reason} or
could not be read: {reason}). Show what was read opens the reading: the
structured reading of a photo, Tables in the document, Text read (cut after
64 KiB, and it says so) and Left out. You can correct a value read from a document;
the correction is recorded with your name and the value it replaced.
The selected run 
Ask, Options, Why and Actionable Twins each show one run: the selected run. The
page's title line names it, with Change run and Clear under Run actions.

A run you start selects itself when it answers.
Otherwise the newest Successful run on the server is selected. A partial run is
never selected for you, but you can open one.
Open an earlier run lists every run the server recorded. Only a run with a
transaction id can be opened.
Clear selects no run. The choice is kept on this device.

When the selected run is not the newest one, a notice says so, for example This page
shows the fetch of {date}; a newer fetch finished on {newer}., with Show the fetch of
{date}.
With no run selected, Options, Why and Actionable Twins show only Your operation's story
starts with a fetch, with Run a fetch and Open an earlier run ({count}). A page
shows what the selected run recorded and nothing else: no figures borrowed from other
runs. If the run recorded nothing for a page, the page says so.
RPCs behind this page

FetchService.RunFetchStream (server stream), ListFetchStarters, ListFetchRuns,
GetFetchAttachments, GetAskLayout (the answer's stored layout).
ConfigService.ListConnections, ListRunners, SetConnectionActive,
SetRunnerActive (admin only).
TwinsService.GetActionQueue, for the waiting decisions.
HypothesisService.CompareOptions and SendToTwins, when an options block is
retried or an option is sent for approval.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/briefs/.title: Briefs
docs/user-guide/briefs/.body:
Briefs

Briefs asks your questions for you, on a schedule, and tells the right people what
needs a decision. Each persona gets a weekly brief with one tap, and you can schedule any
question of your own. Open it with Briefs, under Fetch in the rail
(/active_schedules). The page is titled Weekly briefs.
A brief is an ordinary run of FACE, asked at a set time or when your data changes. Its
answer, options and decisions land on Ask,
Options, Why and
Actionable Twins like any other run.

Weekly briefs
The top of the page lists one row per persona of this instance: the product's five
(Field operations manager, CFO, CRO, CMO and CEO) and any your
instance added. Each row shows the question its brief asks and the persona's plays.
Your own persona, set under Settings › Account, is listed
first and marked Yours.

Add brief schedules that persona's brief. It runs every Monday at 07:00 on this
device's clock, and is sent on WhatsApp to the numbers in Settings › Integrations ›
Channels. Once added, the row reads Added · next run {next}, or PAUSED.
Edit opens the persona editor, the same one as
Settings › Personas. Add persona adds a new one.
What you save is shared with everyone on the instance.
Ask FACE as {name} opens the assistant for that persona, with its question first.

Deadline watch is not a persona. It asks every day at 07:00 which claim windows close
in the next 3 days, and what evidence each still needs.
If the instance's personas cannot be read, the page says so and lists the product's five
in the product's own words.
Your briefs
Below the weekly briefs, each brief has a card:

ACTIVE or PAUSED, and EVENT for a brief that runs when data changes;
who it is for (For: {name}), and what it reads, for example Reads: all
connections;
FREQUENCY, NEXT RUN and LAST RUN. A brief that has not run yet says
Never run, not a success or a failure;
how it notifies (Notify: {channels} · {condition}, or Notify: off), and under LAST NOTICE what its last notice did: Sent, Not needed, Not
sent (with the reason), Partly sent or Waiting for the run to finish.

The switch (Turn brief on or off) pauses or resumes a brief. Edit brief
opens it in the editor. Delete brief asks Delete brief? first. Filter
Tasks shows All, Active only or Paused only; a filter nothing matches
says No briefs match this filter. CREATE NEW SCHEDULE opens a blank editor.
With no brief at all, the page says No briefs yet and offers Create brief. A
list that could not be read shows the error, not an empty page.
Create or edit a brief
The editor is titled New brief or Edit brief: A question FACE asks on its own,
for one person, and who hears the answer.

Who it's for
Pick the persona, or Generalist view. Their question fills in below.

What to ask
Type the question in plain words, or pick one under Start from a common question.
The question is also the brief's name.

Where to look
Tick the connections each run reads. With all ticked, it reads every connection,
including ones added later. A brief that reads nothing cannot be saved.

Who hears about it
Pick WhatsApp, Phone call or Email, and when to Tell them: After every
run, When it drafts a Twins decision, When a decision needs approval, or When
$ at stake reaches a threshold with a Minimum $ at stake. Only decisions that state
a dollar figure count toward the threshold.
When a run finishes, FACE tells the numbers in Settings › Integrations › Channels what
needs a decision: the new decisions, the top ones with the money at stake and the
deadline when stated, and a link to Actionable Twins. Email goes out from the mailbox
connected under Settings › Integrations › Channels, to
that same address. With no mailbox connected, the editor says email is off.

When
At a set time runs Every day, Every week or Every month, at the time of
day you save it. When data changes runs on events (see below). Times are on this
device's clock.

Save brief
Next run shows when it will run first. Cost reads Not estimated: FACE does
not forecast what a brief that has never run will use. Select Save brief. Brief
saved. confirms it; Could not save the brief. Nothing was changed. means nothing
was stored.


At a set time, or when data changes 
A brief set to When data changes runs when a connection's
data listener sees the changes you ask for. The
run is the same full run as a timed one.

Listen to: a PostgreSQL connection with the change-event ledger installed, or a
Kafka connection. No other source type has a data listener.
Run after this many events: how many matching events start a run.
Wait for more events (seconds): after the first matching event, wait this long so
a burst of changes becomes one run.
At most one run every (minutes): the cooldown between runs.
Only tables or topics starting with and Only this change narrow what counts.

Saving turns the connection's listener on, on the managed runner. Its events and
listening time are metered to your account. NEXT RUN reads On the next matching
event. A brief never runs while its previous run is still going, and events that
arrive while it is paused are not counted. Pausing or deleting the last active event
brief on a connection turns its listener off.
On an event brief's card, LAST TRIGGER says when it last fired, how many events
fired it, the first of them, how many of their rows were read back, and the run's
outcome. When the run's analysis finishes, RULE RESULTS FROM THESE CHANGES lists each
rule the changed rows bear on, with its verdict. Not fired yet — waiting for events
means no run has started.
Data listeners
When any connection's listener is on, DATA LISTENERS lists it: LISTENING,
STARTING, DEGRADED, NOT LISTENING with the reason, or OFF; the events and
bytes it read; and the account its usage is metered to. Not reported by the runner
yet means the runner has said nothing yet; the page does not guess a state. The page
reads the listeners again every 15 seconds while it is open.
RPCs behind this page

SchedulesService.ListSchedules, CreateSchedule, UpdateSchedule,
SetScheduleActive, DeleteSchedule.
SchedulesService.ListPersonas, SavePersona, DeletePersona, for the personas.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/options/.title: Options
docs/user-guide/options/.body:
Options

Options answers "what could we do, and what is each option worth?" for the
selected run. It compares the options for each
decision the run's checks stand behind, recommends one only when it is a clear winner,
and lists the scenarios FACE tested. Open it with Options, under Simulate in the
rail (/simulate?tab=swarm).
FACE never acts alone. An option you send goes to a named person for approval on
Actionable Twins, and nothing changes until they approve
it.

What could we do
The page opens on What could we do, under For: {alert} when the run raised an
alert on Why. Each decision the run's checks stand behind is a chip;
the one behind Why's alert comes first. See options on Why opens this page on that
decision. Pick a chip to read its options.
If no check on the run stands behind a decision, the page says No check on this run
stands behind a decision yet, so there is nothing to compare.
Read the options
Every option is scored on one measure, stated at the top. For example: Every
option is scored on one measure: the share of the temperature readings read that sit
past a limit their own row states. Each option card shows:

the option, as a lever and a change (for example a temperature excursion moved by
−1 °C), or by name (Air expedite, Internal transfer, Do nothing);
its rank (#{rank}) and its figure with a 95% range;
the evidence it leans on: the effect estimated from the run's rows with its 95% interval, The
baseline: the other options' effects are measured against it., or Effect not
estimated: {reason};
who must approve it: One named person must approve it. or Two different named
people must approve it. An option marked Advice only: approving it records the
decision and runs nothing. changes nothing when approved.

An option whose baseline is missing reads Not measured: needs {needs} and is never
ranked. Not measured is never drawn as zero.
A clear winner, or none
FACE recommends one option only when it is clearly better than the next option and than the figure as measured. The card is then marked Recommended, and the header says
Recommended: {option} with the reason.
Otherwise the header says No clear winner on this data, with why:

The best option's range overlaps the next one's.
The best option's range overlaps the figure as measured, so it is not clearly better
than leaving things as they are.
Fewer than two options could be measured.

A sample that did not read every row says so: A bounded sample: some tables hold more
rows than were read.
Send an option for approval
Select Send for approval on an option. FACE compares the options again on the server
and puts its own figures on the decision, then queues it for a named approver on
Actionable Twins. Not sent: {error} means nothing was queued.
What FACE tested
Under the options, one line counts the scenarios the run tested and how many succeeded,
with See them.
The scenarios are a List by default: how each ended, as an icon and a word, its
title, its business area and what it found. Graph shows the same scenarios as a
flow from what was tested to how it ended. Select a scenario to open its details page
(/lab/scenario/).
If the run recorded no scenario, the page says This run recorded no scenario.
New Simulation
New Simulation builds and runs a scenario of your own. Back to the options returns
you to the page.

Pick a business area and a scenario
Under Scenario categories, pick a business area and one of its scenarios, or
New scenario: name it, pick its business area, then what it tests.

Pick what to test and the news to watch
Under What to test, pick one or more items (New item adds a business measure,
such as spoiled pallets per week). Under Market news to watch, pick the terms a
coming run searches on the web (New term adds your own). Each run searches only a
limited number of terms, and the ones your team added go first.

Set the levers
Under Scenario levers, set the levers for what you picked. Until you pick, each lever
keeps its usual value.

Save or run
Save Scenario saves it without simulating. Run Full Simulation simulates it.


The result shows how confident the simulation is, the effects it reasoned from (Why:
what this draft reasoned from), any anomalies it detected and its forecast. A forecast
needs at least two points; one point is not drawn as a trend.
Send to Actionable Twins hands the result to the approval queue:



You see
Meaning




Queued for Twins
A card was queued. VIEW IN TWINS opens it.


No actions were produced by this run
The server accepted the scenario and named no card, so there is nothing to approve.


The handoff to Twins did not complete
Nothing was queued. The reason is shown.



Found outside your data
When the run searched the web, what it found is shown here, and only here, under
SHADOW CRAWLER TELEMETRY: each finding with its source, Relevance: {relevance}
and the query that found it (Query: {query}).
How FACE knows this
How FACE knows this (How each scenario ended, what went to the twins, and the run
step by step) is folded at the foot of the page. It holds:

how many scenarios ended each way;
the hand-off to the twins: Sent to the twins: {sent} · removed from twins analyses:
{removed}, or why it is not known;
the run's story: what the analysis proposed and simulated, which verdicts went to the
twins, and what the twins do next;
the agents re-running on their own after a rule was validated or a scenario changed
(Running on their own after a rule or scenario change: {agents}).

RPCs behind this page

HypothesisService.CompareOptions, SendToTwins.
HypothesisService.InteractiveSimulate, FetchService.GetScenarioGraph.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/why/.title: Why
docs/user-guide/why/.body:
Why

Why tells you what is happening and what is causing it, for the
selected run. It answers the run's question first,
then shows every check FACE ran on the rows the run read, what your records and public
pages say about each counterparty, the market & diligence analyses, and the business
rules behind it all. Open it with
Why, under Simulate in the rail (/simulate?tab=knowledge).
Every figure on Why is measured on the rows the selected run read. A figure that could
not be measured says so and why. It is never shown as zero.

The answer
The page opens with one sentence that answers the run's question, from the check that
answers it. A stockout question, for example, is answered by the stock checks. The
answer states the money the failing rows put at stake ({amount} at stake), the cause
in plain words, and the worst rows first (Worst first). Two ways on follow: See
options opens Options on that decision, and Act in Actionable
Twins opens the decisions.
When no check answers the question directly, the answer says No check this run
measured answers the question directly. The largest thing needing attention: and names
the thing with the most money on it: a failing check, the deductions open more than 60
days, or the claims whose window closes within 14 days. Nothing on this run needs
attention. means the run measured nothing that needs saying.
The money and the checks
Under the answer is the money line, for the selected run. It is on Why only, not on
Ask. It has seven
tiles:



Tile
What it counts
Opens




At risk
Shipments past their promise, or with a temperature excursion no claim names
Why


Owed to you
Overbilling and duplicate invoices, plus every open claim at its claimed amount
Why


Claim windows closing in 14 days
Of that, what is claimed on open claims whose window closes within 14 days
Why


Waiting for your approval
The run's decisions not yet decided, and the money they state
Actionable Twins


Recovered this quarter
What your team recorded as recovered
Actionable Twins


Shipments at risk
The value of the shipments at risk, with their count
Why


OTIF fines
What the retailers' on-time-in-full terms fine
(does not open a page)



A board tile shows the change since the last successful run, for example ▲ {amount}
since the last run, or Same as the last run. A figure that was not read or not
stated says Not measured with its reason. It is never shown as zero. Decisions that
state no amount are counted apart ({count} state no amount).
The persona picked under Who this run is for on Ask
decides the order (its Reads first, under
Settings › Personas): one that reads what is owed first leads
with Owed to you and Recovered this quarter; one that reads what is at risk first
leads with At risk and Claim windows closing in 14 days. The rest follow in the
order of the table. With the Generalist view, At risk leads. Only the order
changes, never a figure.
After the money line, a line counts the checks,
{total} checks: {failing} failing, {holding} holding, {notMeasured} not measured.
The operations board follows, with four figures measured on the run's rows:



Figure
Detail




On-time delivery
How many of the delivered shipments were on time, and how many are overdue


Open claims
How many close within 14 days, and how many were filed after the window


Invoices over contract
How many of the invoices checked bill above the contract, and by how much


Stock below reorder point
How many positions are below their reorder point, and how many below safety stock



Each figure states its basis, for example over every row read, or Sample figure, not a
total when the run read a sample. Overdue and days left are measured as of the data's
latest row read, not the time of the run.
What FACE checked
What FACE checked lists every check run on the rows the selected run read, each
once: failing checks first, the most money then the most rows. Holding ({count}) and
Not measured ({count}) are folded below them.
A failing check says what does not hold, for example Deliveries late against their
promise, and how many rows: {failing} of {checked} rows checked do not hold, with
the money its rows put at risk when they state any. Open it to see its rows. A check
that held only in a sample says a sample, not a pass.
The checks cover deliveries and promises, claims and their windows, deductions,
invoices against the contract, rate contracts, stock, bills of lading and proofs of
delivery, customs, insurance and cover, and deadlines and signatures. Each check carries
the Twins category it belongs to.
For: narrows the list to an audience: Everyone, Paralegals (bills of lading,
deadlines, signatures and the claim file's documents) or Brokers & underwriters
(customs and cover). A deadline here is an input to a person, not legal advice.
Above the list, anything that blocks a decision is said first: rules that disagree with
what your systems do, rules that could not be read, and values read from the run's
documents that fail a check (Correct them where the run shows what it was given.).
Counterparty reviews
Counterparty reviews covers the carriers, shippers, buyers, sellers, distribution
centres and logistics providers your data names. For each it shows what your own records
say (shipments, claims, invoices over contract) and what public web pages say, with each
red flag citing its page.

No cited red flag in the pages found. That clears no one.
The searches returned no pages. That clears no one.
Public reviews not searched: the run's rows state no name for this party, and FACE
does not search the web by an internal id.

This is not a background check.
Market & diligence
Market & diligence holds three analyses as cards: Run when you ask, over your own
records and public sources; not part of the selected run. An old /market_diligence link opens the matching card here.



Card
What it gives




Customer analysis
Each account's orders, revenue, cost to serve, margin, OTIF, claims and days to pay, from your own records.


Counterparty background check
A business checked by its name or identifiers (for example USDOT number, MC number, LEI (Legal Entity Identifier)) against public registries and sanctions lists, with its history in your records. Possible sanctions matches need human review.


Freight market
Your lanes' rates against their own baseline and the same window last year, beside public diesel and freight index figures.



Closed, each card says where it stands: Not run yet, Running, Could not run,
or what it found. Open one to choose what to analyse, then select Analyse (or Run
check for the counterparty check). Every public source is listed with its state
(live, cached, stale or not checked), and a figure the server did not
send reads not known, never 0. Recommended actions (drafts for a person to
decide) go to Actionable Twins with Send for
approval, where a named person approves or rejects them.
What this run was given
What this run was given opens the run's own page, where the files and captures
attached to it are listed with how each was read. See
Open a past run.
How FACE knows this
How FACE knows this (The rows behind each figure, the rules FACE read and their
policies) is folded at the foot of the page. It holds:

The rows behind the figures: the board's views over the rows it read, per carrier,
claim, invoice and stock position;
the rules FACE read from your systems, counted apart from the checks: RULES HOLDING
IN THE DATA and RULES BROKEN;
Rules your operations run on, described below.

Rules your operations run on 
Rules your operations run on (Your business rules, checked against what your
systems actually do and against the policy documents you add) lists the business rules
FACE found and the ones you added. All domains ({count}) and the domain pills narrow
the list. These are your business's rules, not FACE's own guard rules, which are on
Admin.
Every rule carries one verdict, each with its own glyph and word, so it never depends on
colour alone:



Verdict
Meaning




Aligned
Aligned with policy.


Drift
Drifted: needs reconciliation.


Shadow
Undocumented.


Missing
Missing: needs reconciliation.


Unrated
No verdict was returned yet.



Set a rule's enforcement

Open the policy editor
Select the tune button on a rule (Open the policy editor). The Enforcement
policy drawer opens below it.

Decide the enforcement
Choose an Enforcement action: Audit only, Review required or Block.
Optionally fill in Tolerance (in the rule's own units), Policy reference (the
clause you cite) and Rationale (why, for the reviewer).

Save policy
Save policy stays disabled until you choose an action. The drawer records who set it
and when. The policy was not saved keeps your entries so you can try again.
Discard drops your changes.


Saving a rule's enforcement validates it. A validated rule goes to the simulations on
Options by itself, and the twins are re-run for your instance. Include this rule in
Simulate takes a rule in or out of that selection.
The drawer also holds the Reconcile inspector: a read-only comparison of Actual —
implementation against Intended — policy. Nothing to compare yet means FACE
captured neither for the rule.
In an open rule's drawer, Edit & recheck opens the rule (Rule Name, Logic
(Plain English), then Save Rule), and Ignore sets it aside. Unsaved marks a
rule you edited or added here until you save a policy on it. Under the list, Create New
Business Rule… adds a rule in plain English.
RPCs behind this page

FetchService.GetOperationsBoard, for the money, the board and the checks.
RulesService.AnalyzeCode, UpdateRulePolicy.
PostureService.GetHealthScore.
MarketDiligenceService.AnalyzeCustomers, CheckCounterparty, AnalyzeFreightMarket,
QueueRecommendedAction, for the market & diligence cards.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/live-sensing/.title: Live sensing and vision
docs/user-guide/live-sensing/.body:
Live sensing and vision

Cameras, sensors, field readers and devices are connection types: an admin connects
them under Data sources, and each one's card on the
Ask page (How FACE knows this › Connections) opens its live view with that
connection already chosen. See Ask.



View
What you see
Status




Live sensors
What the always-on sensor connections are hearing, the candidate findings their detectors raised and, for admins, the health of the ingest path.
Built; needs a sensor connection.


Field reader
A live view of a handheld field reader carried around a yard, a dock or a cold store.
Built; needs a field-reader connection.


Surveillance
Camera feeds graded frame by frame (Threat Detected or No Threat Detected), sensor cueing and the event feed. Photos taken with Camera Input on Ask are listed under Captured media.
Built; needs a camera connection.


Devices
The devices a device connection reported.
Built; needs a device connection.


Store interest
For a shop floor: visitors per zone and hour as a heatmap, and layout suggestions a person approves.
Built; off until an admin enables it per camera and records the privacy checklist.


Receipt reading
Text and fields read off a photographed paper receipt on Ask.
Built; see Ask.



What these views show

A reading with no stated value shows the fault, not a number.
An empty list says why it is empty.

Store interest is aggregate only
Store interest shows aggregate counts only and never identifies anyone. An admin turns it on camera by
camera, draws the zones and records a privacy impact checklist; its suggestions become
cards a named person approves on Actionable Twins.
How frames are graded and located is in Vision & CCTV.

docs/user-guide/actionable-twins/.title: Actionable Twins
docs/user-guide/actionable-twins/.body:
Actionable Twins

Actionable Twins is where you decide. It lists every decision the twins drafted for
the selected run, in three lanes: what waits for you,
what is on its way, and what came back. You approve or reject each one, follow it up,
and see the same decisions where they sit on the map. Open it with Actionable Twins,
under Twins in the rail (/today_command).
FACE never acts alone. A decision stays waiting until a named person approves or
rejects it, and FACE recommends an option only when it is a clear winner (see
Options). The one exception is a
standing rule that two different admins approved, and it
covers only later cards with exactly the same conditions.

List or Map
The toggle at the top switches between List (/today_command) and Map
(/twins/map), the same decisions on the map. On the list, Collapse all draws every
card as one row and Expand all opens them all. Open card and Minimize card
change one card.
The lanes



Lane
Holds




Waiting for you
Decisions that still need a person.


In flight
Decisions approved, with no final outcome recorded yet.


Back
Decisions with an outcome recorded: recovered, partly recovered or denied.



Each lane heading shows how many items it holds and the money their cards state.
Cards that state no amount are counted apart ({count} state no amount), never
added as zero. An empty lane says why, for example Nothing waits for your decision on
this run.
Inside a lane, decisions are grouped by category, with a count such as {count}
actions · {waiting} waiting for you. Decisions whose documents state a deadline come
first, soonest first. Decisions already decided are marked DECIDED.
Filter the decisions

The play chips filter by play, in this order: Claims recovery, Disruptions,
Routes, Fulfilment, then Cold chain, Maintenance, Inventory and
Fleet. Once the twins have finished, each chip shows its count, for example
{play} · {count}.
Deadlines in the next 30 days keeps only decisions due in that window.
All bands, Medium and up and High only filter fraud and leakage indicators
by likelihood.

While a filter is on, a notice titled Filtered to {filter} says so. Show all
clears every filter.
The toolbar above the chips holds:

Options for this run, which opens Options;
Analyze document, which sends a csv, txt, tsv or json file of up to 3 MB
to the twins and reads the list again when it is done;
Draft next steps automatically, with Recovery leakage or Fraud indicators:
an agent drafts steps for a person to approve (Drafted for a person to approve.
Nothing has been filed, sent, paid or held.);
Refresh. While a run is still working, Updating with the latest results… shows,
and the list reads itself again until the run ends.

Read a decision
A card's row shows its title and the money it states, for example {amount} at
risk, {amount} revenue at risk or {amount} drafted order, or not measured:
{reason}. Open the card to read:

the twin's reason, its priority and the run that produced it;
its items, as on an order: route stops, missing documents, recommended vendors. An
amount is printed only when the card states one;
Next:, the stage it waits on, for example Next: Approval — waiting for your
decision;
its pipeline, one step per stage, each done, now, stopped, not yet or
not recorded;
Open the evidence, which opens the decision artifact;
Show on the map, on a decision about a vehicle, a route or an asset;
Why, the figures behind it: what the twin stated, the cited records and the
measured figures, or No measured figures were recorded for this action.

The pipeline stages
Every stage is drawn from what FACE records. A stage FACE keeps no record of says not
recorded.



Decision
Stages




Claim or dispute
Detected → Evidence gathered → Dispute drafted → Approval → Sent → Response → Resolved


Sourcing or fulfilment
Shortfall found → Order drafted → Approval → Placed → Confirmed


Any other decision
Approval, then what the approval carried out



What FACE does not record today:

Placed and Confirmed: FACE places no ERP order. An approval records not
placed: {reason}.
A route approval records the new order. Nothing is sent to a vehicle or a TMS.
Sent is done only when the decision log records that the message went out, and
stopped with not sent: {reason} when it did not.

Approve a decision

Open the card and read what approving does
WHAT APPROVING DOES says what this approval will and will not do. Read the drafts:
the email, the calendar invite, the ERP change.

Select Approve
Your decision is sent at once (Sending your decision…) and the card moves to
In flight. If the server cannot be reached, Decision not delivered yet: {reason} ·
retrying shows, and the app keeps trying. Nothing is recorded until the server
confirms.

Read the outcome
A decision that needs two approvers shows 1 of 2 approvals recorded after the first.
When the server records an approval but part of it could not run, Recorded, but not
executed lists each part with its reason.


When the claims play is selected and more than one claim is ready, Approve all
{count} ready claims · {amount} asks first, then approves each claim one after
another, through the same approval as a single one, under your name.
FACE has no way to edit a draft before it goes out. To change one, reject it with your
reason.
Reject a decision
Every rejection needs a reason: it is the only record of why.

Select Reject
The dialog Why are you rejecting this? opens, naming the decision (Rejecting:
{title}).

Write your reason
Type it in Your reason. An empty reason is refused, and so is one too long to keep
word for word (Room for about {count} more characters.).

Select Reject with this reason
The decision's later stages are marked stopped, and the rejection is kept in its
decision record. Cancel leaves it where it was.


A fraud or leakage indicator is dismissed the same way: Why are you dismissing this
indicator?, then Dismiss with this reason.
Record what happened next
On a claim you approved, Record what happened next records its outcome: Filed,
Awaiting reply, Recovered, Partially recovered or Denied. A recovery
asks for Amount recovered (USD), recorded as you entered it. Nothing is billed on
it. A denial asks why. The claim then moves to Back.
Make this a standing rule
On an approved card, Make this a standing rule proposes that later cards with
exactly the same conditions (its kind, category, the actions approving does, the
counterparty and an amount ceiling) get the tier you choose: Guarded — one named
approver or Autonomous — runs with no approver. Give a reason under Why (shown
to the approver) and select Propose.
The proposal changes nothing on its own: Standing rule {id} is waiting for a second
admin's approval. It is not in effect. It takes effect only when a second, different
admin approves the exact text on Admin, and any
admin can revoke it there.
Follow-ups
A follow-up is a flow that chases the items on FACE's boards (work orders, claims,
deductions) by calling or messaging the people responsible, on rules you approve.
Run a follow-up on selected cards
Select cards on the list, or on the map (Select its card for follow-ups). The
selection bar shows {count} selected, with Follow-up and Clear. Follow-up
opens a sheet: Pick a follow-up. FACE first tries it on each item and sends nothing;
you then choose to run it. After the dry run, Run on {count} items runs it.
The Follow-ups page
Follow-ups (/twins/followups) opens from the sheet. It is not a rail entry: it
lights Actionable Twins. Calls and messages that chase your work orders, claims and
deductions, on rules you approve.

With no follow-up yet, Start with a ready-made follow-up offers starters, for
example When a claim's window closes in 3 days, message the carrier. Use this
opens one as a draft. Nothing runs until you arm it.
Each follow-up is built from steps: When (what starts it), Reach people (a
voice call, WhatsApp or SMS, or telling the addressee), Work orders (mark an order
Draft or Sent; approving or rejecting stays a person's decision) and Timing
and checks (wait, or check before going on).
A follow-up is Not armed until you arm it, and runs only as a dry run until then
(Runs only as a dry run until you arm it.). Once Armed, it Runs by itself
when its trigger fires.
The assistant on the page drafts changes as pending steps; a person approves them.
Tasks lists the open follow-up tasks with their due time.

While no carrier is connected, the page says Calls and messages can't go out until
your carrier is connected., with Connect a carrier, and steps that need one show
Needs a carrier.
Map view
The Map view (/twins/map) draws the selected run's sites, vehicles and routes
where your data places them, with their decisions on them. FACE geocodes nothing: a
thing is placed only where its source states a position.

The banner says what is on the map from your data: On the map from your data:
{sites} places, {vehicles} vehicles, {routes} routes. It also says which run the map
shows, and when vehicle positions come from earlier runs or are live positions rather
than this run's.
What the map draws

Placed assets: sites and vehicles at their stated position. Vehicles come from a
connection tagged telemetry, equipment or shipments; the banner names them, or says
No connection is tagged telemetry, equipment or shipments yet.
Route proposals: The line joins this card's stated positions in the proposed
order. It is not a road. A route waiting for the route judge's verdict cannot be
approved yet.
Reefers: minutes out of band: cold-chain pins, with value at risk only when the card
states it.
Money at stake, Cold-chain excursions and Detention & dwell: money layers,
each with its total and what it could not place.
Fleet plan (live): planned stops from the vehicles' current GPS positions and
pending shipments, not from the selected run.
Live layers from each active connection that reports positions, and the providers
FACE found near sites in trouble (Providers found), each with what the option
costs against doing nothing.

Layers lists every layer with a switch, how many features it has on the map
({count} on the map), the attribution its source requires, and how old its data is
(Old data · newest {time}). Fit to sites frames every site, route and provider.
Not on the map lists what your data names but the map cannot place, each with its
reason: No location in the data, or Address only — waiting for the FACE
geocoder.
The basemap is FACE's own, served by your FACE instance. No third-party map, tile or
geocoding service is called.
Select a place
Tap a site, a vehicle or a route, and its card opens beside it. With a keyboard, open
On the map and choose an entry. Esc, the close button or a tap on the map closes
the card. Show on the map on a list card opens the map on that card.

A site card tells its story first, for example how its demand moved in this run,
then Outbound demand, Inventory safety nets, Cold chain, Policies,
Verified shippers and Suppliers, each with its Basis.
supplier or shipper here. Open the entity page opens the site's own page.
A vehicle card shows Predictive maintenance and Cold chain for this run,
then its pending decisions with Approve and Reject.
A route card shows its mode, its temperature band, the Re-plan (kilometres in
the current order against the proposed order) and what triggered it.

A figure the run does not contain says not measured, and why.
Site plans 
Site plans opens a side panel over the map with the plans FACE inferred from your
BIM/CAD files: each plan's levels, its elements (zones, docks, yard slots) and the twin
entity each element is bound to. Open it from a place's card, from a plan's footprint on
the map, or from Layers.

Plans come from IFC or DXF files. DWG is a proprietary format and is not read:
export DXF or IFC from your CAD tool.
PDFs and pictures are read by the vision model, and what it finds is labelled
proposed by the model until you confirm it.
Select an element to see its twin (This element is the twin {entityClass} {id}.),
or This element is not in the twin. Only a confirmed zone, dock or yard slot is
written. Open in the twin opens the entity.
3D model shows the open plan in the map's low-poly style: zones and yard slots as
coloured floor areas, walls, columns and racks as tall as the file states, and docks
and doors as pins. Overview, From above and Low angle reset the camera,
Full screen opens the model on its own, and a tap selects the element on the page.
An element whose height the file doesn't state is drawn flat, one with no outline or
position isn't drawn, and the model counts both. A plan in pixels, or in units its
file doesn't state, has no 3D model.

Twin entities 
Twin entities is a side panel over the map (/twins/map?panel=entities): every
entity FACE discovered from your sources (sites, docks, assets, devices), each with where
it came from. Open it from Layers.
All classes filters by class, Search id or values searches, Load more reads
the next page and New entity adds one by hand. Select an entity to open its page.
An empty twin says so; Could not read the twin means the request failed.
Decision artifacts
A decision artifact is the full record of one decision, with the drafts it would produce.
Open the evidence on a card opens it, marked PENDING before approval. The page
shows DECISION ARTIFACT #{id}, the title, the decision trail and the GENERATED
DRAFTS. A link that carries no decision shows No decision artifact.
Remediation
Remediation: Compliance, Finance and Operations, above the lanes, open
the remediation screen for that twin. Each shows the verdict, the server's statement of
which data it rests on, VIOLATIONS ({count}) or FINDINGS ({count}) with each
item's remediation and rule, and the AUDIT TRAIL. Unable to Assess is not a
verdict: nothing could be assessed, and the summary says why.
Findings can become work orders. Remediation orders lists them; FACE sends no order
anywhere: approving records a decision, and a person sends the order and marks it sent.
On the compliance screen, Routing table holds your own map from finding category to
department. FACE holds no org chart and proposes no route. Enter a DEPARTMENT, a
CONTACT or both, then Save rule. A rule applies to future orders only.
When the list is empty



You see
Meaning




The twins are working…
The run is still working.


The twins finished and proposed nothing
The run's data led to no decision that needs a person.


Digital twin reasoning…
The decisions are loading.


Failed to fetch action queue: {error}
The decisions could not be read. This is not an empty run.



RPCs behind this page

TwinsService.GetActionQueue, ExecuteAction, ListDecisionLog, ProposeStandingRule, UploadAnalyze
(server stream).
MapFeatureService.ListMapLayers, StreamMapFeatures (server stream).
TwinGraphService.GetTwinSiteDetails, for a site's card.
ComplianceService.AnalyzeCompliance, AssignRemediation, DecideRemediation.
runink.ui.siteplan.v1.SitePlanService, for the site plans.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/fleet-and-control/.title: Routes and fleet
docs/user-guide/fleet-and-control/.body:
Routes, fleet and the twin map

FACE places each asset where your fetched data says it is, proposes route changes, and
drafts orders for connected equipment. Everything here waits for a named person's
approval.
The map
Actionable Twins › Map shows each asset at the position its data states, with its
pending decisions, site plans and twin entities. Route proposals and vehicle cards open
over the map. See Actionable Twins › Map view. Routes
are computed by FACE itself; no outside map or routing service is called.
Orders for connected components
For a connected component (a robot, a drone, an automated mobile robot or a conveyor),
FACE can draft an order to be issued over that component's own control interface. The
card shows, before you decide:

the order in words, the component and the endpoint it targets;
the exact command it would send, as a dry run;
the evidence the order rests on.

The card sends nothing by itself. Approval is a separate, deliberate act, and some
control actions also need a one-time confirmation code. Nothing is issued to a
component that is not connected and approved by an admin.
Status: built and approval-gated; it needs a connected component and has not been
used with a customer.
Supplier tiers and the supplier portal
Supplier tiers show who supplies whom. Approved supplier contacts can sign in to a
supplier portal that lists only the orders addressed to their own party; every change a
supplier makes (a confirmation, a new date or quantity, a document) arrives as a
proposal a named person approves. See Access and the trial.
Status: built; supplier sign-in needs Runink to approve each supplier contact.

docs/user-guide/contacts-and-verificatio.title: Contacts and verification
docs/user-guide/contacts-and-verificatio.body:
Contacts and verification

Contacts
Settings › Integrations › Contacts lists who FACE's agents may message or call: one
row per contact and channel, with whether that channel can reach them. Contacts can be
imported from a connected system (CRM, ERP, TMS and others); imported contacts are
read-only and are updated, not duplicated, when you import again. A banner names each
channel contacts may use but nobody has set up. See Settings.
Send an answer to contacts
On Ask, the send button opens the same contact list. Tick one or more
contacts, pick the channel each may receive (WhatsApp or SMS), read the exact message
FACE will send, then select Send now. Nothing goes out before that.
Verifying counterparties
Before you deal with a carrier, supplier or customer, FACE's due-diligence agents check
it against public registries and market data, using only the identifiers a person
typed, never your records. Each result names every source, its publisher, licence and
retrieval time. These checks appear as cards on Why.

Counterparty background check
Customer analysis
Freight market analyst

Admins set the public names and thresholds these agents use on the
Admin page.

docs/user-guide/voice-and-calls/.title: Voice and calls
docs/user-guide/voice-and-calls/.body:
Voice and calls

FACE can speak with people on your behalf: follow-ups to the people responsible for an
item, requests for quotation to carriers and suppliers, and voice dispatch. Every call
uses a phone line Runink configures for your organisation.

The caller is told it is an AI. Every call opens with "This is an automated AI
assistant from" your company's name, before anything else,.
This is in the product; it has not yet been heard on a customer's call.
Calls follow rules you approve. A follow-up calls or messages people only on the
rules you approved, and runs by itself only once armed. See
Actionable Twins › Follow-ups.
Calls are recorded as transcripts in your organisation's sealed storage.
Drafts carry your company name. Letters and quotation requests FACE drafts are
signed with your company name.

You can also dictate a question on Ask with the microphone.
Status: built; not switched on for any customer. Telephony is carried by Twilio and
exists only when a voice line is configured.
The voice dispatch agent is described in its model card.

docs/user-guide/settings/.title: Settings
docs/user-guide/settings/.body:
Settings

Settings is where you set up who you are, who your briefs are for, what FACE connects
to, and your plan. Open it with Settings at the foot of the rail (/settings). It
has five tabs: Account, Personas,
Integrations, Subscription and
Chat history. The address
names the tab (/settings?tab=account, personas, integrations or subscription), so
a link or a bookmark opens the right one.
Account
Account (/settings?tab=account) is about you: who is signed in, your preferences,
your sessions and your data.

Admin
If you are an admin of the selected instance, an Admin card comes first. It opens
Admin. Nobody else sees it.
Who you are
The identity card lists your Email, Name, Signed in with, Role,
Platform admin, Tenant and Account ID. A value the server did not provide
reads Not provided. Signed in with is Google account, Password or an API
key.
Preferences

Theme: Light, Dark or System. This device remembers your choice.
Interface language: the language of the app's screens.
Agent language: The agent listens to voice commands and reads its answers aloud
in the agent language. It is also the language FACE writes its answers in.
Your role: the persona you are. Your brief is listed first on Briefs. Not set
changes nothing. The order of Why's money line follows the persona picked on Ask
(Who this run is for), not this setting.
Offline answers says whether this device can answer offline, and why not.

Security

Sign out ends this session.
Sign out everywhere ends every session of yours on every device, this one
included. Confirm with Yes, sign out everywhere.

Your data
It stays on your instance. No exit fees, no lock-in. Delete my account deletes your
own account for real, after you type your email address: the dialog lists what is deleted
and what your organisation keeps, and says that the access list is not edited, so a
still-listed address that signs in again gets a new, empty account. If you are the last
admin it refuses; if the server cannot be reached it says your account was not deleted. See
Delete your account. A copy of your data is
asked for from the privacy contact (a link in that dialog). Open-source licences lists
the licences of the software the app includes.
Personas
Personas (/settings?tab=personas) holds who a brief is for: Who a brief is for: a
name, the question its brief asks, and the money figure it reads first. What you save
here is shared with everyone on the instance.
Every persona of the instance is a profile: the product's five, in your instance's words
if someone reworded one, then the ones your instance added. Each shows:

what it Reads first: Owed, At risk or the money line's own order (Line
order);
Responsible for, Asks (the question its brief asks) and Plays (None
picked: this persona answers for every play.);
Briefs: how many it has and the next run, or No brief yet;
Next step: Add a brief for {name} or See the briefs for {name}.

Edit and Add persona open the persona editor, the same one as on
Briefs. Save with Save for everyone. An added
persona can be deleted (Delete for everyone), and a reworded product persona can be
reset (Put back the product's words).
Integrations
Integrations (/settings?tab=integrations) has four sections: Channels,
Systems, Contacts and Runners. The address names the section with
&section= (channels, data-sources, contacts or runners).
Channels
Channels holds how FACE reaches people: each channel's status (voice, SMS and
WhatsApp), the sender numbers, the carrier's write-only secrets and the delivery trail.
Everyone with a role on the instance can read it; only an admin can change it.
KEYS & NUMBERS holds the WhatsApp Phone Number, Phone Number, SMS Phone
Number, Stripe API Key, Google Credentials (Gmail, Drive) and Google
Analytics ID. A secret shows only Configured (hidden) or Not Set. To change it,
enter a new value: Enter a new value to replace it. The stored value is never shown.
EMAIL FOR BRIEFS is the mailbox your briefs are emailed from. Briefs by email leave
from your own mailbox and go to its own address; FACE has no shared sender. Connect it
with Connect Gmail or Connect Microsoft 365 when your instance has those
sign-ins set up, or as an SMTP mailbox with Test and connect: FACE logs in to
test it and keeps it only if that works. The card shows the address, the provider and
whether it can send now.
Systems
Systems is the list of your data sources. Each row shows the connection's name,
type and id, where it runs (Runink managed or runs on {runner}), its credential
chip (for example credential stored) and its last test. A stored credential is
never shown; the chip says only that one is held.
The row buttons are Edit, Rotate credentials, Test, Listener and
Delete. Test opens the source with its stored credential on the connection's
runner, read-only and time-limited, and reads nothing from it. Delete asks first,
because it also deletes the credential bundle. A files connection also offers Index
documents.

Add a connection
New connection opens the wizard: Pick a source, fill in its details, choose a
runner, then test and save. Its steps are Source, Details, Credentials,
Runner and Review.

Source. Pick a source card from the catalog, or search by product or by system.
Details. Name the connection and fill in its settings. For a database, choose
the Encryption in transit. Every choice encrypts, and there is no plaintext
option: Encrypt. Do not verify the certificate., Encrypt and verify the
certificate chain. or, the strictest, Encrypt, verify the chain and the
hostname.
Credentials. A credential field is write-only: once saved it is never shown
again.
Runner. Choose where the source is read from. Runink managed runs inside the
server. Every test and read of the connection runs on the runner you pick, or is
refused.
Review. Check every value, then select Test & save. A passing test means the
source answered; it does not mean data has been read.


A connection proposed by a run opens the same wizard from Confirm, on the proposal's
source card with its name filled in. You still enter every address and credential.
For each connector's settings, see Data sources.
Contacts
Contacts lists who the agent may message or call, one row per contact and channel,
with whether that channel can reach them. A banner names each channel contacts may use
but nobody set up, with a button to set it up.
Import from a system (Import contacts) reads contacts from your connected
systems (CRM, ERP, TMS and others). Imported contacts are read-only here: change them at
the source and import again, and they are updated, not duplicated.
Runners
Runners lists where reads of your data sources run: the managed runner (Runink
managed, part of the server, the default for every connection) and runners on your own
network that the server connects to. Add runner registers a self-hosted runner and
gives its one-time setup ticket. Each runner shows its state (active, pending or
revoked), its health and how many reads it has in flight.
Subscription
Subscription (/settings?tab=subscription) shows your organisation's plan as
Runink recorded it: the plan, its status and the seats. FACE takes no payment itself.
During the trial the workspace is fully usable for 14 days, then read-only until a plan
is bought; see Access and the trial. Plans and
prices are on runink.org.
No subscription is on record for this account. means the record was read and is
empty. The subscription record could not be read. This does not mean there is no
subscription. means the request failed.
Chat history
The assistant starts empty in each new session. Chat history lists every chat you
had with it, newest first, grouped by persona (No persona last). Open one to read
its transcript; Continue makes it the assistant's conversation again and opens the
panel. Chats are stored sealed in your organisation's storage. A history that could not
be read says so and offers a retry.
RPCs behind this page

runink.ui.profile.v1.ProfileService: GetProfile, EndAllSessions.
ConfigService.GetIntegrationConfig, SetIntegrationConfig.
runink.ui.datasources.v1.ConnectionsService and RunnersService.
runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService: GetOverview, ListPlans, QuotePlan.

See the API reference.

docs/user-guide/account-deletion/.title: Delete your account
docs/user-guide/account-deletion/.body:
Delete your account

You can delete your own FACE account from inside the app. This page says where, what is
deleted, what your organisation keeps, and how to ask for deletion if you can no longer use
the app.
In the app

Open Settings (the foot of the rail), then the Account tab.
In the Your data card, choose Delete my account.
Read what is deleted and what is kept, then type your own email address in the field. The
red Delete my account permanently button stays disabled until the text is your
address.
Choose Delete my account permanently. FACE deletes the account on the server first.
Only when the server confirms does the app sign you out and clear the data it holds on
your device. If the server cannot be reached, or refuses, the dialog says so and your
account is not deleted.

The deletion is always of the account you are signed in with. The server takes it from your
verified session, never from what the request says, and checks the address you typed
against that session again.
The only admin cannot delete the account. If you are the last organisation admin of the
instance, FACE refuses and says so: make another member an admin first, then delete. The
instance's break-glass administrator account cannot be deleted from the app.
What is deleted

your sign-in account: email address, password hash, two-factor secret and role;
every session of yours, on every device, which end at once;
