The whole universe is universe.json. manifest.json lists every download with its size and SHA-256, and SHA256SUMS is the same list for sha256sum -c.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/quickstart.title: Apache Kafka, live estate
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/quickstart.body:
Apache Kafka, live estate


Warning: The test-estate safety rule: stand the test estate up only beside a test instance, never a production deployment. The broker below is encrypted and every client logs in, but its certificate authority, keys and passwords are generated on your machine for this test only. Use a scratch machine.

Streaming · type kafka · a broker on your machine, fed without end
What it is
A Kafka broker on your own machine that never stops receiving events, so you can watch FACE take in a stream rather than a recording. A producer generates the quickstart estate's operations: trucks moving between the sites, dock doors, cold rooms, forklifts, meters, drone surveys, yard gates, and the mainframe's order and inventory changes.
The events are about the same Quillmere estate as every other quickstart: the same warehouses, yards, docks, trailers, carriers, customers and items, with the same IDs. The values are authored for the quickstart, not measured. Every record says so in its provenance field: authored quickstart estate.
The broker setup follows Confluent's Kafka on Docker tutorial: one Apache Kafka node in KRaft mode, no ZooKeeper. A Schema Registry is added, because the values are Avro. For the recorded topics and the ksqlDB catalogue, see Apache Kafka. The connector reference is Streaming: Kafka.
FACE connects to Kafka only over SASL_SSL. The broker below speaks TLS with a certificate from a certificate authority you generate, and every client logs in with SCRAM-SHA-512. The Schema Registry answers HTTPS only, from the same authority, and every call logs in with its own user and password. FACE refuses a Kafka connection without encryption or without a login, and a registry over plain http:// or without its login.
What you need

Docker with Compose, and openssl.
The producer image, face-stream-producer:1.4.0.


Note: The producer image is not on a public registry yet. Without it, steps 1 to 3 still give you a running broker and Schema Registry, but no events.

1. Generate the keys and passwords
In an empty directory, save this as setup.sh and run it once (sh setup.sh). It writes the passwords to .env, which Compose reads, and the certificate authority, the broker's and the registry's certificates and the client files to secrets/. The authority's private key is deleted as soon as it has signed, so nothing else can be signed with it.
#!/bin/sh
# The name FACE uses to reach this machine. Keep localhost when FACE runs here.
KAFKA_HOST=${KAFKA_HOST:-localhost}
set -eu
umask 077
mkdir -p secrets
pw() { openssl rand -hex 20; }
cat > .env  "secrets/$1.ext"
  openssl x509 -req -in "secrets/$1.csr" -CA secrets/ca.crt -CAkey secrets/ca.key -CAcreateserial \
    -days 365 -sha256 -extfile "secrets/$1.ext" -out "secrets/$1.crt"
}
leaf broker "DNS:broker,DNS:$KAFKA_HOST"
leaf schema-registry "DNS:schema-registry,DNS:$KAFKA_HOST"
cat secrets/broker.key secrets/broker.crt > secrets/broker-keystore.pem
rm -f secrets/ca.key secrets/ca.srl secrets/*.csr secrets/*.ext

# The producer reads its passwords from files, never from a flag.
printf %s "$SCRAM_PRODUCER" > secrets/producer-sasl-password
printf %s "$REGISTRY_PRODUCER" > secrets/producer-registry-password
# The console tools in step 2 log in as face-reader.
cat > secrets/face-reader.properties 
If FACE runs on another machine, set the name it reaches this one by first, for example KAFKA_HOST=kafka-host.example.invalid sh setup.sh. The certificates then carry that name and the broker advertises it.
2. Start the broker, the registry and the producer
Save this as compose.yaml in the same directory:
x-kafka-image: &kafka-image apache/kafka:4.2.2
x-karapace-image: &karapace-image ghcr.io/aiven-open/karapace:6.2.4

services:
  # Formats the broker's storage WITH its SCRAM users, once, before it starts.
  format:
    image: *kafka-image
    user: "1000:1000"
    volumes: [kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data]
    entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        cat > /tmp/format.properties  /dev/null

  broker:
    image: *kafka-image
    hostname: broker
    container_name: broker
    depends_on:
      format: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
    ports:
      - "9092:9092"
    volumes:
      - kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data
      - ./secrets:/etc/kafka/tls:ro
    environment:
      CLUSTER_ID: rtWtPypOQIeDOIHE0I7Rtg
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
      # Containers use broker:29092; FACE uses ${KAFKA_HOST}:9092. Both are
      # SASL_SSL. The controller listens on the container's loopback only.
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: INTERNAL://broker:29092,EXTERNAL://0.0.0.0:9092,CONTROLLER://localhost:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: INTERNAL://broker:29092,EXTERNAL://${KAFKA_HOST}:9092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: INTERNAL:SASL_SSL,EXTERNAL:SASL_SSL,CONTROLLER:SASL_PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: INTERNAL
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@localhost:9093
      KAFKA_SASL_ENABLED_MECHANISMS: SCRAM-SHA-512
      KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM_INTER_BROKER_PROTOCOL: SCRAM-SHA-512
      KAFKA_LISTENER_NAME_INTERNAL_SCRAM___SHA___512_SASL_JAAS_CONFIG: org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required username="broker" password="${SCRAM_BROKER}";
      KAFKA_LISTENER_NAME_EXTERNAL_SCRAM___SHA___512_SASL_JAAS_CONFIG: org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required;
      KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM_CONTROLLER_PROTOCOL: PLAIN
      KAFKA_LISTENER_NAME_CONTROLLER_SASL_ENABLED_MECHANISMS: PLAIN
      KAFKA_LISTENER_NAME_CONTROLLER_PLAIN_SASL_JAAS_CONFIG: org.apache.kafka.common.security.plain.PlainLoginModule required username="broker" password="${SCRAM_BROKER}" user_broker="${SCRAM_BROKER}";
      KAFKA_SSL_KEYSTORE_TYPE: PEM
      KAFKA_SSL_KEYSTORE_LOCATION: /etc/kafka/tls/broker-keystore.pem
      KAFKA_SSL_TRUSTSTORE_TYPE: PEM
      KAFKA_SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION: /etc/kafka/tls/ca.crt
      KAFKA_SSL_ENABLED_PROTOCOLS: TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS: 0
      KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"

  # Writes the registry's login file: salted hashes, made by Karapace's own tool.
  registry-auth:
    image: *karapace-image
    volumes: [registry-auth:/auth]
    entrypoint: ["sh", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        r=$$(karapace_mkpasswd -u face-reader -a sha512 '${REGISTRY_FACE_READER}')
        p=$$(karapace_mkpasswd -u producer -a sha512 '${REGISTRY_PRODUCER}')
        printf '{"users": [%s, %s], "permissions": [{"username": "face-reader", "operation": "Read", "resource": "Subject:quillmere\\\\..*"}, {"username": "producer", "operation": "Write", "resource": "Subject:quillmere\\\\..*"}]}\n' "$$r" "$$p" > /auth/auth.json

  schema-registry:
    # Karapace answers the Confluent Schema Registry API.
    image: *karapace-image
    entrypoint: ["python3", "-m", "karapace"]
    depends_on:
      broker: {condition: service_started}
      registry-auth: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
    ports:
      - "8081:8081"
    volumes:
      - ./secrets:/etc/kafka/tls:ro
      - registry-auth:/auth:ro
    environment:
      KARAPACE_KARAPACE_REGISTRY: "true"
      KARAPACE_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      KARAPACE_PORT: 8081
      KARAPACE_ADVERTISED_HOSTNAME: schema-registry
      # HTTPS only, and every call logs in.
      KARAPACE_SERVER_TLS_CERTFILE: /etc/kafka/tls/schema-registry.crt
      KARAPACE_SERVER_TLS_KEYFILE: /etc/kafka/tls/schema-registry.key
      KARAPACE_REGISTRY_AUTHFILE: /auth/auth.json
      # Its own broker connection: SASL_SSL as schema-registry.
      KARAPACE_BOOTSTRAP_URI: broker:29092
      KARAPACE_SECURITY_PROTOCOL: SASL_SSL
      KARAPACE_SASL_MECHANISM: SCRAM-SHA-512
      KARAPACE_SASL_PLAIN_USERNAME: schema-registry
      KARAPACE_SASL_PLAIN_PASSWORD: ${SCRAM_SCHEMA_REGISTRY}
      KARAPACE_SSL_CAFILE: /etc/kafka/tls/ca.crt
      KARAPACE_TOPIC_NAME: _schemas
      KARAPACE_LOG_LEVEL: WARNING

  producer:
    image: face-stream-producer:1.4.0
    depends_on: [broker, schema-registry]
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./secrets:/run/quickstart:ro
    command:
      - produce
      - kafka
      - --bootstrap=broker:29092
      - --security-protocol=sasl_ssl
      - --sasl-mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
      - --sasl-username=producer
      - --sasl-password-file=/run/quickstart/producer-sasl-password
      - --tls-ca-file=/run/quickstart/ca.crt
      - --registry=https://schema-registry:8081
      - --registry-username=producer
      - --registry-password-file=/run/quickstart/producer-registry-password

volumes:
  kafka-data:
  registry-auth:

Start everything:
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f producer

The producer creates its topics, registers their schemas, lists the anomalies it plants, and then sends about 10 events a second. It retries until the broker and the registry answer, so the start order does not matter. Nothing on the network is unencrypted: the broker's controller listener is on its own loopback, and every other port is TLS with a login.
3. List the topics and read a few records
Log in as face-reader, the user FACE will use:
docker exec broker /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server broker:29092 \
  --command-config /etc/kafka/tls/face-reader.properties --list
. ./.env
curl -s --cacert secrets/ca.crt -u "face-reader:$REGISTRY_FACE_READER" https://localhost:8081/subjects

You see the twelve topics below and one -value subject for each.
docker exec broker /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh \
  --bootstrap-server broker:29092 \
  --consumer.config /etc/kafka/tls/face-reader.properties \
  --topic quillmere.fleet.telematics.v1 \
  --from-beginning --max-messages 5 \
  --property print.key=true --property print.timestamp=true

The key is the trailer ID. The value is Avro in the Confluent wire format: a zero byte, the 4-byte schema ID, then the Avro body. The console consumer prints it as raw bytes. To read values as text, run the producer without --registry: it then writes JSON values and registers no schemas.
4. Add the connection in FACE
In Settings › Integrations › Systems, add a Kafka connection:



Setting
Value




bootstrap_servers
localhost:9092


topics
quillmere.


client_id
face-quickstart


security_protocol
sasl_ssl


sasl_mechanism
scram-sha-512


username
face-reader


ssl_ca_pem
the contents of secrets/ca.crt


schema_registry_url
https://localhost:8081


schema_registry_username
face-reader






Credential
Value




password
SCRAM_FACE_READER from .env


schema_registry_password
REGISTRY_FACE_READER from .env



ssl_ca_pem is a certificate, not a secret: it is what lets FACE check the broker's and the registry's certificates against the authority you generated, instead of trusting anything. localhost works when FACE runs on the same machine as the broker. If FACE runs elsewhere, use the KAFKA_HOST you gave setup.sh in both addresses, for example kafka-host.example.invalid:9092 and https://kafka-host.example.invalid:8081.
topics is a prefix filter: quillmere. matches all twelve topics.
FACE lands a fetch of one Kafka connection as one table, every topic it reads side by side. So that the readings are read as readings, give the two sensor-reading topics their own connections, each with the property runink.domain:



Connection
topics
Property runink.domain
What FACE reads from it




Fleet sensor readings
quillmere.fleet.sensor-readings.
telemetry
vehicle positions on the map, and cold-chain time out of band


Equipment readings
quillmere.assets.equipment-readings.
equipment
trends towards each channel's stated limit, with the projected crossing



and narrow the first connection's topics to the other ten (quillmere.fleet.telematics., quillmere.site., quillmere.drone., quillmere.yard., quillmere.mainframe.). All three use the same security settings and credentials.
Step by step in the Console

Open Settings › Integrations › Systems and select New connection.
Source: under Sensors & telemetry, select Apache Kafka, then Next.


Details: enter a Connection name (the Id follows it) and the Environment. Under Settings, fill in Bootstrap servers (comma-separated), Topics (a prefix) and User (face-reader).

Set Security protocol to sasl_ssl. It is the only value FACE saves: plaintext and SASL_PLAINTEXT send everything unencrypted, and ssl carries no login.
Under Credentials, enter Password and Schema Registry password from .env.
Open Advanced and set SASL mechanism to scram-sha-512, Client ID, Schema Registry URL (https://…), Schema Registry user (face-reader) and CA certificate (the contents of secrets/ca.crt). The form has no switch to skip certificate checks, and FACE refuses a connection with insecure_skip_verify on.
Runner: keep Runink managed, or pick a registered runner that can reach the broker, then Next.


Review: check the values, keep Test after saving ticked and select Test & save. If a security setting is missing, the Console says which and does not save.

The test routes to the runner and asks the broker to answer. Tested: the source answered means the broker is reachable and accepted the login; it does not mean records have been read. Select Done.

The connection joins the list and appears among the sources on Ask, and in every brief's source list.
The topics
Every topic has 3 partitions. The key is a business ID, as plain text, so a consumer can join on it without the registry. The value schema is registered under the topic name (-value). Positions are WGS84 degrees, in latitude and longitude. Times are UTC, and each record's Kafka timestamp is the time of the event.



Topic
Key
What it carries
How often




quillmere.fleet.telematics.v1
trailer_id
Position along the lane between sites, speed, heading, odometer, fuel, engine fault, reefer setpoint and return-air temperature, rear door
every 5 s per trailer, 10 trailers


quillmere.site.dock-doors.v1
dock_id
Dock door open or closed, dock occupied, door cycle count, last change
every 10 s per dock, 9 docks


quillmere.site.environment.v1
sensor_id
Temperature and humidity per zone: ambient, cold room, freezer, dock apron, the port's reefer rack
every 15 s per sensor, 14 sensors


quillmere.site.equipment.v1
equipment_id
Forklifts, AGVs and straddle carriers: position, state, battery, speed, load
every 5 s per machine, 11 machines


quillmere.site.energy.v1
meter_id
Demand and energy per circuit: refrigeration, lighting, dock doors, chargers, reefer rack, gate
every 60 s per meter, 16 meters


quillmere.drone.survey.v1
flight_id
Survey frames with position and altitude: case counts by rack location in the DCs, trailer counts in the yards and the port, perimeter checks
every 4 s while flying; one 8-minute flight per site each hour


quillmere.yard.gate-events.v1
trailer_id
Trailers in and out of the yard and port gates, read by RFID or plate
on each arrival and departure


quillmere.yard.trailer-positions.v1
trailer_id
Parked trailer's yard slot, load state, gate-in time and dwell
every 30 s per parked trailer


quillmere.mainframe.orders.cdc.v1
order_id
Order header changes from the order-entry mainframe
every 10 s


quillmere.mainframe.inventory.cdc.v1
@
On-hand and allocated cases per item and warehouse
every 5 s, after a full refresh at start


quillmere.fleet.sensor-readings.v1
asset_id
Sensor readings: a GPS fix (metric gps_fix, latitude/longitude with geo_stated, speed, odometer) for every tractor, van and trailer; every reefer's return air (metric temperature) with its load's stated band (threshold_min/threshold_max) and the load spec's allowance out of band (max_excursion_minutes), and, on a reefer trailer carrying a shipment, the load's value (load_value, load_value_currency)
every 30 s per vehicle (28), every 60 s per reefer (7)


quillmere.assets.equipment-readings.v1
asset_id
Sensor readings for every equipment channel of the fleet, the yards and the warehouses: tractor coolant, oil pressure, battery, brake pads, tyres; reefer return air and compressor duty; yard tractor hydraulics, gate barrier motors, reefer plug-ins; forklift batteries and motors, dock levelers, refrigeration compressors, cold and freezer rooms. Each states its limit in attributes (alarm_c, trip_c or replace_below_pct, with limit_source)
every 120 s per channel (183)



The two sensor-reading topics use the field names a telemetry source lands as (asset_id, observed_at, metric, value, value_stated, unit, the threshold pair with its *_stated flags, attributes). The tractors and vans run loops from their distribution centre through three customer delivery sites and back, on straight lines between the points, not on roads. A dozen channels drift towards their limit on a three-hour ramp and reset, time compressed so that minutes of the stream show the slope: coolant creeping up, brake pads wearing, a reefer's return air leaving its 2-8 °C band, a cold room drifting off its setpoint, a refrigeration compressor running hotter.
The sites are the quickstart's three distribution centres and their yards, at their authored addresses (Elk Grove Village IL, Plainfield IN and Edwardsville IL), and one port terminal: Quillmere Calumet Terminal, a point in the Lake Calumet port district in Chicago. The trucks run four lanes along the interstate corridors between them. The lanes are polylines through the cities on those corridors, not a road network.
The mainframe records
The two mainframe topics are change data, as a capture agent delivers it from an IMS database updated by CICS transactions. Each record carries the fixed-width record, already converted from EBCDIC, and the same fields decoded. op is REFRESH for the initial full read, then INSERT or UPDATE.
The order header record, copybook QORDHDR, 88 bytes:
05 OH-ORDER-ID     PIC X(10).
05 OH-CUST-ID      PIC X(10).
05 OH-CUST-PO      PIC X(16).
05 OH-WHSE-ID      PIC X(10).
05 OH-STATUS       PIC X(2).     OP, AL, PK or SH
05 OH-LINE-COUNT   PIC 9(3).
05 OH-TOTAL-CENTS  PIC 9(11).
05 OH-CHANGED-TS   PIC X(26).    YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.NNNNNN
The inventory balance record, copybook QINVBAL, 88 bytes:
05 IB-SKU-ID       PIC X(10).
05 IB-LOC-ID       PIC X(10).
05 IB-DESC         PIC X(24).
05 IB-UOM          PIC X(2).
05 IB-ON-HAND      PIC S9(7) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE.
05 IB-ALLOCATED    PIC S9(7) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE.
05 IB-CHANGED-TS   PIC X(26).
The mainframe is a source in its own right: it opens with a balance for every quickstart item at every warehouse, then changes them. New orders continue the order numbers after the quickstart's 24 orders and use its customers and items.
The planted anomalies
Six anomalies recur every hour, so FACE has something to find whenever you connect. The minute is counted from when the producer started.



ID
Minute
Where
What




ANOM-L1
10 to 30
fleet.telematics, trailer TRL-102
A reefer temperature excursion. The door opens, then the return air climbs through 9.2, 10.8 and 11.4 °C and stays above the 8 °C limit for about 12 minutes. It is the same profile as the cold-chain scenario of shipment SHP-50004.


ANOM-L2
25 to 45
site.dock-doors, DOCK-EAST-02
A stuck sensor. It keeps sending heartbeats, but the door state, cycle count and last-change time do not move for 20 minutes. Every other door changes at least every 10 minutes.


ANOM-L3
32 to 40
drone.survey at WH-SOUTH
A drone count that disagrees with the mainframe. For one item, the drone counts 48 cases (one pallet) fewer than the mainframe's on-hand balance at that moment. Every other item agrees.


ANOM-L4
from 30
yard.gate-events
A duplicate gate read. The first gate event after the half hour is delivered twice, with the same event_id.


ANOM-L5
35
fleet.telematics, trailer TRL-105
A GPS jump. One frame puts the trailer about 380 km north of its lane, 5 seconds after and before frames on the lane, at an ordinary speed.


ANOM-L6
40 to 48
drone.survey at YARD-SOUTH
A perimeter finding: three frames report a gap in the north fence.



The producer prints this list, with the item for ANOM-L3, when it starts.
Reproducing a run
The stream is deterministic. The same --seed and --start give the same records, byte for byte:
docker run --rm face-stream-producer:1.4.0 produce kafka --dry-run --ticks 60 --start 2026-10-11T12:00:00Z

--dry-run prints a minute of records as JSON lines and opens no connection. Other flags:



Flag
Default





--bootstrap
none
The broker, host:port


--security-protocol
plaintext
sasl_ssl for this broker; FACE itself connects only with sasl_ssl


--sasl-mechanism
SCRAM-SHA-512
SCRAM-SHA-512 or SCRAM-SHA-256


--sasl-username, --sasl-password-file
none
The broker login; the password is read from the file


--tls-ca-file
none
The certificate authority the broker's and the registry's certificates must chain to


--registry
none
The Schema Registry URL, https:// with a secured broker. Without it, values are JSON.


--registry-username, --registry-password-file
none
The registry login; the password is read from the file


--rate
about 7
Events per second across all topics. A higher rate runs the estate faster.


--seed
20261005
The quickstart universe's seed


--start
now
Event time of the first record


--retention, --retention-bytes
24h, 64 MiB
Topic retention, set when the producer creates a topic



Stop and clean up
docker compose down -v
rm -rf secrets .env

-v removes the broker's volume with every topic and record, and the registry's login file. Removing secrets/ and .env deletes the keys and passwords.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/quickstart.title: MQTT
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/quickstart.body:
MQTT


Warning: The test-estate safety rule: stand the test estate up only beside a test instance, never a production deployment. Its systems are throwaway test services with published credentials: change-me is every test credential. They are still encrypted and still ask for a login, because FACE refuses a connection that is not (see Connector security). Use a scratch machine or a scratch cluster.

Grade D · dataset: Stream (a timestamped recording) · type mqtt
What it is
An MQTT 3.1.1 broker. In the test estate it carries reefer temperature readings and unit state from the trailers. The connector reference is Telemetry.
Grade
D. Dataset and model: the quickstart dataset and its expected model ship. There is no vendor system to stand up for this type; load the dataset and fetch it.
See the grade table for all 32 types.
Settings and credentials
From the connection catalogue. Settings are ordinary fields on the connection record. Credentials are kept in a sealed bundle and never returned.




Names




Type
mqtt


Other spellings that resolve
mqtts, iothub, sensorbus, messagebus


Settings
broker_url, topics, qos, client_id, username, collect_seconds, max_messages, protocol_version, use_tls, insecure_skip_verify


Credentials
password



The test connection
Reefer telemetry broker



Setting
Test value




broker_url
mqtts://mqtt.quillmere.invalid:8883


topics
quillmere/reefer/+/temperature,quillmere/reefer/+/unit


qos
1


client_id
face-collector


username
face-reader


collect_seconds
60


max_messages
5000


protocol_version
3.1.1


use_tls
true



Credentials: password. In the test estate, every credential is change-me. Credentials are write-only: they go into the sealed credential bundle and are never returned.
Stand up the test system
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.

Run an MQTT 3.1.1 broker you control, with a TLS listener (port 8883) and password logins, and a face-reader user. Eclipse Mosquitto is one open-source option: give its listener a certfile, keyfile and cafile, and a password_file. FACE refuses a broker without TLS or without a login.
Download messages.jsonl from the recording below and publish it. Each line is one message, in time order: its topic, qos, retain flag and JSON payload. With Mosquitto's client and jq, over the same TLS listener (ca.crt is the CA that signed the broker's certificate, and  is the name on it):
jq -r '"\(.topic)\t\(.qos)\t\(.retain)\t\(.payload | tojson)"' messages.jsonl |
while IFS=$'\t' read -r topic qos retain payload; do
  if [ "$retain" = true ]; then r=-r; else r=; fi
  mosquitto_pub -h  -p 8883 --cafile ca.crt -u  -P change-me \
    -t "$topic" -q "$qos" $r -m "$payload"
done


Add the connection in Settings › Integrations › Systems, with broker_url set to mqtts://:8883, use_tls on and the password credential. Leave insecure_skip_verify off: FACE refuses a connection with it on. FACE subscribes to quillmere/reefer/+/temperature for the collection window.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/discovery/.title: Explore, sample and profile
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/discovery/.body:
Explore, sample and profile

FACE learns about a source in three steps. Each step reads more than the one
before it, and each is bounded separately.



Step
RPC
Reads
Moves customer rows?




Explore
ConfigService.ExploreConnection
The source's own catalogue: dataset names, column names, declared types, nullability and declared constraints
No


Sample
ConfigService.SampleConnectionDataset
A bounded set of real rows from one dataset
Yes, bounded


Profile
Used when FACE maps the estate, automatically at the start of a fetch
A bounded row sample of named columns, plus optional per-column aggregates
Bounded



Explore
Explore asks the connector to describe what the source holds, without assuming
anything about its data model. The response is:

description (SourceDescription), which is never unset on a non-error return:
supported: whether this source has a catalogue that FACE can read.
reason: a human-readable explanation. Display it; do not match on it.
datasets[]: each DescribedDataset has a name, a kind (table, view,
entity set, topic, media track, …), a qualifier (for example
DATABASE.SCHEMA or catalog.schema) and columns[], plus row counts,
relationships, tags and partition keys where the source states them.
datasets[].sample is always unset here, because Explore does not sample.
aspects[]: which questions were asked (asked), whether the answer was
readable (readable), the source call used (source), and a detail.
Check this before concluding that something is absent.


discovery_attempted: whether a connector's discovery actually ran. It is false
when the id did not resolve or the type has no connector. true together with
supported=false is a normal, useful answer for a source with no catalogue.

Every *_stated flag in the description means the source itself said so. A
column's nullable is meaningful only when nullable_stated is true, and the
same rule applies to units, row counts, sizes and last-altered times. FACE never
fills these in from defaults.
Which values may leave a source during Explore
Explore reads metadata only. It does not read:

row counts that would need a scan (COUNT(*))
most-common-value lists or histograms, because those are literal customer values
sample rows

A catalogue is permission-filtered. What comes back is what this credential can
see, which may be smaller than what exists.
Explore support by connector



Connector
Explore reads




PostgreSQL, MySQL
information_schema tables and columns, up to 500 tables. Declared primary, unique and foreign keys come from pg_catalog.pg_constraint on PostgreSQL and information_schema on MySQL.


PostgreSQL (also)
Table, view and column comments from pg_catalog.pg_description, and view definitions from pg_get_viewdef, for the listed datasets. Partitions and extension-owned relations are not listed, and the count left out is stated. Reading them needs no role beyond the default PUBLIC access to pg_catalog.


Snowflake
INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and .COLUMNS for the connection's database (and schema, when set), including ROW_COUNT where Snowflake maintains it.


Databricks
system.information_schema columns and tables, column tags (declared units and PII classes), and CHECK … IN (…) vocabularies. It is metastore-wide unless a catalog property scopes it.


SAP (OData)
One GET of the service $metadata (CSDL). Entity sets become datasets.


Salesforce
Org version list, Describe Global, then a per-object describe (up to 200 objects described).


Guidewire
/rest/apis, the per-API OpenAPI documents and typelists.


Kafka
Topic catalogue (Metadata) plus Schema Registry value schemas. It reads no record.


CCTV
RTSP DESCRIBE, or ONVIF profiles followed by DESCRIBE.


Flipper edge reader
The edge agent's capability catalogue.


All others
supported=false with a reason that says whether the source has no catalogue at all (Modbus, device capture, a file) or the connector does not read one.



Sample
SampleConnectionDataset is the one ConfigService RPC that moves customer data.
You name one dataset by qualifier and name, exactly as Explore reported
them. The server re-quotes both parts for each engine. Every identifier part goes
through an identifier allowlist first, and a name that the allowlist rejects is
refused with the reason. It is never escaped or quoted around.
Bounds:

row_limit must be in 0..1000. 0 means the connector's default. A value
outside that range is refused, not clamped.
Each connector applies its own ceiling:
| Connector | Default rows | Ceiling | Cell size cap | Method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Snowflake | 10 | 100 | 512 bytes | FIXED_SIZE_RANDOM (SAMPLE (n ROWS)) |
| Databricks | 25 | 1000 (above is refused) | 4096 bytes | FIRST_ROWS (the first rows the engine produced) |

Sampling is served for the connectors in the table above. Any other type answers
sampled: false with a reason naming the source type. Use Explore for its
structure.


Before sampling, the server explores the dataset to learn its governance
(masked columns, row filters). The response sample then carries:

columns and rows. Each SampleCell separates is_null from an empty
value.
method and method_detail: the statistical class and the source's own clause.
masked_columns, row_filter and governance_checked. governance_checked is
false when the governance answer could not be obtained.
caveats, which is never empty.

Show masked_columns, row_filter and governance_checked beside the rows.
A masked column returns its masked value and still counts as a successful read.
Sampled rows are not the dataset. A null rate, a distinct count or an absent
value computed over 25 rows says nothing about the table.
Profile
FACE maps the estate as part of every fetch, over the connections that fetch reads; a
newly confirmed connection joins at the next fetch. There is no separate control to map it
by hand. When it maps the
estate for analysis, it profiles each connection within fixed budgets:

Which datasets. At most 12 datasets per connection are profiled, taken
in catalogue order. The result reports datasets_profiled next to
datasets_discovered.
Sample reads. FACE reads the columns it names from the catalogue. It never
uses SELECT * and adds no COUNT(*). The default is 25 rows, with ceilings
of 100 rows, 64 columns and 512 bytes per value.
Time. The deadline is 30 s by default and at most 2 minutes. The deadline
bounds how long FACE waits, not the work the warehouse does.
Statistics. An optional aggregate pass computes, per column:

non-null and null counts
null rate
distinct count
range (min/max)
mean and standard deviation

Each figure carries a *Stated flag and a basis. A range can be withheld with
a stated reason.

Opting out. A connection listed in metadata_only_connection_ids is read
for its catalogue only, and no data is read.

No sampled value is ever written to a log.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/sql-wareho.title: SQL warehouses and databases
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/sql-wareho.body:
SQL warehouses and databases

FACE reads Snowflake, Databricks SQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL through their
standard drivers.
Common behaviour

Queries are read-only. Every statement must start with SELECT, WITH,
SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN. A statement that contains restricted
keywords is refused. Unclosed comments and string literals are refused.
Parameters are bound. Values in params are passed to the driver as bound
parameters, never interpolated into the SQL. A positional parameter list may
accompany only a single statement.
Multi-statement batches report partial failure. If some statements in a
batch are refused by the engine, the read still returns the rows from the
others. The message states how many statements failed. It lists up to 8
reasons, and the count is never truncated.
Credentials come from the credential bundle, never from the record. See
Connections and credentials.
Test dials the source. For every engine on this page,
Test opens a connection and runs the driver's Ping. A success means the
endpoint answered and the credential was accepted. It does not mean the role
can read any particular table.
How queries arrive. In a fetch, Snowflake and Databricks run FACE's
built-in fetch template for that engine. PostgreSQL and MySQL read the
business tables they expose (a sweep of their tables). Both run on the
selected runner. Outside a fetch, SqlService.Execute and
ExecuteSelect accept an explicit sql and params against a stored
connection_id (see /docs/developer-guide/api/).
A failure is reported as a failure. When an engine cannot be reached, the
fetch reports  Execution Failed for : …, with personal data
masked. No other data is substituted.

Snowflake









Type spellings
snowflake


Config message
SnowflakeConnectionConfig


Settings
account (required), warehouse, database, schema, role, user


Credentials
password (or pat / token for a programmatic access token). user or username may also come from the bundle.


Connection string
connection_string in the form user[:password]@account/database[/schema][?param=value…], parsed at save time


Transport
HTTPS through FACE's hardened transport. The address policy applies, and internal addresses are refused unless allow_internal_network=true is set.


Test
A live dial (driver ping)


Explore
INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and .COLUMNS, scoped to database and to schema when set. Includes the table kind, column order, the account's own type spelling, declared nullability, and ROW_COUNT (left unstated for views).


Sample
SAMPLE (n ROWS). Default 10 rows, at most 100, cells capped at 512 bytes.



Optional runner-deploy settings (none of them is a credential) are compute_pool,
image_repository, runner_image (pinned by digest, …@sha256:),
network_rule, external_access_integration. See Runners.
Databricks









Type spellings
databricks


Config message
DatabricksConnectionConfig


Settings
host (the workspace host, required; https:// is assumed, and http:// is refused), http_path (required: the /sql/1.0/warehouses/… path of one SQL warehouse or cluster)


Scope properties
catalog (or databricks_catalog, unity_catalog), schema (or databricks_schema)


Credentials
personal_access_token (or token)


Connection string
connection_string, parsed at save time


Transport
Port 443, through FACE's hardened transport. The address policy applies, and internal addresses are refused unless opted in.


Test
A live dial (driver ping)


Explore
system.information_schema columns joined to tables (metastore-wide, or one catalog when catalog is set). Declared units and PII classes come from column tags. Complete vocabularies come from CHECK (col IN (…)) constraints.


Sample
Default 25 rows, at most 1000 (a larger value is refused). Cells are capped at 4096 bytes. Method: FIRST_ROWS.



Optional runner-deploy settings (none of them is a credential) are cluster_policy_id,
node_type_id, spark_version, runner_artifact, runner_artifact_sha256,
runner_scope (the name of a secret scope), service_principal (an
application id, not its secret).
PostgreSQL









Type spellings
postgres, postgresql


Config message
PostgresConnectionConfig


Settings
host, port (default 5432), database, username, ssl_mode


Credentials
password; username may also come from the bundle


Test
A live dial (driver ping)


Explore
information_schema tables and columns (up to 500 tables) and declared keys from pg_catalog.pg_constraint



MySQL









Type spellings
mysql


Config message
MySqlConnectionConfig


Settings
host, port (default 3306), database, username; ssl_mode as a property


Credentials
password


Test
A live dial (driver ping)


Explore
information_schema tables and columns, and declared keys from TABLE_CONSTRAINTS joined to KEY_COLUMN_USAGE



Multi-statement mode is off at the driver.
Database TLS (ssl_mode)
PostgreSQL reads the typed ssl_mode field. MySQL reads the ssl_mode property.
Every PostgreSQL and MySQL connection must state it, and must have a username and a
password credential. See Security requirements.



Value
Behaviour




(empty)
Refused. The setting must be stated, so that it can be audited.


require
Encrypt without verifying the server certificate


verify-ca, verify-full
Encrypt and verify


disable, prefer, allow
Refused. These modes send data without TLS, or can fall back to it silently.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/enterprise.title: Enterprise SaaS and ERP
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/enterprise.body:
Enterprise SaaS and ERP

The SaaS and ERP connectors speak each vendor's REST or OData API directly. Each
section below lists what the connector reads, the settings it takes and what Test
checks.
Summary



Connector
Type spellings
Test
Explore
Extraction




SAP (OData)
sap
No live probe
Yes ($metadata)
Metadata through Explore


Salesforce
salesforce
Live (OAuth token request)
Yes
SOQL query with paging


Guidewire
guidewire
Live (/rest/apis)
Yes
Cloud API resource reads with paging


ServiceNow
servicenow
Live (Table API request)
No catalogue read
Fixed Table API tables


Google Workspace
gmail, google_sheets (fetch only)
Not available
No
Gmail and Sheets reads during a fetch



For a type with no live probe, Test returns success: true with
live_check_performed: false, which means the configuration was saved and
nothing was verified. See Connections and credentials.
Every address on these connectors must be https://. http:// is refused, and so is
a bare host that the connector would dial as http (SAP's host and base_url,
Guidewire's base_url). A bare ServiceNow instance name and an empty Salesforce
login_url are dialled as https. See
Security requirements.
All HTTP-based connectors here dial through FACE's hardened HTTP client. It uses
no proxy, applies the address policy, and follows at most 5
redirects, all to the same host. A redirect to a different host is refused, so a
credential never travels to a host the connection did not name.
SAP (OData / CSDL)
SAP connections describe an SAP system through SAPConnectionConfig (system_id,
client, username, password, host, system_number). Those are RFC and SAP
GUI destination parameters. OData discovery is driven by connection
properties:



Property
Meaning




odata_url (also odata_base_url, odata_service_url, service_url, base_url, endpoint, url)
The OData service root. Write it as https://…: http:// is refused, and the connector would dial a value with no scheme as http. The URL must not contain user:pass@.


odata_service_path (also service_path, service)
Appended to the service root


sap_client (also sap-client, mandt, client)
Sent as the sap-client query parameter


sap_gateway_url
Instead of one service: the Gateway origin, whose OData V2 service catalogue is enumerated



Credentials: username (setting or credential), and password (also api_key,
token or secret) from the credential bundle. Internal addresses are allowed by
default, because SAP systems usually live on private networks.

Explore. One GET of the service's $metadata, capped at 16 MiB.
Entity sets become datasets of kind entityset, qualified by the CSDL
namespace.
Properties keep their document order and the service's own type spelling
(for example Edm.Decimal(13,3)).
Literal units come from Measures.Unit / ISOCurrency, and PII flags from
PersonalData.IsPotentiallyPersonal.
Validation.AllowedValues becomes a vocabulary (up to 128 values). It is
always reported as incomplete, because CSDL does not enforce it.
Nullability is reported only where the document states it.
No row counts are requested.


Test. Saves the configuration. Explore is the reachability check: it reads the
service's $metadata.

Salesforce









Config message
SalesforceConnectionConfig: login_url, client_id


Credentials
username, password, security_token (appended to the password), client_secret


Auth
OAuth 2.0 username–password flow against /services/oauth2/token


Properties
soql (the query a fetch runs), api_version (default v60.0; must match vNN.N), max_records / max_rows, include_deleted (uses queryAll)


Internal addresses
Controlled per connection with allow_internal_network




Test posts the token request to the login host. A success means the
credentials were accepted. Discovery and queries then dial the instance_url
that the token response names.
Extraction runs one SOQL statement, either the query you pass or the
connection's soql property. The connector does not choose objects for you.
It follows nextRecordsUrl on the same host only.
Rows: default 5,000, at most 50,000.
Paging: at most 200 pages within a 3-minute budget.
A response that contradicts itself (done with a next page, or not done
without one) is refused rather than returned short.


Explore reads the org's version list, then Describe Global, then a
describe per object:
Up to 200 objects get column detail. The rest are listed without columns,
and the reason says how many.
Picklists become vocabularies (up to 512 values). A vocabulary is marked
complete only when the org flags the picklist as restricted.
Lookup targets appear in the declared type as reference(Account).
No row counts are requested, to protect your metered API allocation.



Guidewire









Config message
GuidewireConnectionConfig: base_url (the Cloud API root), tenant_id


Credentials
username and password, sent as HTTP Basic


Properties
resource (also route, path): the route a fetch reads. max_records / max_rows.


Internal addresses
Controlled per connection with allow_internal_network




Test calls /rest/apis and requires a non-empty API list.
Extraction reads one resource (the query or resource) inside the
base_url path. A route that escapes the base path is refused.
Page size: 200 by default, 500 maximum.
Rows: 5,000 by default, 50,000 maximum.
Paging: at most 200 pages within 3 minutes. links.next is followed on the
same host only.
A 200 response without Guidewire's data envelope is refused rather than
read as empty.


Explore enumerates /rest/apis, the per-API OpenAPI documents and the
typelists. Typelist vocabularies are marked complete when the codes served
match the count the index declares.
The connector speaks HTTP Basic, which is what self-managed installations use.

ServiceNow
ServiceNow settings are read from connection properties: systemUrl (the
instance URL). The credentials are username and password (HTTP Basic).
Internal addresses are refused unless allow_internal_network=true is set.

Extraction reads the Table API tables syslog, sysevent and sys_audit,
with an 8 MiB cap per response.
Test requests the first of those tables.
Explore returns supported=false. ServiceNow data is read through extraction.

Google Workspace
Google Workspace is read only during a fetch, through two connection types.
Test and Explore apply to registry connectors, so Test reports
Unknown connection type for these two types. Google Docs is not a
connection type: FACE does not read Google Docs.



Type
What a fetch reads
Settings




gmail
Up to 5 messages matching the fetch command as a Gmail query (label:INBOX when the command is fetch)
—


google_sheets
One range of one spreadsheet
properties spreadsheet_id (falls back to the connection name) and range (default A1:Z50)



Credentials: a google_sheets connection may hold google_service_account_json; without it,
and always for gmail, the instance-wide Google integration configured in
Settings › Integrations › Channels is used. The type is matched case-insensitively but otherwise exactly
(google_sheets, not Google Sheets).

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/files-obje.title: Files and object storage
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/files-obje.body:
Files and object storage

FACE reads spreadsheets, delimited and JSON files, Parquet, and objects in your
own cloud buckets. Every read is streamed and bounded, and a clipped read is
always marked as truncated.
Read bounds (all file formats)



Bound
Default
Meaning




Bytes read
64 MiB
A ceiling on what is read from the source, including a single pathological line


Rows kept
10,000
A ceiling on what is returned



When either bound is reached, the response message ends with
— TRUNCATED: .
Supported formats: csv, tsv, json (a top-level array), jsonl / ndjson,
txt, html, parquet, and xlsx / xlsm for Excel. For objects, FACE takes
the format from the key's extension.
Excel









Type spellings
excel, xlsx, spreadsheet


Config message
ExcelConnectionConfig: file_path, has_header


Credentials
None (CREDENTIAL_STATE_NONE_NEEDED)


Test
Checks that file_path exists on the reading node, is not a directory, and ends in .xlsx or .xlsm. It is a local file check, not a network dial.


Execute
Reads one sheet. The query names the sheet, and an empty query reads the first sheet. Rows are decoded one at a time and stop at the row cap.


Explore
supported=false. A workbook's sheets and header row are its schema.



For CSV and other delimited text, use an object-store connection or a document
source.
Object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob)









Type spellings
objectstore, s3, awss3, gcs, googlecloudstorage, azureblob, azure, blobstorage


Config message
ObjectStoreConnectionConfig






Setting
Meaning




provider
s3, gcs or azure. Aliases such as minio, ceph, aws, gcp and azblob are normalised. It is required, and an unknown provider is refused.


bucket
The bucket, or the container for Azure. Required.


prefix
An optional key prefix that scopes the connection


region
S3 region


endpoint
An S3-compatible endpoint (MinIO, Ceph, your own objectd). Empty means AWS S3 over TLS. For GCS or Azure, a custom service endpoint. It must be https://: http:// is refused.


account
Azure storage account name (required for Azure)


use_tls
Whether an S3-compatible endpoint given without a scheme uses TLS. A scheme on endpoint overrides it. A bare S3 host:port without use_tls is refused.



Credential keys:



Provider
Keys




S3
access_key and secret_key (also aws_access_key_id / aws_secret_access_key), optional session_token


GCS
service_account_json (also credentials_json, google_credentials). It may be omitted only with a custom endpoint.


Azure
account_key, or sas_token, or connection_string




Test has a 10-second budget and runs one live call per provider: S3
BucketExists, GCS bucket attributes, or Azure container properties. Messages
distinguish "does not exist, or these credentials cannot see it" from
"cannot reach".
Execute reads one object. The query is the object key, and prefix is
prepended when the key does not already start with it. Parquet objects are read
from their footer, and all other formats are streamed. Object reads use
S3-compatible stores; for GCS and Azure, Test checks the bucket or container.
Explore returns supported=false. Listing a bucket gives keys, not a schema.

Parquet
A Parquet file is read from its footer, so FACE needs its size and random access.
That makes an object in an S3-compatible store the supported source. FACE reads
in batches of 256 rows under the same row cap. A file larger than the byte
ceiling is refused with
parquet file is … bytes, beyond the …-byte ceiling.
Document sources
A fetch hands the following connection types to FACE's document extraction (OCR)
path rather than to a tabular connector:

gdrive
gcp_bucket
sftp
local
pdf
word
network

They read connection properties: path (it falls back to the connection name),
host, port, and bucket for buckets. Their output is extracted text.

SFTP requires a verified host key and refuses to connect without one.
Downloads stop if nothing arrives for 60 seconds.
Downloads are capped at 2 GiB by default; a deployment setting changes the cap.

These types have no registry connector, so Test and Explore do not apply to them.
Of these types, only sftp meets the
connector security policy. The others have no
security rule, so a connection of those types cannot be saved, and a stored one is
refused when a fetch reads it.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/streaming-.title: Streaming: Kafka
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/streaming-.body:
Streaming: Kafka

FACE connects to Kafka (and to Redpanda, which speaks the same protocol) to
enumerate its topic catalogue and read declared structure from a
Confluent-compatible Schema Registry. FACE implements the handshake,
ApiVersions, Metadata and the SASL exchange natively. No Kafka client
library is used.

Note: Kafka connections serve the topic catalogue and Schema Registry structure through
Explore.

Type spellings
kafka, redpanda, apachekafka (the "Apache Kafka" card).
Azure Event Hubs and Amazon MSK are not aliased, because they require SASL
mechanisms this connector does not speak.
Settings (KafkaConnectionConfig)



Setting
Meaning




bootstrap_servers
One or more host:port values (default port 9092). Required, and there is no default broker. List several: Test succeeds as soon as any one of them answers.


topics
Optional prefix filters over the catalogue. An empty list is normal and enumerates every topic the principal may see. Reading the catalogue moves no data.


client_id
Sent in every request header. The default is runink-face-.


security_protocol
sasl_ssl. Required. Unset (which means plaintext), plaintext, sasl_plaintext and ssl are refused: ssl encrypts but carries no login.


sasl_mechanism
scram-sha-512 or scram-sha-256. Required. SCRAM verifies the broker's server signature and refuses the connection if it does not match. Any other mechanism is refused.


username
The SASL username (a setting). Required.


schema_registry_url
An https:// base URL. Optional: without it, topics are listed with no columns. The URL must not contain credentials. http:// is refused.


schema_registry_username
The registry's HTTP-basic user. Required when a registry URL is set.


ssl_ca_pem
The PEM CA certificate the broker's TLS certificate must chain to, for a broker with a private CA. Empty means the public roots. Only these roots are trusted for the broker, its host name is still checked, and a value holding a private key is refused. It is a public certificate, not a credential. The Schema Registry keeps the system roots.



Credentials: password for SASL (required), and schema_registry_password for the
registry (a separate credential, because the registry authenticates separately;
required when a registry URL is set).
insecure_skip_verify is refused: the broker's and the registry's certificates are
always checked. A connection that does not meet these rules cannot be saved, and a
stored one is refused on every read until it is upgraded. See
Security requirements.
Set allow_internal_network to control whether the connection may reach internal
addresses.
Test
Test performs a real handshake against the bootstrap servers in order: dial, TLS,
ApiVersions, and the SASL exchange. It
returns success on the first broker that completes it. If none does, it returns
no bootstrap server answered: … with each broker's error.
A successful Test does not establish:

that the principal may list topics, because topic authorisation is checked
per topic
that the Schema Registry exists or answers, because Test does not contact it
that any topic holds a record

Explore
Explore reads the topic catalogue (up to 5,000 topics) and, where a registry is
configured, each topic's value subject (-value). No record body is
read.



Topic
Columns




With a registered value schema
The schema's fields, with the Avro type verbatim, nullability from the union, enum symbols as allowed values, and each doc as a description. This is declared structure.


Without one
None. FACE never infers fields from sampled messages.


Registry not asked, or unreadable
None. The schemas aspect shows asked=false or readable=false, so you can tell this case apart from "no schema".



Topic names ending in .by-.v (for example acme.orders.events.by-order_id.v1)
yield a partition key, marked with a name-match basis. It is never reported as
declared. Key subjects and offsets are not requested, and the aspects say so.
For Kafka, use Explore. Sample and Profile apply to the SQL warehouses.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/event-list.title: Event listeners
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/event-list.body:
Event listeners

A data listener follows one connection's stream of business changes: rows changed
in a transactional database, records produced to a Kafka topic. It counts them, meters
them, and hands them to briefs that run when data changes,
which run a fetch when the changes you ask for arrive.
The listener itself reads only each change's coordinates (where, what kind, which key),
never its values. The run it fires is a fetch like any other: it reads the connection's
tables with the connection's own login, reads back the rows that changed, and reports
which business rules those rows conform to or break. Nothing is installed in your
source by FACE.
It is not the Metadata listener on a connection in Settings › Integrations › Systems,
which watches a source for schema changes. The two are switched on separately.
Which sources



Source
How it listens
What you install




PostgreSQL
LISTEN on a channel, then reads a change-event ledger table
the ledger, once, by your DBA (below)


Apache Kafka
reads every partition of the connection's topics from the latest offsets
nothing



Other source types have no data listener. A connection bound to a self-hosted runner is
reported NOT LISTENING with that reason: listening runs on the managed runner only,
and a connection bound to a runner is never moved to another one.
PostgreSQL: the change-event ledger
The listener needs your database to say what changed. It uses an ordinary trigger, a
ledger table and NOTIFY, not logical replication:

Logical replication needs wal_level=logical, a role with REPLICATION that streams
every column of every published table, and a replication slot. A slot whose consumer
is away keeps WAL without limit, which can fill the database's disk.
The ledger costs one small row per change and keeps least privilege: the connection's
login only needs SELECT on one more table. NOTIFY is only a wake-up call; a listener
that was disconnected reads every row after the last one it saw, so nothing is lost.

Your database administrator runs this once, adapting the table list to yours. Each
trigger names its table's business-key column; the ledger records the schema-qualified
table and that column, so an event-fired run can read the changed row back. Grant the
connection's login SELECT on the ledger and on the tables it reads.
CREATE TABLE ops.change_events (
  seq         bigserial   PRIMARY KEY,
  occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
  table_name  text        NOT NULL,   -- schema.table
  op          text        NOT NULL CHECK (op IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')),
  key_column  text        NOT NULL,
  row_key     text        NOT NULL,
  provenance  text        NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

-- TG_ARGV[0] names the table's business-key column.
CREATE FUNCTION ops.record_change() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE k text; s bigint;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN k := to_jsonb(OLD) ->> TG_ARGV[0];
  ELSE k := to_jsonb(NEW) ->> TG_ARGV[0]; END IF;
  INSERT INTO ops.change_events (table_name, op, key_column, row_key)
    VALUES (TG_TABLE_SCHEMA || '.' || TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP, TG_ARGV[0], COALESCE(k, ''))
    RETURNING seq INTO s;
  PERFORM pg_notify('face_ops_events', s::text);
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER shipments_change AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON ops.shipments
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ops.record_change('shipment_id');

GRANT SELECT ON ops.change_events TO face_reader;

Table and column names must be lower case. The listener reads ops.change_events and
listens on face_ops_events by default. To use other names, set two properties on the
connection: face.events.ledger (schema.table, lower case) and face.events.channel.
The ledger grows by one row per change, so delete old rows on your own schedule; the
listener only reads rows newer than the last one it saw.
Apache Kafka
Nothing to install. The listener reads the connection's topics (its Topics prefix
filter, or every non-internal topic) without a consumer group, so it never moves an
offset your own consumers depend on. It starts at each partition's latest offset: it
reports what is produced while it runs, not the topic's history. A Kafka event carries
its topic and record key; there is no row to read back, so the run's rule results cite
record keys.
Set up an event-triggered analysis
The listener has one switch: the briefs that run when its data changes. Saving an
active brief of that kind turns the connection's listener on; pausing or deleting the
last one on that connection turns it off.

Check the connection
In Settings › Integrations › Systems, the PostgreSQL connection must test green with
the login that will read it, and the ledger must be installed (above). A Kafka connection
needs nothing more. Both must meet the
security requirements.


Open a new brief
Open Briefs under Fetch in the rail and select CREATE NEW SCHEDULE. The
editor is titled New brief. Under What to ask, type the question each run asks,
for example one about freight billing, or pick one under
Start from a common question.


Choose When data changes
Under When, select When data changes. The time options give way to the event
settings.


Say which changes count

Listen to: the PostgreSQL or Kafka connection. Only those types are listed.
Run after this many events: for example 1 to analyse every change, or 5 for a
batch.
Wait for more events (seconds): so a burst of changes becomes one run.
At most one run every (minutes): the cooldown; never less than one minute.
Only tables or topics starting with: for example ops.freight_invoices; empty
means all.
Only this change: for example INSERT; Any change means all.

The note under these settings says what saving does: it turns the connection's data
listener on, on the managed runner, and installs nothing.
Under Where to look, tick the connections each run reads.


Save
Select Save brief. On Briefs, its card shows the EVENT chip beside ACTIVE,
and NEXT RUN reads On the next matching event.


Watch the listener
DATA LISTENERS heads the Briefs page, one row per connection: the state the
runner last reported (LISTENING, STARTING, DEGRADED, NOT LISTENING with the
reason, or OFF), how it reads, the events and bytes it read, how long it has
listened, and Metered to. Within about 15 seconds of saving, the row reads
LISTENING.


Read what the run found
When matching events arrive, the card's LAST TRIGGER shows how many events fired the
run and the first five of them (table or topic, operation, key), how many of their rows
were read back, the run's transaction id and its outcome. When the run's analysis
finishes, a few minutes later, RULE RESULTS FROM THESE CHANGES lists each rule the
triggering rows bear on: its verdict (Drift, Shadow, Missing or Aligned),
its id and category, and Rows: the keys of the rows it is about. The same rules
appear among the business rules on Why.



What an event-fired run reports
A brief that runs when data changes fires a fetch with the events that fired it (the first and the newest,
at most 25) and the connection that saw them. The runner reads back the rows those
events name, at most 50, with the connection's own login: a parameterised SELECT by
key on each table, and a key whose row is gone (deleted, or pruned since) is reported as
gone, never guessed. The analysis receives them as the changes that triggered the run
and gives each rule it finds the keys of the triggering rows it is about.
Only keys that really fired the run are kept: a key the analysis cites that was not a
triggering row is dropped, and a rule that cites none is not attributed to the run.
Each result is shown with the rows it rests on, so you can check it against the source.
An event-fired run never reuses an earlier answer to the same question: its subject is
the rows that fired it.
Usage counters
A listener's activity is counted, against the account of the person who created the
brief that switched it on:



Metric
Quantity




listener_events
events read


listener_seconds
seconds spent listening



Each record is written once: a repeated report or a restarted control plane never
records the same usage twice. Briefs shows the account next to Metered to, and the
bytes read. These counters are shown for your information; FACE does not charge by
usage.
The platform's own estate
The quickstart PostgreSQL that Runink hosts runs
with this ledger installed, and a transactional writer (the writer sidecar beside the
database) keeps the quickstart estate moving. Every row the writer produces carries its own ids (SO-9…, SHP-9…, SINV-9…,
CLM-9…) and a provenance column naming the quickstart estate.



Table
Rule its rows exercise
How often the writer breaks it




ops.freight_invoices
billed rate per mile equals the carrier's contract rate (the MySQL estate's freight.rate_contracts)
about 12% of invoices bill 8–18% over


ops.shipments
delivered by the planned time
about 15% of deliveries are late


ops.claims
filed within the contract's claim window (60, 90 or 120 days)
about 15% of claims are filed on a July 2026 shipment, past its window


ops.inventory_positions
on hand stays above the reorder point
order lines draw stock down and restocking lags, so a position sits below it for a while



Every 20 seconds the writer creates orders and their lines, ships, delivers and invoices
shipments, files claims and restocks low positions; most rows conform. A brief that runs
when data changes, asking about freight billing, filtered to ops.freight_invoices and INSERT, has an
off-contract invoice to find within minutes.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/telemetry/.title: Telemetry: MQTT, RFID, GPS, sensors
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/telemetry/.body:
Telemetry: MQTT, RFID, GPS, sensors

Four connectors read physical telemetry: a sensor bus, a tag reader, a fleet
tracker and a fixed probe gateway. Every protocol is implemented natively
against its wire format. MQTT 3.1.1 packets, LLRP inventory rounds and Modbus-TCP
register reads are written in FACE, with no third-party
protocol library. All four emit one row type, SensorReading.
You add these in Settings › Integrations › Systems. Once added, each one's card on
Ask opens its live view: Live sensors and Devices for MQTT, sensor gateways,
GPS and RFID. Every link must be encrypted: see each section below, and
Security requirements.
Plant equipment normally lives on private networks. Set allow_internal_network on
a connection to control whether it may reach internal addresses. The cloud
instance-metadata service is always refused. See Networking.
Common rules

An empty batch is not a success. A connector that connected and received
nothing returns Success=false with
 connector reached  and received no readings. A silent reader is
reported as silent, never as "no excursions".
Zero means "use the default" for every window and cap below. It never
means "collect nothing". Values above a maximum are reduced to the maximum.
Readings are sorted by observed time, then asset, then metric.
What Test does not establish. A successful probe does not establish that a
sensor is publishing, that an antenna is attached or aimed, that a probe is
calibrated, or that any readings exist.

MQTT (sensor bus)









Type spellings
mqtt, mqtts, iot, iothub, sensorbus, messagebus, iottelemetry (iot_telemetry)


Config message
MQTTConnectionConfig, or legacy IoTConnectionConfig with endpoint plus a comma-separated topics property


Protocol
MQTT 3.1.1 (protocol level 4): CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH/PUBACK, PING, DISCONNECT






Setting
Meaning




broker_url
tls://host:8883 (also ssl://, mqtts:// or wss://). Required to carry a TLS scheme. tcp://, mqtt://, ws:// and a bare host:port are refused.


topics
Topic filters. Required: an empty list is an error, and FACE never subscribes to # by default. A query can override the list with comma-separated filters.


qos
0 or 1 (FACE subscribes at QoS 1). 2 is refused.


client_id
The default is a stable id derived from the connection id


username
A setting. Required. The password is a credential.


collect_seconds
The listening window: default 15 s, maximum 5 min


max_messages
Default 500, maximum 20,000


protocol_version
4 or 0. 5 and 3 are refused with an explanation.


use_tls
Required on. The broker's certificate is always checked: insecure_skip_verify is refused.


property asset_topic_segment
The topic segment index that holds the asset id



Credentials: password (required); username may also come from the bundle.

Test dials the broker and completes CONNECT/CONNACK within 10 s, then
disconnects. It does not subscribe.
Execute subscribes, listens for the window, and decodes each message:
JSON objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and numeric strings become
readings.
When a JSON value names no metric, the metric comes from the topic's last
segment.
Non-JSON payloads are kept as rows with payload_kind and a short sample.
Topic, QoS and retained flags go into attributes.


The connector speaks MQTT 3.1.1 over TLS, at QoS 0 or 1, with a clean
session on every connect. A legacy iot connection that declares a non-MQTT protocol (such
as AMQP) is refused by name.
Explore returns supported=false. MQTT has no catalogue call.

RFID (LLRP and vendor REST)









Type spellings
rfid, epc, llrp, tagreader


Config message
RFIDConnectionConfig






Setting
Meaning




protocol
llrp (default, also llrps) or http (also https, rest)


endpoint
LLRP: host or host:5084. HTTP: the reader's event API base URL.


reader_id
Carried onto every reading. It defaults to the endpoint.


location
Where the reader physically is. It is carried onto every reading.


antenna_ports
Antennas to enable (1–65535). Empty means all.


collect_seconds
The inventory round: default 10 s, maximum 2 min


max_reads
Default 1,000, maximum 50,000


report_duplicates
Report every sighting instead of first/last seen per EPC


use_tls
TLS. It is also implied by https:// or llrps://. Required for LLRP: an LLRP link without TLS is refused. LLRP has no login of its own, so TLS is all the protocol offers.


property api_key_header
The header for an API key (default X-API-Key)



An HTTP reader's endpoint must be https://.
Credentials for HTTP readers, tried in order:

token → Authorization: Bearer
api_key → the API-key header
password with the username property → HTTP Basic

Test for LLRP connects and waits for the reader's connection-attempt event.
For HTTP, it makes one GET to the event API within 8 s.

Execute runs an inventory round and returns one reading per tag sighting.
EPC, antenna, RSSI and read count go into attributes when the reader states
them. HTTP event bodies are capped at 16 MiB, and an over-cap stream is refused
rather than reported as a short round.
Explore returns supported=false.

GPS and telematics









Type spellings
gps, telematics, eld, tracker


Config message
GPSConnectionConfig






Setting
Meaning




provider
samsara, geotab or generic_rest (also generic, rest, http, https). If it is empty and the endpoint is https://, generic_rest is used. The nmea provider (and the nmea type) is refused: it is a raw TCP stream with no encryption. Use the tracker's https API instead.


endpoint
A REST base URL, https://. Required.


asset_ids
Restrict to these vehicles or assets. A query may narrow further, but only within this set.


lookback_minutes
Default 60, maximum 7 days


include_sensors
Also request reefer and cargo sensor channels where the provider has them


property carrier / fleet
Carried onto readings



Credentials by provider:



Provider
Credentials




Samsara
api_key, token or bearer_token


Geotab
database, username, password (or session_id)


Generic REST
bearer_token / token, or api_key, or username + password




Test:
Samsara: one GET /fleet/vehicles/stats?types=gps&limit=1
Geotab: a Get of one Device
Generic REST: one request


Execute returns position fixes as readings (latitude, longitude,
geo_stated), with speed and heading in attributes. It also returns sensor
channels where requested.
At most 5,000 readings and 20 pages. Truncation is stated in the message.
REST bodies are capped at 8 MiB.
Units are taken from the provider (for example Geotab's unit-of-measure ids)
and never assumed.


Explore returns supported=false.

Sensor gateway (Modbus-TCP and HTTP)









Type spellings
sensorgateway (sensor_gateway), sensor, modbus, temperature, infrared, thermal, probe


Config message
SensorGatewayConnectionConfig with one or more SensorChannel






Setting
Meaning




transport
modbus_tcp (default) or http. mqtt is refused here: use an MQTT connection, which emits the same rows.


endpoint
Modbus: host:802, with use_tls on. HTTP: an https:// base URL.


unit_id
The Modbus unit (slave) id


channels
Required. There is no safe default register.


collect_seconds
The sampling pass: default 15 s, maximum 5 min


poll_interval_seconds
The interval between polls: default 5 s. It is carried as sampling_interval_seconds.


use_tls
Modbus/TCP Security. Required for Modbus: Modbus has no login of its own, so a gateway without TLS is refused.



Each SensorChannel states its own mapping:



Field
Meaning




asset_id, device_id
What is measured, and by which device


metric
temperature, infrared, humidity, shock, door or battery. It is written verbatim to the reading.


address
Modbus: the starting register. HTTP: the JSON path of the value.


register_type
holding (default), input, coil or discrete


data_type
int16 (default), uint16, int32, uint32 or float32. Word-swapped variants are accepted.


scale, offset
value = raw * scale + offset. A scale of 0 means 1.


unit
Written to the reading's unit, for example C, F, %RH or g


threshold_min / _stated, threshold_max / _stated, threshold_source
The band the product spec states, and where it is stated. Leave these unset when nobody stated one.



HTTP credentials: token, api_key, or username + password.

Test connects and reads the first channel. For HTTP, it fetches the
document and resolves the first channel's path. A failure names the channel,
register and unit. A Modbus exception response is reported as the device's own
refusal.
Execute polls every channel at the interval for the whole pass. The raw
register and count go into attributes.
Explore returns supported=false. Modbus has no register map, so the
channel list you configure is the schema.

The SensorReading row
Every telemetry connector, and the Flipper edge reader, returns
rows with these columns, in this order:



Column
Meaning




asset_id
The thing measured, for example REEFER-12


device_id
The thing measuring


reading_id, window_id
The reading id, and the monitoring run it belongs to


reference, carrier
Shipment or monitoring reference and carrier, only when the source states them


observed_at
RFC 3339, UTC


observed_at_source
Whose clock: device, gateway, or received (receipt time, used when the wire carries no timestamp)


metric, value, value_stated, unit
The measurement. value_stated=false marks a row with no numeric payload (a heartbeat, a door event, a tag sighting). Such rows are kept, because a gap in a feed is evidence too.


threshold_min, threshold_min_stated, threshold_max, threshold_max_stated, threshold_source
The band the source stated, and where


sampling_interval_seconds
The configured cadence. 0 means the source did not say.


max_excursion_minutes, max_excursion_minutes_stated
The excursion allowance stated by the spec


load_reference, load_value, load_value_stated, load_value_currency
The load on the asset, where named. load_value is money only with an ISO 4217 load_value_currency stated by the source; a load's weight (load_weight, payload_weight, net_weight, a numeric load) never fills it and is kept in attributes as load_weight / load_weight_field / load_weight_unit


location, latitude, longitude, geo_stated
Where the reading was taken


source, transport
The connection type and the protocol actually spoken


quality
The source's own quality flag. FACE never computes it.


attributes
Everything else the protocol knew, such as EPC and antenna, speed and heading, register and raw count, or topic



The *Stated fields
In the protocol format FACE uses, "the probe read 0 °C" and "the row has no
reading" look the same, and in a cold chain they are opposite facts. So every
connector sets a *_stated flag from whether the source carried the field,
never from whether the value is non-zero:

A threshold is never assumed. FACE does not assume 2–8 °C because an asset is
called REEFER. A band that no one stated stays unstated, and analysis reports
that the threshold was not stated.
A unit that is absent stays absent. FACE never assumes Celsius.
A position without geo_stated is not a position.

Consumers must read a value only when its *_stated flag is true. See
/docs/concepts/ for how these rows feed temperature-excursion
and claims evidence.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/logistics-.title: Logistics systems of record
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/logistics-.body:
Logistics systems of record

Order, transport, warehouse, yard and inventory management systems are read by
one REST implementation, parameterised by system. Across these systems, what
differs is the default resource and the vendor's paging and filter dialect. Those
differences are data, not separate connectors.
Systems and type spellings



System
Type spellings
Default resource
Changed-since parameter
Default lookback




OMS (orders)
oms, ordermanagement
orders

1,440 min


WMS (warehouse)
wms, warehousemanagement
inventory

240 min


WHS (warehouse receipts)
whs, warehouse

YMS (yard)
yms, yardmanagement
appointments
updatedSince
720 min


TMS (transport)
tms, transportmanagement
shipments

IMS (inventory)

inventory

UAS (drone fleet)

Generic
logisticsapi, logistics
from system
—
—



With the generic logisticsapi type, the system comes from the config's
system field. The default paging parameters are limit, offset and cursor.
Provider dialects
Setting provider changes the paging and changed-since parameters:



provider
Changed-since
Page size
Offset / cursor




project44
updatedAfter
perPage
offset


fourkites
since
page_size
page_token


manhattan

size
page


blue_yonder
