—


ibm_sterling
modifyTsFrom
maximumRecords
—


netsuite
lastModifiedDate
limit
offset


oracle
LastUpdateDate
limit
offset


generic or empty
the system's defaults




Settings (LogisticsAPIConnectionConfig)



Setting
Meaning




system
oms, wms, whs, yms, tms, ims (and the other systems above)


provider
The vendor dialect (see above)


base_url
An https:// URL. Required. http:// is refused, and so is a value with no scheme, which the connector would dial as http.


resource
The resource path to read. Empty uses the system default.


site_id
Warehouse, yard or DC scope


auth_mode
api_key (default), bearer, basic, oauth2_client_credentials or none


api_key_header
The API-key header. Default X-API-Key.


token_url, scope
For oauth2_client_credentials. token_url must be https://.


page_size
Default 200, maximum 1,000


max_records
Default 5,000, maximum 50,000


lookback_minutes
Changed-in window. Default is per system, maximum 90 days.



Older connections that were stored with the per-system messages
(OMSConnectionConfig, WHSConnectionConfig, TMSConnectionConfig,
YMSConnectionConfig, InventoryConnectionConfig) are still read:

Their base_url is used.
system_type or provider becomes the provider.
warehouse_id or yard_id becomes the site.

Every setting can also be given as a connection property (base_url, resource,
site_id, provider, auth_mode, …).
Credentials by auth_mode



auth_mode
Credential keys




api_key
api_key (also apikey, token, access_token), sent in api_key_header


bearer
token (also bearer_token, access_token, api_key)


basic
username and password


oauth2_client_credentials
client_id and client_secret. The token is cached until shortly before it expires.


none
—



Behaviour

Test requests the target resource with a page size of 1, within 15 s. A
success means the API answered and accepted the credential.
Execute pages through the resource:
Within the record cap, at most 200 pages, and a 3-minute budget.
Each page is capped at 16 MiB.
Redirects are followed on the same host only, up to 5.
Rows are the records as the API returns them. The columns are the union of
fields seen across the rows. An empty result is reported as
Success=false:  connector reached … and received no records.


Explore returns supported=false. These systems publish no common
catalogue.
Internal addresses. Set allow_internal_network to control whether the
connection may reach internal addresses.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/cctv-video.title: CCTV and video
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/cctv-video.body:
CCTV and video

A camera is a data source in FACE. It can be an IP camera or NVR over RTSPS, an
ONVIF device over HTTPS, an HTTPS feed, a video file, or the operator's own device
camera pushing frames. You add it in Settings › Integrations › Systems. Its card on
Ask then opens Surveillance, the live feed, with that camera already chosen.
The connector's job is reachability and description. Frame analysis happens in FACE's
vision pipeline (see /docs/concepts/).
Type spellings



Where
Spellings




Connector registry (Test, Explore)
cctv, videostream (video_stream, the "Video Stream" card), camera


Fetch routing
cctv, video_stream, videostream, camera, webcam



Settings (CctvConnectionConfig)



Setting
Meaning




endpoint_url
rtsps:// or https://, or a file path readable on the processing node. rtsp:// and http:// are refused, because they are unencrypted. Do not put credentials in the URL.


username
Camera username (a setting)


max_frames
Frames sampled per extraction. 0 means the server default, not "none".


transport
RTSP transport: tcp (default) or udp


device_capture
Marks a push source: the operator's device records frames and sends them to FACE. endpoint_url stays empty.



Credential: password. It answers RTSP Digest (preferred) or Basic challenges,
and ONVIF WS-Security UsernameToken with a password digest. It is never echoed,
logged or written into lineage.
Cameras live on site networks. Set allow_internal_network to control whether a
connection may reach internal addresses.
Test
Test on a camera connection, from Settings › Integrations › Systems, uses this
probe:



Endpoint
What Test does




rtsps://
TCP connect to the camera (5 s)


https://
One HEAD request with the credentials. 401/403 is reported as feed rejected the credentials (HTTP …).


File path
Checks that the file exists and is not a directory


Device capture
Validates the configuration. There is no server-side endpoint to dial. device_capture together with an endpoint_url is refused.



A successful probe says the camera accepted a connection. It does not say that
video is being published or that a frame will decode.
Explore: asking the camera what it is



Endpoint
Explore reads




rtsps://
Native RTSP OPTIONS + DESCRIBE (Accept: application/sdp). There is one dataset per media track, with codec, clock rate, packetisation and profile, plus resolution and frame rate where the camera states them, including from the H.264 parameter sets.


https:// (ONVIF)
ONVIF over SOAP 1.2: GetSystemDateAndTime, GetDeviceInformation, GetServices/GetCapabilities, GetProfiles, GetVideoSourceConfigurations and GetStreamUri. Each returned stream URI is then described over RTSP in the same call. You type a host and a credential, and FACE finds the streams.


File path, device capture
supported=false, with the reason



CCTVService.DescribeSource returns the same description for an ad-hoc endpoint.
Each reason repeats what a DESCRIBE does not establish:

that video is being published (an NVR describes a channel whose camera is
unplugged)
that the codec will decode on this deployment
that the scene is what you expect
that playback (SETUP/PLAY) will be allowed

ONVIF uses Media ver10. A device that serves profiles only on Media2 reports zero
profiles, and the reason says so. FACE does not multicast-probe your LAN
(WS-Discovery) and does not subscribe to events. Each camera is added by address.
Snapshots
When a camera supports ONVIF GetSnapshotUri, FACE can fetch a still with one
authenticated GET instead of decoding video. Only the path and query from
the device's answer are used. The host and port stay the ones on your
connection, so a device cannot redirect FACE to another address. The response
must validate as an image.
Frames: two paths



Path
RPC
What it does
What it leaves behind




Graded
SurveillanceService.IngestSurveillanceFeed (and a fetch's camera branch)
Samples or receives frames, then grades: object grading, material, damage, and evidence frames
One lineage record per ingest, evidence artefacts, observations


Live
SurveillanceService.DetectLiveFrame
One validated frame, boxes only.
Shown on Surveillance; not stored as an observation or evidence



A live answer carries box_origin = BOX_ORIGIN_LOCAL_DETECTOR, the detector's own
label, and no grade, material or damage fields. Its detection_note is never empty.
Frame limits

Accepted formats: JPEG and PNG (unsupported image format "…" (only jpeg/png accepted))
At most 12 MiB per frame, and 40 million pixels
The number of frames sampled from a feed per sweep is a deployment setting.

A camera connection's Execute has no tabular result and says so. Frames reach
analysis through the ingest path, not through SqlService.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/edge-flipp.title: Flipper edge reader
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/edge-flipp.body:
Flipper edge reader

The Flipper connector reads a handheld field reader: a Flipper Zero that an
operator carries on a yard walk, a dock inspection or a cold-store sweep. It
covers the places fixed telemetry does not reach, such as a third-party
crossdock, a trailer from a carrier who shares no feed, or an uninstrumented
freezer room.
You add the reader in Settings › Integrations › Systems. Its card on Ask then
opens Field reader, the live view, and Devices, the devices it reported, with
that reader already chosen.
Readings from a handheld are sparse and hand-initiated. A gap between two
readings means nobody was standing there, not that a feed dropped. FACE states a
cadence only when a sweep was configured with one.
How it connects
FACE does not talk to the device directly. It makes HTTPS requests to the edge
device agent (flipperd), which runs next to the Flipper and owns its serial or
USB link. Replugs, flat batteries and reboots are handled locally by the agent.









Type spellings
flipper, flipperzero, handheld, fieldreader


Settings (properties)
agent_url (also endpoint, url, base_url, host): the agent's https:// address. http:// is refused, and so is an address with no scheme, which the connector would dial as http.


Sweep context (properties, passed to the agent)
reader_id (device_id, reader), location (site), reference (shipment_reference), carrier, threshold_source, threshold_min, threshold_max, max_excursion_minutes


Credential
token (also api_key, agent_token), sent as Authorization: Bearer


Internal addresses
Controlled per connection with allow_internal_network (the agent is usually on a local network)



Behaviour

Test calls the agent's /healthz and succeeds only when the agent reports a
connected device. Otherwise the message says which layer failed: the agent is
running with no device, or the link is open but the device does not answer RPC.
Execute calls /readings with the sweep context. It returns
SensorReading rows exactly as the agent
reported them. Responses are capped at 1 MiB. An agent answer with
success: false is passed through as a failure.
Explore reads the agent's /capabilities catalogue.

What it will not fabricate
A Flipper Zero has no cargo thermometer. Its only onboard temperature is the
battery fuel gauge inside its own case. The agent reports that value as
reader_enclosure_temperature, and FACE never renames, rescales or reinterprets a
metric. A reading that measures the reader keeps saying so. Thresholds and their
*_stated flags are copied verbatim from what the operator stated for the sweep.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/web/.title: Web and crawler
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/web/.body:
Web and crawler

FACE reads the web in two ways:

a web connection reads one configured page as rows of text
the crawler service scrapes a page, or runs a bounded crawl from a seed URL

Web connection









Type spellings
webtelemetry (web_telemetry), webpage (the "Webpage" card), web, url, website


Settings (properties)
url (also endpoint, target_url, page_url, website, host)


Schemes
https only. http:// is refused, and a bare address is read as https.


Internal addresses
Refused unless allow_internal_network=true is set on the connection. Set it to read an intranet page.




Execute fetches exactly one page and follows no links:
30-second timeout, body capped at 8 MiB.
At most 5 redirects, on the same host only.
Only text and HTML are accepted. A document or image is refused, with a
pointer to the file path.
FACE extracts the readable text and splits it into chunks of up to 2,048
characters, with at most 400 chunks.


Rows have the columns url, final_url, fetched_at, http_status,
content_type, title, chunk_index, chunk_count, chunk_chars, content,
truncated, source and transport. truncated is true when the body or the
chunk count hit its cap.
Test fetches the page, reading at most 64 KiB, within 15 s, and applies the
same address and redirect rules.
Explore returns supported=false. The connector reads one page by design.

The request's User-Agent is Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RuninkFACE/1.0) unless
the deployment sets its own user agent.
Crawler service
CrawlerService exposes:



RPC
Behaviour




Scrape
Reads one url and returns its title, main content and metadata. render_js is reserved.


Crawl
Starts from url and visits linked pages, returning a crawl_id, a status and pages_visited.


GetCrawlStatus
Returns the pages of a crawl: url, title, content_snippet and status for each.



Crawl bounds:

url must be an absolute http(s) URL with a host.
depth: 0 means the default of 2. The maximum is 5, and a negative value is
refused.
limit (pages): 0 means the default of 10. The maximum is 500, and a
negative value is refused.
allow_external: false by default. The crawl then stays on the seed's host and
its subdomains, on the same port. Only http(s) links are followed.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/runners/.title: Runners
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/runners/.body:
Runners

A runner is the process that executes a fetch. It dials your sources, runs
the queries and reads the telemetry. The FACE control plane orchestrates, stores
connections and serves the FACE app, but it does not run fetches itself. You add,
edit and remove runners in Settings › Integrations › Runners. Each
fetch names a runner (runner_id), and a fetch with no runner is refused with
no runner is selected.
Kinds of runner



Kind
Where it runs
How the control plane reaches it




Managed runner (shown as Runink managed)
A dedicated FACE runner process beside the control plane, run by the platform
The control plane dials it over mutually authenticated TLS with the platform's rotating mesh identity. There is no plaintext fallback.


Registered runner
Any runner you add with an endpoint in Settings › Integrations › Runners
The control plane dials that endpoint. https:// endpoints use public TLS on port 443. All others use the mesh identity.


Self-hosted (enrolled) runner
Your machine, inside your network, behind NAT if needed
The runner dials out to FACE and holds one long-lived stream. Nothing dials in to it.



On the managed path, several runners can register themselves with the platform's
replicated registry by heartbeat. A tenant's fetches stick to one live runner so
its cache stays warm, and a newly added runner starts receiving work with no
configuration change.
Why data can stay in your network
A self-hosted runner runs the whole fetch pipeline in-process on your
machine. It dials your warehouses, APIs, readers and cameras from inside your
network, and only the fetch result travels back over its outbound stream.
Your sources never need an inbound firewall rule, a public address, or
reachability from the FACE platform. Because the runner makes the connection,
the two ends do not need to share an address family either.
Enrolling a self-hosted runner
Enrolment uses RunnerEnrollmentService.Enroll, one bidirectional stream:

Get a credential. An organisation admin mints a service-account key
for their own tenant (IdentityService.GenerateServiceAccountKey). Only a
service-account credential can enrol a runner. A person's session, even an
admin's, is refused with
runner enrolment requires a service-account credential; a user session token cannot enrol a runner.
Configure the runner. It needs these environment variables:
| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RUNNER_ENROLL_ADDR | The FACE gRPC address as the runner can reach it. Setting it turns enrolment on. |
| RUNNER_ENROLL_TOKEN | The service-account token. It is required whenever the address is set, and the runner refuses to start without it. |
| RUNNER_ID | A stable id kept across restarts, so a reconnect reuses the same slot. Up to 64 characters from A–Z a–z 0–9 - _ .. It is generated when empty. |
| RUNNER_NAME, RUNNER_VERSION | Display only |
| RUNNER_ENROLL_TLS | TLS with system roots, always. false is refused: the runner logs Runner enrolment refused: RUNNER_ENROLL_TLS=false is not supported and does not enrol, because the stream carries a service-account token. Terminate TLS in front of the control plane instead. |

Say hello. The first message must be RunnerHello with runner_id,
name, version, capabilities (for example fetch) and load_score.
Any other first message is refused.

Get accepted. FACE answers with EnrollmentAccepted:
runner_id: the tenant-namespaced id.
tenant_id: taken from the verified token, never from the hello, so a
runner cannot enrol into a tenant it holds no credential for.
heartbeat_interval_seconds (15).


Do the work. FACE pushes RunnerWorkAssignment messages, each with a
dispatch_id and a RunFetchRequest. The runner answers with a
RunnerWorkResult carrying the same dispatch_id and either a
RunFetchResponse or an error. A result for an unknown dispatch is dropped.
Heartbeat. RunnerHeartbeat messages update load_score.
Disconnect. Closing the stream de-registers the runner. A runner that
re-enrols with the same id replaces its previous stream. If the stream ends,
the runner reconnects after 5 seconds.

A fetch for a tenant that has an enrolled runner is dispatched down that runner's
stream. The control plane waits up to 10 minutes for the result. If none
arrives, it reports
runner "…" accepted the work and has not answered within 10m0s — the run may still be in progress there.
It does not retry the work on control-plane compute.
Enrolled runners are listed only to their own tenant. A runner's name,
version and capabilities are its own statements, and FACE does not verify them.
Credentials on a runner
For the managed runner, the control plane reads a connection's credential bundle
once for each dispatch (an audited read). It then seals the bundle to the
runner's in-memory key under that dispatch's context. The runner:

opens the bundle only for a verified mesh peer
uses it for that fetch
never writes it to disk or logs it

A restarted runner has a new key, so earlier sealed blobs cannot be opened. See
/docs/architecture/security/.
Health

List. ListRunners always lists the managed runner. Its state is
RUNNING only when a live heartbeat is in the replicated registry. Otherwise it
is UNKNOWN, with a description that says liveness was not observed.
compute_units is 0 when capacity is not measured.
Process health. GetRunnerHealth reports the answering process's CPU,
memory and goroutine count. Any metric it does not measure is named in
unmeasured instead of being reported as zero.

Keeping fetches off the control plane
A deployment can require runner isolation (ask Runink), so that a SQL fetch fails rather than falls
back to the control plane when the runner cannot be reached. The failure reads
…: runner isolation enforced but runner unreachable — refusing control-plane execution for ….
The refusal appears on the fetch response as a notice as well as an error.
Warehouse runner settings
Snowflake and Databricks connections can carry runner-deploy settings, such as a
compute pool, image, network rule, cluster policy, node type or artifact
checksum (see SQL warehouses). FACE stores and
format-checks them when the connection is saved:

A value that looks like a credential is refused.
runner_artifact must not contain a .. segment.
runner_artifact and runner_artifact_sha256 must be given together.

An organisation admin can deploy, redeploy and decommission runners from
Settings › Integrations › Runners
(see Runner deployment).
Snowflake and Databricks targets are offered only when FACE's runner channel is configured,
because those runners connect out to FACE. Without it, the tab lists them as unavailable and
says why.

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/networking.title: Networking and address policy
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/networking.body:
Networking and address policy

IPv6 first, IPv4 fully supported
The Runink platform is IPv6-first, and many data platforms are still reachable
only over IPv4. FACE supports both, so no connector pins an address family.

TCP dials use Happy Eyeballs (RFC 8305). This covers the HTTP-based
connectors, the raw-socket protocols (MQTT, LLRP, Modbus, NMEA, Kafka, RTSP),
the Snowflake and Databricks transports, and the PostgreSQL and MySQL drivers.
When a name resolves to both IPv6 and IPv4 addresses, FACE races them and uses
whichever connects first.
gRPC dials (control plane to runner) try addresses in order. They follow
RFC 6724 preference, so IPv6 comes first, and fall back to the next address
after a connect timeout. They do not race.
Reaching IPv4-only services from an IPv6-only network needs NAT64 or an
equivalent egress path. That is a deployment concern, not a connector setting.
See /docs/admin-guide/deployment/.

Writing addresses

IPv6 literals need brackets when a port is given: [2001:db8::10]:5432,
rtsps://[2001:db8::20]:322/stream, tls://[2001:db8::30]:8883.
A bare IPv6 literal without a port is also accepted where a connector
applies a default port. FACE detects "has a port" by parsing, not by looking for
a colon, so 2001:db8::10 gets the default port appended and bracketed
correctly.
Default ports:
| Protocol | Default port |
|---|---|
| PostgreSQL | 5432 |
| MySQL | 3306 |
| MQTT over TLS | 8883 |
| LLRP | 5084 |
| Modbus-TCP over TLS | 802 |
| Kafka | 9092 |
| RTSPS | state the port in the URL |
| Databricks | 443 |
| Runner https:// endpoint | 443 |

Every address must use an encrypted transport. Cleartext schemes such as http://,
tcp://, mqtt:// and rtsp:// are refused. See
Security requirements.

A URL must not contain credentials (user:pass@). Connectors that parse URLs
refuse them and ask you to store the credential on the connection instead.

Connector address policy
Connectors dial addresses that people type into a form. To stop those addresses
from reaching the platform's own internals, outbound connections are checked
against an egress policy on the address actually being connected to, after DNS
resolution. The policy blocks internal and cloud metadata addresses unless an
operator explicitly allows a connection to reach internal addresses; the cloud
instance-metadata service is never a data source.
Allowing internal addresses on a connection
A connection whose source genuinely sits inside your network, such as a reader or
gateway on the plant network, can be allowed to reach internal addresses with the
property allow_internal_network (also accepted: allow_private_network,
allow_internal). Use true or false. When an address is refused, the message
names the property:
refusing to reach 10.1.2.3: it resolves to a private address, which is inside this deployment's own network rather than on the public internet. If that is genuinely the source you mean, set `allow_internal_network=true` on this connection

Redirects and proxies

Redirects. HTTP connectors follow redirects only to the same host. A
redirect to another host is refused, so a credential sent to the source you
named is never replayed to a different one:
refusing to follow a redirect from … to ….
Proxies. Connector HTTP clients use no proxy, so the address that is
checked is the address that is connected to.

Timeouts and body caps
Every connector bounds its dial, its handshake and its response body. Over-cap
responses are refused rather than read short. See each connector page for its
figures. When a body exceeds its cap, the message is:
… returned more than N bytes: refusing to report a partially-read answer as a complete one — narrow the request (a shorter collection window, a smaller page size, a single resource) or point the connection at an endpoint that pages

docs/admin-guide/data-sources/troublesho.title: Troubleshooting
docs/admin-guide/data-sources/troublesho.body:
Troubleshooting

These are the messages FACE connectors actually return, grouped by where you see
them. An ellipsis (…) stands for a value the message fills in.
Test says "Configuration saved", with no green tick
Configuration saved — a live connectivity check isn't implemented yet for this source type
This is not a failure. The configuration is stored, and live_check_performed is
false because the type has no live probe (SAP). For SAP, use Explore, which reaches
the service. See
Connections and credentials.
Security refusals



Message
Cause
What to do




this connection cannot be saved without its security settings: …
The connection would send data or a credential unencrypted, skip the certificate check, or lacks a required login. Each problem after the colon names the setting or credential.
Set what each problem names. See Security requirements.


this connection is not secured: …; open it in Settings › Integrations and upgrade its security
A stored connection fails the policy, so every read of it is refused
Open it in Settings › Integrations › Systems and use Upgrade security


nothing was dialled: …
Test on a draft that would be refused
Fix the settings it names, then Test again


FACE has no security rule for connector type "…", so it cannot be used
The type has no security rule
Use a supported connector type



Connection and credentials



Message
Cause
What to do




Unknown connection type "…"
The type matches no connector after lowercasing and removing spaces, underscores and hyphens
Use a spelling from the connector pages. Google Workspace types (gmail, google_sheets) are read by fetch only.


Connection not found
The id is no longer stored, for example after a stale list
Refresh the list


snowflake connection "…" has no password (or programmatic access token) in its credential store: …
The credential bundle has no password, pat or token
Re-enter the password in the connection form. A password on the record itself is never read.


databricks connection "…" has no personal access token in its credential store: …
No personal_access_token in the bundle
Re-enter the token


databricks connection "…" names no HTTP path: …
http_path is empty
Copy the /sql/1.0/warehouses/… path from the warehouse's connection details


ssl_mode … can send data unencrypted or ssl_mode is not set
disable, prefer and allow can send data without TLS, and an unset mode cannot be audited
Set require, verify-ca or verify-full


CREDENTIAL_STATE_ABSENT on the list
This node holds no credential bundle for the connection
Re-enter the credential. The state cannot tell "never entered" from "not on this node".


CREDENTIAL_STATE_UNREADABLE on the list
A bundle exists but cannot be opened
This is a key or storage problem on the instance, and re-entering the credential will not fix it. See /docs/admin-guide/deployment/.



Fetch



Message
Cause
What to do




No data source was selected. Choose at least one configured source …
The fetch named no connection. FACE reads only the sources you select and never fills in other data.
Include at least one connection on Ask (or tick one in the brief), or name one in the request


None of the … selected data source(s) could be processed.
Every selected connection was skipped or failed. The message lists each reason after Errors encountered:.
Fix the reason given for each connection, for example a missing credential or a connection with no runner



Network



Message
Cause
What to do




refusing to reach …: it resolves to a … address, which is inside this deployment's own network …
The connection is not allowed to reach internal addresses
If the source really is internal, set allow_internal_network=true on the connection


refusing to dial …: that is the cloud instance-metadata service, not a data source. This refusal has no opt-in
The address is the metadata service
Correct the address. There is no override.


refusing to dial multicast address … — a data source has one server
Multicast target
Use the source's unicast address


refusing to follow a redirect from … to …: …
The source redirected to a different host
Point the connection at the final host directly


stopped after 5 redirects
Redirect loop
Use the final URL


… returned more than N bytes: refusing to report a partially-read answer as a complete one — …
The response exceeded the connector's cap
Narrow the request: a shorter window, a smaller page_size, one resource



SQL



Message
Cause
What to do




only read-only queries (…) are allowed
The statement is not a read
Send a read-only statement


query contains restricted keywords
The statement could change data
Remove the write or DDL clause


this query is a batch of N statements and M bound parameter(s) were supplied: …
Parameters were sent with a multi-statement query
Send one statement with its parameters


… read N row(s): K of M statement(s) were refused by the engine and their rows are NOT in this result; …
Some statements in the batch failed, usually on grants
Grant the role access, or drop those statements



SaaS and ERP



Message
Cause
What to do




salesforce authentication failed: token endpoint returned 400: …
The OAuth username–password flow was rejected
Check client_id, client_secret, the password plus security_token, and whether the connected app allows this flow


no SOQL to run. …
A fetch reached Salesforce with no soql property
Set soql on the connection


`api_version` must look like v60.0; got "…" …
Malformed api_version
Use vNN.N


no Guidewire resource to read. …
No route configured
Set resource. Explore lists every route the installation declares.


this connection carries a Guidewire username but no password. …
The bundle has no password
Re-enter it


this SAP connection does not say where its OData service is, …
No odata_url property
Set odata_url to the service root, or sap_gateway_url to enumerate the Gateway's catalogue


SAP connector for system … cannot READ rows yet: …
A fetch was run against an SAP connection. SAP connections serve metadata.
Use Explore for SAP metadata


invalid ServiceNow connection parameters (systemUrl required)
Missing systemUrl property
Set it to the instance URL



Files and object storage



Message
Cause
What to do




missing S3 credentials: provide access_key and secret_key
Incomplete bundle
Add both keys


bucket "…" does not exist at …, or these credentials cannot see it
Wrong bucket, or no list permission
Check the name and the policy


reading objects is wired for S3-compatible stores only; …
An object read from a GCS or Azure connection. Object reads use S3-compatible stores.
Use an S3-compatible endpoint for object reads


no object key given: pass the key to read as the query
Execute was called without a key
Pass the object key as the query


"…" is not an .xlsx/.xlsm file — use the CSV format for delimited text
Excel connection pointed at another format
Use an object-store connection for CSV



Streaming and telemetry



Message
Cause
What to do




kafka extraction …
A fetch was run against a Kafka connection. Kafka connections serve the topic catalogue.
Use Explore for the topic catalogue


no bootstrap server answered: …
No broker completed the handshake
Check addresses, security_protocol and SASL settings


sasl_mechanism "…" is not allowed: set it to scram-sha-512 or scram-sha-256
Only SCRAM is accepted
Use scram-sha-512 or scram-sha-256 over sasl_ssl, on a listener that offers it


SCRAM server signature does not verify: …
The broker accepted the proof but could not prove it holds the credential
The peer is not the broker the credential was created on: check bootstrap_servers and the listener


TLS handshake with broker … failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
The broker's certificate is from a private CA
Paste that CA's certificate into ssl_ca_pem


no topics configured for broker …: …
The MQTT topics list is empty
List the topic filters to read. FACE never defaults to #.


broker_url has no TLS scheme: … or broker_url uses …://, which is unencrypted
The MQTT broker address is not TLS
Use the broker's tls://, ssl://, mqtts:// or wss:// listener, with use_tls on


qos 2 is configured but …: set qos to 0 or 1
QoS 2 is configured. The connector delivers at QoS 0 and 1.
Use QoS 0 or 1


 connector reached … and received no readings
Connected, but nothing arrived in the window
Check that devices are publishing, and lengthen collect_seconds


rfid: no endpoint configured: …
Reader address missing
Set endpoint


gps connection has no provider: expected one of samsara, geotab, generic_rest, nmea
No provider set on a non-URL endpoint
Set provider to samsara, geotab or generic_rest. nmea is refused (next row).


provider nmea is a raw TCP stream with no encryption, so FACE cannot secure it: …
An NMEA connection
Use the tracker's https API (generic_rest) instead


sensor gateway transport is "mqtt", which this connector does not serve: …
MQTT configured on a gateway connection
Create an mqtt connection instead


gateway at … accepted the connection but reading channel "…" (asset …, register … on unit …) failed: …
Wrong register, unit id or register type
Check the channel's address, register_type and unit_id against the gateway's register map


… connection is configured for API-key auth but no key is stored: …
Logistics API with no api_key credential
Add the key, or change auth_mode



Cameras and edge



Message
Cause
What to do




cannot reach RTSP feed at …: …
The camera did not accept a TCP connection
Check the host, the rtsps:// port and the network path


feed rejected the credentials (HTTP 401)
Wrong camera credentials
Re-enter the username and password


device_capture is set but endpoint_url is also "…": choose one — …
Both push and pull are configured
Clear one of them


unsupported image format "…" (only jpeg/png accepted)
A pushed frame is not JPEG or PNG
Send JPEG or PNG


the Flipper agent at … is running but has no device: …
The agent is up with no Flipper attached
Connect and power on the device

docs/admin-guide/deployment/.title: Deployment
docs/admin-guide/deployment/.body:
Deployment

Runink deploys, configures, upgrades and monitors FACE for you. FACE runs on the Runink
platform layer, which ships with FACE: you do not buy Runink TIDDE (Trusted Intelligence for Developer & Data Experience)
separately, and there is no
infrastructure for a customer admin to configure in the app.
Where FACE can run



Placement
Where the work runs
Where your data is processed




Trial
Runink's machines
On Runink's machines; you are told so when access is granted


Managed by Runink
Runink's machines
On Runink's machines


In your cloud
Your own cloud account
In your account


On your premises
Your own servers
On your site


Air-gapped
A server on your site with no outside connection
On your site; updates arrive as signed offline bundles



Which placements are offered, and their prices, are on the FACE product page at
runink.org. There is no Google Cloud Marketplace
listing yet.
What stays the same everywhere

No outside AI service. Every model call goes to the inference plane of the
placement; see Sovereign models.
Reads happen on runners. The managed runner reads sources the platform can reach;
a self-hosted runner in your network reads sources behind your firewall and dials out
to FACE. See Runners.
Fails closed. FACE refuses to start without its encryption key, its mesh identity
or its inference endpoint, rather than run in a degraded mode.
Licence. Runink issues the licence for your instance. An expired or invalid
licence refuses every call; a trial past its 14 days becomes read-only.

Getting help
Health, upgrades and backups are Runink's job. For an incident, contact your Runink
contact; for a security report, write to security@runink.org.

docs/developer-guide/.title: Developer guide
docs/developer-guide/.body:
Developer guide

FACE is a gRPC API first. The FACE app uses the same public services described in the
API reference, so anything a person does in the app an integration can do too,
under the same roles and the same approval gate. FACE is proprietary: you build on
it through the API and its connectors, not by changing its code.
What you can build on



Surface
What it is for
Status




gRPC API
Every service and method: connections, fetches, analysis, twins and decisions, compliance, vision, identity. Reachable as gRPC or gRPC-web on the instance's address, with a bearer session.
Available


Connector model
How a data source is described, tested, explored and read, and what to send to add one.
Available


Events and briefs
Event-triggered and scheduled questions over your sources. See Event listeners and Briefs.
Available


SDKs, MCP tools, plugins
None published. FACE's diagnostics MCP server is internal to the process and not reachable by customers.
Not yet available



The data model in one paragraph
A connection describes one source (its type, address and settings) with its
credentials stored apart and never returned. A run reads selected connections and
returns an answer, the analysis behind it and the decisions the twins drafted. A
decision becomes an action card with typed artifacts (an email draft, a claim, an
order) and, where one applies, an evidence document built only from cited records.
Approving or rejecting a card is a separate call, checked against the card's approval rule and recorded. The
Concepts section defines each term.
Services not yet in the reference
These services exist in the API but have no reference page yet:
StoreInterestService (store interest aggregates and layout proposals),
SupplierPortalService (the supplier portal) and LoopService (read-only report of
FACE's agent loops, for admins).

docs/developer-guide/connector-model/.title: Connector model
docs/developer-guide/connector-model/.body:
Connector model

Every data source FACE reads goes through one connector model. A connector is code in
FACE; a connection is your configuration of one. You add and manage connections
through ConfigService (or the app's connection wizard); you do not write connectors.
What every connector does



Step
RPC
What happens




Describe
CreateConnection, UpdateConnection
A connection names its type and its typed config message. Secret-valued fields go to the sealed credential store and come back empty on read.


Test
TestConnection
Opens the source with its stored credential, read-only and time-limited, and reads nothing. Read success and live_check_performed: a type with no live probe says so instead of claiming success.


Explore
ExploreConnection
The source describes what it holds (schemas, tables, topics, folders) without FACE being told its data model. A source with no catalogue says it cannot, rather than returning an empty list.


Read
A fetch (FetchService)
A runner reads the selected connections with driver-prepared, bound queries; FACE builds no SQL from model text. Every read is recorded on the data-lineage log, as structure only, never values.



Rules every connector keeps

Read-only. No connector writes to a source.
Secure transport. Every connection must use TLS or the source's own secure
protocol; FACE offers no plaintext connector. See
Network egress.
Stated, not inferred. A field the source did not carry is marked as not stated;
an empty read is a failure, never "nothing found".
Credentials never come from the server. A connector reads only its own
connection's sealed credentials.

The catalogue
The supported connection types and their configuration fields are listed in the
Connections API and, with a downloadable quickstart dataset for
most of them, in Data sources. To ask for a new
connection type, contact Runink.

docs/developer-guide/api/.title: gRPC API reference
docs/developer-guide/api/.body:
gRPC API reference

FACE is a gRPC API first. The FACE app uses the same public services described here, so any
action in the app can also be done by an integration. This section is the reference for that
API: how to connect and authenticate, the conventions every service follows, and one page per
domain listing each RPC with its messages, fields and errors.
The reference comes from the .proto definitions and the server implementation. Where the two
disagree, the page describes what the server does.
At a glance









Protobuf package
semantics.v1


API version
1.0.0 (see Versioning)


Transports
Native gRPC over HTTP/2 with TLS; gRPC-web for browsers


Authentication
authorization: Bearer  metadata on every call except two


Services
The protos define 41 services with 227 RPCs. These pages document 30 services and 115 RPCs in full. The rest are listed by name in Not yet documented here, and the internal ones in Internal services.



Domains

Identity, licences & landing: Login, sessions, TOTP, service-account keys, licence validation, dashboard.
Configuration, connections & runners: Data-source connections, runners, integrations, runner enrolment.
Fetch & traces: Run the fetch pipeline, stream progress, read traces and SOPs.
Twins, simulation & claims: Digital twins, action queue, hypotheses, claims triage.
Analysis, posture & rules: Statistical analysis, estate posture, rule reconciliation.
Compliance, finance & operations: Domain analyses and remediation routing.
SQL: Read-only SQL against configured engines.
Lineage & activity: What each source delivered; live agent activity.
CCTV, surveillance & documents: Camera sources, evidence frames, OCR, material analytics.
Calling & support: Call signalling and the support log.
Agent orchestrator: The streamed agent loop and its tool gate.
Metering & schedules: Compute usage and budgets; briefs (recurring fetch schedules).
Crawler, metasearch & CRM: Sovereign crawl and search, bias rules, HubSpot.

Connecting
Connect to your FACE instance through the platform edge, over TLS. The edge address is the
host name your instance is published at. This reference uses the placeholder
face.example.internal:443. Both transports reach the same services on that address:

Native gRPC (HTTP/2 + TLS). Use this for server-to-server integrations, runners and
command-line tools. It is the only transport for client-streaming and bidirectional RPCs.
gRPC-web. Use this for browser clients. The FACE app is a gRPC-web client served from
the same origin as the API, and it sends the same bearer token as any other client. gRPC-web
carries unary and server-streaming RPCs only.

The FACE app also sends an x-agent-trace-id metadata header on every call. The value is a
random id minted once per app session. ActivityService uses it to scope a subscription to
the runs that session started (see Lineage & activity).
Other clients may send their own id or omit the header.

Note: Do not build a client on server reflection. It is restricted to platform-internal callers.
Build your client from the published .proto files instead (see
Getting the protos).

Authentication
Every RPC requires a session token in the authorization metadata, except these two:



RPC
Why it is open




semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login
It is how a session is obtained.


semantics.v1.ActivationService/ValidateLicense
It checks a licence before anyone can sign in.



Nothing else is exempt, including the landing dashboard. Server reflection is not bearer-token
authenticated, but it answers only verified mutual-TLS mesh peers. Any other caller gets
UNAUTHENTICATED (server reflection requires a verified mTLS peer). It is not an anonymous
surface.
Getting a token. Call IdentityService/Login
with one of these methods:

Email and password, followed by a TOTP code if the account has two-factor enabled.
An OIDC ID token from the identity provider configured for your deployment. The email in
the token must be verified and must be on the deployment's allowlist.

A successful login returns a signed session token that is valid for 12 hours. Send it on every
call:
authorization: Bearer 

Sessions are checked against the server's session store on every request. A token that was
revoked by Logout, or by an admin changing the account, stops working within seconds on every
replica.
Machine clients. An org admin can mint a service-account token with
GenerateServiceAccountKey.
It is valid for 365 days and scoped to the admin's tenant. Store it as a secret.
Tenant scope. The tenant comes from the verified session, never from a request field. A
request field that names a tenant is accepted only when it matches the session's tenant.
Roles

Summary

Every RPC except the admin-only ones.

Only the RPCs that change nothing and dial no customer source. A reader cannot run a fetch.


ROLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT

One role table for the whole API. Every semantics.v1 RPC has a least role, checked before
the handler runs. An RPC with no entry in that table is refused, so nothing ships ungated. A
refusal is PERMISSION_DENIED with this action needs the editor or admin role on this instance
or this action needs the admin role on this instance. Every RPC not listed below is open to any

Gated by the handler itself: IdentityService/UpdateUser (org admin only), RalphOrchestratorService/ExecuteLoop (each tool the loop calls is gated
on its own), RunnerEnrollmentService/Enroll (service accounts only), and
FetchService/GetDispatchKey, ApplyDataListener and ListDataListeners (verified mesh peers
only).
Further checks apply across the whole API:

Service accounts, on unary calls, are refused on every ConfigService RPC except
ListRunners and ListConnections, on all of ActivationService, on every IdentityService
RPC, on member and role management, and on messages and calls to people. On streaming calls
they are refused on all ConfigService, ActivationService and IdentityService streams and
on member and role management.
An unrecognised role grants nothing. The session is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED.
Subscription tier. On a TRIAL, ConfigService/CreateDatabricksCluster is refused with
PERMISSION_DENIED.
Licence. When the deployment has a licence configured and it is expired or invalid, every
authenticated call fails with PERMISSION_DENIED (license expired or invalid).

Status codes
FACE uses standard gRPC status codes. The grpc-message text is written for people, and the
FACE app shows it verbatim for refusals. Clients may show it too, but should branch on the code.



Code
When FACE returns it




UNAUTHENTICATED
No authorization metadata, or a token that is malformed, expired, revoked or not issued by this deployment. Sign in again.


PERMISSION_DENIED
The session is valid but not allowed: wrong role, service-account restriction, subscription tier, another tenant's resource, or an expired licence.


INVALID_ARGUMENT
A required field is missing or a value is malformed.


FAILED_PRECONDITION
The request is well formed but the instance cannot serve it yet. Typical causes: no data source is connected, the sovereign model plane is not configured, or a required integration is not set up. Fix the configuration and retry.


NOT_FOUND
The named record, trace, connection or schedule does not exist for this tenant.


DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
A runner accepted dispatched work but did not answer in time. The run may still be in progress on the runner, so this does not mean it failed.


RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
The caller exceeded the per-user rate limit (on by default), or a budget or size limit. Back off and retry.


UNIMPLEMENTED
The RPC is defined in the protos but this server does not serve it. This reference lists the RPCs the server serves.


UNAVAILABLE
A dependency, such as a runner or the model plane, is temporarily unreachable. Safe to retry with backoff.


INTERNAL
The server failed. Nothing is claimed to have happened.



Many RPCs also report an expected refusal in the response body (success: false plus
message) instead of an error. Each RPC's section says which style it uses.
When an optional field is absent, report it as not measured.
Streaming



Kind
RPCs
Transports




Server streaming
FetchService/RunFetchStream, TwinsService/StreamTwins, TwinsService/UploadAnalyze, HypothesisService/SimulateScenario, SurveillanceService/SubscribeTelemetry, ActivityService/SubscribeAgentActivity, RalphOrchestratorService/ExecuteLoop, LiveSensorService/StreamReadings, SensorTelemetryService/StreamSensorReadings, MapFeatureService/StreamMapFeatures
Native gRPC and gRPC-web


Bidirectional streaming
HypothesisService/InteractiveSimulate, RunnerEnrollmentService/Enroll, FetchService/Talk
Native gRPC only



Streams are authenticated once, when they open, with the same bearer token and the same rules as
unary calls. A long-lived stream therefore keeps running after its token expires. Re-open it with
a fresh token when you reconnect. Set a deadline (grpc-timeout) on unary calls and reconnect
server streams with backoff.
Versioning
The protos form one module with one version, currently 1.0.0. The build lints the module
with buf and runs a breaking-change check against the previous release. A change that breaks
the wire format or generated code is rejected unless it is explicitly listed as an exception,
with the reason recorded. Additive changes (new fields, RPCs and enum values) arrive without
notice. Clients should ignore unknown fields and treat unknown enum values as unspecified.
Where a field has been retired, its number and name are reserved, so they are never reused
with another meaning. Deprecated RPCs keep working for at least one release and are marked on
their pages.
Getting the protos
The .proto files are provided with the platform. The module is semantics/v1/*.proto under a
buf module root. It imports:

google/protobuf/timestamp.proto (well-known types), and
runink/ui/judgement/v1/judgement.proto, the platform's shared judgement types, which ship
with the FACE protos.

Generate clients with buf generate or protoc for your language. All messages use proto3.
Worked example
This example signs in with grpcurl, then makes an authenticated call. grpcurl reads the
protos from disk rather than using reflection. Run it from the directory that holds the proto
module root (semantics/) and the shared runink/ import tree.
1. Sign in
grpcurl \
  -import-path . \
  -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \
  -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS",
       "username": "analyst@example.com",
       "password": "'"$PASSWORD"'"}' \
  face.example.internal:443 \
  semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login

A successful response:
{
  "status": "STATUS_SUCCESS",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
  "message": "Authentication Successful"
}

If the account has two-factor enabled, the response is STATUS_MFA_REQUIRED with an
mfaSession. Send it back within 5 minutes:
grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \
  -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY",
       "mfaSession": "'"$MFA_SESSION"'", "mfaCode": "123456"}' \
  face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login

2. Authenticated call
TOKEN=$(grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \
  -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS", "username": "analyst@example.com",
       "password": "'"$PASSWORD"'"}' \
  face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login | jq -r .token)

grpcurl \
  -import-path . \
  -proto semantics/v1/face.proto \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{}' \
  face.example.internal:443 \
  semantics.v1.LandingService/GetDashboardStats

Without the header, the same call fails:
ERROR:
  Code: Unauthenticated
  Message: authorization token is not provided

3. Sign out
grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{}' \
  face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Logout

This ends every session of the account, not only this one.
grpcurl prints and accepts JSON field names in lowerCamelCase (mfaSession), and it also
accepts the proto names (mfa_session). Keep passwords and tokens out of your shell history.
The example reads them from environment variables.
Shared types
Judgement
runink.ui.judgement.v1.Judgement is the platform's verdict on one claim, usually an action
an agent proposed. It appears in fetch results, action cards and the orchestrator stream.



Field
Type
Description

Verdict
The verdict.

string
Stable reason code.

string
The sentence a person can act on. Render it as text, never as markup.


basis
Basis
The basis recorded for this verdict (informational).

string
What was judged, as a person reads it: the action or card title.


claim
string
The claim judged about the subject.


accepted
bool
false means the verdict was a dissent and the action was removed from the answer.


judged_at
google.protobuf.Timestamp
When the judgement ran. Unset means not recorded. It never means "now".


ref

Where the action sat in the answer, for example decisions[0].

int32
How many evidence items were weighed.

int32
0 for the first answer. 1 and higher for answers the agent loop revised.


verdict_text
string
The verdict spelled out verbatim. Show it when verdict is VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED.



JudgementSet
Every verdict from one run, accepted and rejected, with the server's counts.



Field
Type
Description

repeated Judgement
The verdicts. This may be one page of a longer list.

Use the counts as sent. Do not recompute them from judgements.
Verdict



Value
Meaning

Not judged, or a verdict this enum does not know. Show verdict_text.


VERDICT_CONCUR
The evidence supports the claim.


VERDICT_DISSENT
The evidence contradicts the claim. reason_code names what.

The evidence is absent, unreadable or does not bear on the claim. Never agreement.


VERDICT_OUT_OF_SCOPE

Basis



Value
Meaning

The basis recorded for this verdict (informational).

The basis recorded for this verdict (informational).


BASIS_MODEL
The basis recorded for this verdict (informational).



Internal services
semantics.v1.ModelService (Generate, GenerateStream, SynthesizeSpeech,
SpeakFetchSummary, and the deprecated Embedding, which answers Unimplemented) is FACE's
internal interface to its own sovereign model plane. It accepts calls only from the FACE process
itself (loopback plus a verified mesh mTLS identity) and refuses every other caller with
UNAUTHENTICATED, whatever token is presented. It is not part of the integration surface and is
not documented here. Model-backed features are reached through the domain services that use them.
The one exception is ModelService/GetModelStatus. The FACE app calls it with an ordinary
session to learn whether the inference plane answers. Any role may call it, and it carries no
user data.
FetchService/GetDispatchKey is also internal: only a runner serves it, and only to a verified mesh peer.
The same endpoint also serves the platform's shared components that FACE mounts: estate domains,
data sources, billing, profile and member administration. Those services are defined outside the
semantics.v1 package and are not covered by this reference.

docs/developer-guide/api/identity/.title: Identity, licences & landing
docs/developer-guide/api/identity/.body:
Identity, licences & landing

Sign-in, sessions, two-factor enrolment, service-account keys, licence validation and the
landing dashboard. IdentityService is where every client starts: Login is one of only two
RPCs on the whole API that take no bearer token (the other is
ActivationService/ValidateLicense). See the API overview
for how the token is carried.
Summary



Service
RPC
Kind
Purpose




IdentityService
Login
Unary
Exchange credentials, a TOTP code or an OIDC ID token for a session token


IdentityService
Logout
Unary
End every session of the calling account


IdentityService
DeleteAccount
Unary
Delete the caller's own account, after a typed confirmation


IdentityService
EnrollTotp
Unary
Generate a TOTP secret to enrol


IdentityService
ConfirmTotp
Unary
Prove the authenticator works and turn two-factor on


IdentityService
UpdateUser
Unary
Change an account's email, role or password


IdentityService
CreateInstance
Unary
Acknowledge an instance request (provisions nothing)


IdentityService
GenerateServiceAccountKey
Unary
Mint a service-account token for the caller's tenant


ActivationService

Unary
Check a signed licence key


LandingService

Unary
Live dashboard counters for the caller's instance



IdentityService
Full name semantics.v1.IdentityService.
This service handles authentication and account management for one FACE deployment. Membership
and roles of an instance are managed through the platform's shared Admin page, not through this
service: it has no RPC that adds or deletes another user. A person deletes only their own account, with DeleteAccount.
Login
rpc Login(LoginRequest) returns (LoginResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: None. This RPC is exempt from bearer authentication.
Errors: INTERNAL if the server cannot issue a session or start the MFA step, or cannot
provision the local account for a first-time SSO user. An ordinary sign-in failure is not
a gRPC error. The call succeeds with status: STATUS_FAILURE and a human-readable message.

Login is a one-step or two-step exchange, selected by method:



method
Required fields
Outcome




AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS
username (the account email), password; captcha_token when the deployment enforces reCAPTCHA
STATUS_SUCCESS with token, or STATUS_MFA_REQUIRED with mfa_session if the account has TOTP enabled


AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY
mfa_session (from the previous response), mfa_code (6-digit TOTP)
STATUS_SUCCESS with token


AUTH_METHOD_GOOGLE_OIDC
oidc_token (an OIDC ID token from the deployment's configured issuer); captcha_token when the deployment enforces reCAPTCHA
STATUS_SUCCESS with token



Behaviour worth knowing:

Session lifetime. A session token is valid for 12 hours unless it is revoked first.
Revocation (logout, or an admin changing the account) takes effect on every replica.
MFA window. The mfa_session from a STATUS_MFA_REQUIRED response expires after 5
minutes. After that the MFA step fails with "MFA session expired" and the client must sign in
again.
SSO-only deployments. A deployment can be locked to SSO. Password sign-in then fails with
"Password sign-in is disabled".
OIDC. The ID token must verify against the configured issuer and carry a verified
email. That email must also be on the deployment's allowlist. If SSO is configured and the
allowlist is empty, nobody can sign in through SSO. A first-time SSO user gets a local account
with the Reader role.
Tenant. Sessions issued by Login are bound to the deployment's default tenant. Handlers
scope all reads and writes to the tenant in the verified session, never to a tenant named in a
request.

Failure message values include Invalid credentials, Captcha verification failed,
Invalid two-factor code, SSO is not configured, SSO verification failed,
This account is not authorized for this instance and Unsupported authentication method.
Request: LoginRequest



Field
Type
Description




method
LoginRequest.AuthMethod
Which sign-in step this is.


username
string
Account email, for AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS.


password
string
Account password, for AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS.


captcha_token
string
reCAPTCHA v3 token for the login action, for AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS and AUTH_METHOD_GOOGLE_OIDC. Checked (score, action and hostname) only when the deployment configures reCAPTCHA; a missing or failing token then gets Captcha verification failed. FACE's own deployment does not enforce reCAPTCHA, so the field is not checked there. Field 5, formerly hcaptcha_token.


oidc_token
string
OIDC ID token, for AUTH_METHOD_GOOGLE_OIDC.


mfa_code
string
6-digit TOTP code, for AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY.


mfa_session
string
The mfa_session returned by the credentials step, for AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY.



Reserved: field 2 (key).
Response: LoginResponse



Field
Type
Description




status
LoginResponse.Status
Outcome of this step.


token
string
The session token (a signed JWT) on STATUS_SUCCESS. Send it as authorization: Bearer .


message
string
Human-readable outcome, safe to show to the user.


mfa_session
string
Short-lived challenge to send back with AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY, on STATUS_MFA_REQUIRED.



Logout
rpc Logout(LogoutRequest) returns (LogoutResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session.
Errors: UNAUTHENTICATED if the session carries no subject. INTERNAL if the sessions
could not be revoked. In that case nothing was revoked.

Revokes every session of the calling account, not only the one making the call. The
account is taken from the authenticated session. The token field in the request is accepted
for wire compatibility and is ignored, so one caller cannot end another account's sessions.
Request: LogoutRequest



Field
Type
Description




token
string
Ignored. The session revoked is the one authenticating the call.



Response: LogoutResponse



Field
Type
Description




success
bool
true once the sessions are revoked.



DeleteAccount
rpc DeleteAccount(DeleteAccountRequest) returns (DeleteAccountResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session, any role. Service-account tokens are refused.
Errors: UNAUTHENTICATED with no verified session. PERMISSION_DENIED for a service
account. INVALID_ARGUMENT when confirm_email is not the caller's own address.
FAILED_PRECONDITION when the caller is the last organisation admin, or the deployment's
break-glass admin, or the session carries no email. UNAVAILABLE when the accounts could not
be read. INTERNAL when a step failed. In every case the account is not reported deleted.

Deletes the caller's own account, as Google Play requires of an app that creates accounts.
The account is the one the verified session names, never a field of the request, and the
request holds no way to name another. The typed confirmation, the caller's own email address,
is compared case-insensitively with the email of the verified session.
Deleted: the account record, every session, the follow-up flows the person owns with their
runs, chat and proposals, their scenario-builder scenarios, items and terms, their pending
mailbox connects, the brief suggestions they dismissed and the spreadsheets they attached on Ask. Retained, because it is the organisation's: briefs, personas, connections,
schedules, the run history, the mailbox the organisation connected, follow-up tasks, the audit
log and the decision records. The person's account number inside retained records is replaced by
the pseudonym former-member- plus ten hex characters (a hash of the account number, the same
one the audit stream uses for an actor). The decision log is not rewritten: its stored
entries keep the opaque account number, and the pseudonym is applied where the log is served.
The access list is not edited: a later sign-in with a still-listed address creates a new, empty
account. One audit entry (ACCOUNT_DELETED: the hashed actor, the classes of data deleted and
retained, no content) is written once. The call is idempotent: every session ends first, then the
person's data goes, then the account record last, so after a failed call the person signs in again
and repeats it; a repeat after success returns already_deleted: true. Earlier encrypted versions
of the deleted records stay in storage history until it is compacted and cleaned:
storage_status is scheduled until the store's erase service has purged them and read back
nothing, and never complete before. The in-app path is described in
Delete your account.
Request: DeleteAccountRequest



Field
Type
Description




confirm_email
string
The caller's own email address, typed by the person.



Response: DeleteAccountResponse



Field
Type
Description




deleted
bool
true once the account no longer exists and its sessions are ended.


already_deleted
bool
true when the account was already gone (a repeat after success).


deleted_classes
repeated string
The classes of data deleted.


retained_classes
repeated string
The classes the organisation retains.


pseudonym
string
The code that stands for the person in retained records.


storage_status
string
scheduled while earlier encrypted versions may remain in storage history; complete only after the erase service's read-back listed nothing.


storage_scheduled_until
string
RFC 3339 time by which those versions are due to be gone: the deletion's start plus 24 hours.



EnrollTotp
rpc EnrollTotp(EnrollTotpRequest) returns (EnrollTotpResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. A caller may enrol their own account, and an org admin may enrol any
account.
Errors: PERMISSION_DENIED if the email is not the caller's own account and the caller is
not an org admin. An email that does not exist gets the same error, so the RPC cannot be used
to test whether an account exists. INTERNAL if the secret cannot be generated.

Generates a fresh TOTP secret and an otpauth:// provisioning URI (issuer FACE). Nothing is
stored until ConfirmTotp succeeds. Returns success: false with
User not found when the account disappears between the permission check and the lookup.
Request: EnrollTotpRequest



Field
Type
Description

Email of the account to enrol.

Description

ConfirmTotp
rpc ConfirmTotp(ConfirmTotpRequest) returns (ConfirmTotpResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. Same rule as EnrollTotp: the caller's own account, or any account
for an org admin.
Errors: PERMISSION_DENIED under the same conditions as EnrollTotp. INTERNAL if the
secret cannot be saved.

Checks code against secret. On a match, the server stores the secret and turns on two-factor
sign-in for the account. A wrong code returns success: false with
Invalid code — please try again.
Request: ConfirmTotpRequest



Field
Type
Description

string
Email of the account being enrolled.

string
The secret returned by EnrollTotp.

string
Current 6-digit code from the authenticator app.

Type
Description

bool
true once two-factor is enabled.

Human-readable outcome.



UpdateUser
rpc UpdateUser(UpdateUserRequest) returns (UpdateUserResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Service-account tokens are refused.
Errors: PERMISSION_DENIED for any role other than org admin. INTERNAL if the change
was saved but the account's existing sessions could not be ended.

Updates the non-empty fields among email, role and password on the account identified
by user_id. After a successful change, every existing session of that account is revoked, so
the new role or password applies at the next sign-in. Some failures return success: false
with a message instead of an error: UserID required, No such user,
That email is already in use and Update failed.
Request: UpdateUserRequest



Field
Type
Description

string
Required. The account to change.

string
New email. Empty leaves it unchanged.

string
New role. Empty leaves it unchanged.


password
string
New password. Empty leaves it unchanged.


is_active
bool
Not applied. The account model has no active or disabled state. When true, the response message says the flag was not applied. To disable an account, remove it on the Admin page.



Response: UpdateUserResponse



Field
Type
Description

bool
Whether the change was applied.


message
string
Human-readable outcome.



CreateInstance
rpc CreateInstance(CreateInstanceRequest) returns (CreateInstanceResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Service-account tokens are refused.

docs/developer-guide/api/connections/.title: Configuration, connections & runners
docs/developer-guide/api/connections/.body:
Configuration, connections & runners

This page covers how a FACE instance is told about the systems it reads from and the compute it
runs on. ConfigService stores connections: a source system, its non-secret settings and a
separately held credential bundle. The same service tests connections, explores a source's
catalogue and takes bounded samples from it. It also registers runners, reports health,
manages the integration settings (messaging numbers, billing and Google credentials, partner
links) and offers two direct Databricks helpers. RunnerEnrollmentService works the other way
round. A runner that the control plane cannot dial, for example one behind NAT, opens an
outbound stream and receives its fetch work over that stream. Authentication and status-code
conventions are on the API overview.

Note: Secrets are write-only. Credentials go in once, through CreateConnectionRequest.credentials
(or the secret-valued fields of a connector config message), and are held apart from the
connection record. No RPC on this page returns a stored secret. Connection config messages come
back with their secret fields empty, and GetIntegrationConfig reports only whether a secret is
configured.
Warning: Every connection must be secured. FACE refuses to store a connection that would send data,
or the credential that reads it, unencrypted or to a server whose certificate is not checked.
CreateConnection refuses it with INVALID_ARGUMENT. A stored connection that does not meet
the policy is still listed (with security_ok: false), but every read of it is refused with
FAILED_PRECONDITION until it is upgraded. See Connector security.

Summary



Service
RPC
Kind
Purpose




ConfigService
ListConnections
Unary
List stored connections, each with its credential state and source backing


ConfigService
CreateConnection
Unary
Store a connection together with its credentials


ConfigService

Unary
Remove a connection and its credential bundle


ConfigService
TestConnection
Unary
Live-probe a stored connection where the connector supports it


ConfigService

Unary
Read a source's catalogue (datasets, columns, keys, governance) without reading rows


ConfigService

Unary
Read a bounded sample of real rows from one dataset

ConfigService

Create a Databricks notebook job on an existing cluster and run it


ConfigService

Unary
Read integration settings (secrets reported as configured or not)

RunnerEnrollmentService
Enroll
Bidirectional streaming
A runner's outbound, long-lived stream for receiving fetch work



ConfigService
Full name semantics.v1.ConfigService.
Instance configuration: connections, runners, integration settings and resources. Every RPC needs
a bearer session. Service-account tokens are refused (PERMISSION_DENIED) on every
ConfigService RPC except ListConnections and ListRunners, which a workload needs in order
to run. Reading (ListConnections, ListRunners, ListResources, GetRunnerHealth,
GetIntegrationConfig) is open to any role. Creating, deleting, testing, exploring and sampling
a connection need the writer or admin role. Registering a runner, the Databricks helpers and
SetIntegrationConfig are admin-only. See Roles.
ListConnections
rpc ListConnections(ListConnectionsRequest) returns (ListConnectionsResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. Service-account tokens are allowed.
Errors: INTERNAL when the connection registry cannot be read.

Returns every connection stored on this instance. Each row carries two server-computed fields
that answer different questions. credential_state tells you whether this node holds a
credential bundle for the connection. source_backing tells you whether anything this deployment ships
stands behind the connection. Nothing is dialled to compute either. Use
TestConnection to find out whether a source is reachable.
Connection config messages come back with their secret fields empty. Properties whose names look
like secrets are moved to the credential store when the connection is created, so they do not
appear in properties either.
Request: ListConnectionsRequest
No fields.
Response: ListConnectionsResponse



Field
Type
Description




connections
repeated Connection
Every stored connection. credential_state and source_backing are filled on each row.


warnings
repeated string
Conditions that apply to the list as a whole. It is empty in the normal case. When the operator has not configured durable storage for connection credentials, it carries a warning that the credential bundles may not survive a restart, so rows may outlive their secrets. The text is written for a person: show it as is and do not match on its wording.



CreateConnection
rpc CreateConnection(CreateConnectionRequest) returns (CreateConnectionResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. Service-account tokens are refused.
Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT when the connection does not meet the
connector security policy. The message is
this connection cannot be saved without its security settings: followed by each problem,
one plain sentence per setting or credential to fix. Nothing is written. Every other failure
returns success: false with message: no connection in the request, an id that already
exists, an invalid id, a missing type, a malformed runner-deploy setting, or a credential
store that could not be written.

Stores a connection and its credentials in a single operation. The credential bundle is written
first. If that write fails, no connection record is created, so a success: true always
means that both were stored.

Id. If connection.id is empty, the server generates one. Either way the id comes back in
connection_id, on failure too, so a retry can reuse it instead of creating a second row. An
id must not be blank, must not have leading or trailing whitespace, must not contain a path
separator or a NUL byte, and must not start with .. An id that already exists is refused.
There is no update RPC: to change a connection, delete it and create it again.
Type. connection.type is required. The server normalises its spelling to the canonical
type name, so "Service Now", "service-now" and "servicenow" are one type. A type the catalogue
does not know is stored in normalised form rather than refused. See
Connection types and credential keys.
Credentials. There are two sources, and the server merges them into one write-only bundle:
the credentials map, and the secret-valued fields of the config message (password,
client_secret, api_key, personal_access_token, service_account_json,
security_token). When both set the same key, the map wins. A properties entry whose name
looks like a secret (for example *_token, *_secret) is moved into the bundle as well.
Values that look like secrets are refused in the Snowflake and Databricks runner-deploy
settings.
Warnings. These are the same as ListConnectionsResponse.warnings. A warning is not a
failure: the connection was created, and the caller is told what the storage does and does not
guarantee.

Request: CreateConnectionRequest



Field
Type
Description




connection
Connection
The connection to store. credential_state and source_backing are ignored on input.


credentials
map
Secret values, keyed by the type's credential key names. Stored in the credential store. Never returned.



Response: CreateConnectionResponse



Field
Type
Description




success
bool
True when the connection and its credentials were stored.


connection_id
string
The connection's id, which the server generated if the request left it empty. Set on failure as well.


message
string
The reason on failure. Empty on success.


warnings
repeated string
Storage-durability warnings, as in ListConnectionsResponse. Not a failure.



DeleteConnection
rpc DeleteConnection(DeleteConnectionRequest) returns (DeleteConnectionResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. Service-account tokens are refused.
Errors: None as gRPC status. Read outcome: DELETE_CONNECTION_OUTCOME_NOT_FOUND for
an unknown id, DELETE_CONNECTION_OUTCOME_FAILED for an empty id or a storage failure.

Removes a stored connection and its credential bundle. The credential bundle is removed first,
and the record is kept if that fails. DELETED therefore never means that the record went while
the secret stayed.
What a delete does not do:

It does not revoke anything at the source. Nothing is dialled. A key that must be revoked
has to be revoked in the system that issued it.
It does not rewrite references. Fetch definitions, rules and lineage records that name
this connection id keep the id, and it no longer resolves.
NOT_FOUND means only that this instance does not hold the id now. It does not prove that
the connection never existed elsewhere, for example on another instance or in a snapshot
restored later.

Request: DeleteConnectionRequest



Field
Type
Description




connection_id
string
The id to remove. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. An empty id is refused with outcome: FAILED and message "no connection id provided". It is never reported as not found.



Response: DeleteConnectionResponse



Field
Type
Description




success
bool
Exactly outcome == DELETE_CONNECTION_OUTCOME_DELETED. Branch on outcome.


outcome
DeleteConnectionOutcome
Which of the three results happened.


connection_id
string
The id that was asked about, echoed back on every path. It is empty when the request id was empty.


message
string
Human-readable detail. On FAILED it carries the underlying error. Do not branch on it.


warnings
repeated string
Storage-durability warnings, as in ListConnectionsResponse. On an instance without durable storage, a delete may not survive a restart.



TestConnection
rpc TestConnection(TestConnectionRequest) returns (TestConnectionResponse);


Kind: Unary.
Auth: Bearer session. Service-account tokens are refused.
Errors: None as gRPC status. Returns success: false with message when the connection
cannot be read, does not exist ("Connection not found"), has a type with no registered
connector, does not meet the connector security policy (nothing is
dialled, and message names each problem), or fails its probe.

Looks up the stored connection and its credentials and asks the connector to probe the source.
With draft set instead of connection_id, it tests a connection that has not been stored yet,
exactly as a stored one would be tested, and then forgets it.
Read success and live_check_performed together:



success
live_check_performed
Meaning




true
true
The source answered and accepted the credentials ("Connectivity verified").


true
false
The connector for this type has no live probe. The configuration is stored and nothing was verified. This is not a failure.


false
true
The probe ran and failed. message carries the connector's error.


false
false
No probe was attempted: the connection could not be resolved (see message).



Even a true/true result only establishes that the endpoint is reachable and that the credential
was accepted. It does not establish that records exist, that a sensor is publishing, or that the
credential has scope for any other resource.

Field
Type
Description

string
The stored connection to test. Credentials are read from the credential store. Empty when draft is set.


draft
Connection
A connection that has not been stored, tested and then forgotten: nothing is written and no credential bundle is kept. Read only when connection_id is empty. A draft bound to a runner other than the managed one is refused without dialling.


draft_credentials
map
The draft's credentials, as on CreateConnectionRequest.credentials. Never stored.

Description

See the table above.

Human-readable result or error. Do not branch on it.


live_check_performed
